top_reviews.title: Comfortable & great for "weird", problem feet
top_reviews.text: I am lucky if I can find a pair of shoes every year to fit me.  Due to a medical issue, my left foot swells and it's nearly impossible to find a shoe to fit, especially when my right foot swells only slightly.  I'm essentially 2 different sizes.  If I happen to find an adjustable shoe that fits & is somewhat comfortable, I buy one in every color I can find and have been known to wear them for 10 years in some cases.  Having been frustrated for the last 2 years looking for some kind of sandal, I finally bought these shoes I'd always considered "old lady" shoes.  When they arrived I was pleasantly surprised to find they aren't really bad looking and they actually FIT and are super-comfortable! They adjust in muliple areas with a velcro strap, meaning I can tighten them to the max for my "normal" foot & change the other foot's fit throughout the day based on how it changes.  Several other brands I've tried because they looked adjustable, turned out not to be so when I got them.  I've wasted a lot of money on shoes that don't fit lately, I'm super happy that these do.  Because they are on sale I'm back for another pair in black.  I'm just sorry it took me until September to find good open-toe shoes that fit this summer!  They are going with me on a trip to Las Vegas later this year & hopefully I can walk comfortably in them for an extended period.

top_reviews.title: Propet means comfort
top_reviews.text:
Propet shoes are for anyone who has difficulty being comfortable while working long 12-14-16 hours days. My line is - Never fear, PROPET is here!

These are great and work well for a stylish look and serve as a comfortable practical shoe for my size 11 stompers. Because of a serious injury when I shattered my foot in two places (while kicking a football at 19 years old), my gait was off, I walked slightly imbalanced until I had my final final surgery. I dealt with the pain and discomfort from so many sneakers and shoes because I couldn't find a brand that was comfortable and fit well. Because of being in survival mode and working multiple jobs including teaching and food service (waitressing) both of which require long shifts of walking, standing, and hustling, I kept thinking there has to be a good shoe brand out there that will be okay for handling the lingering long work days. This is it.

I've used Propet for years as recommended by a shoes salesperson ten years ago. Propet is worth the cost, even the higher end $125+ pairs of shoes are worth it! Comfortable and no foot pain. When I wear these, I'm comfortable and always get compliments about how nice, stylish, cute these are. Excellent product.

top_reviews.text: These shoes feel just like the other Propet shoes I bought, which is  wonderful.  Everything about this shoe is comfortable even the strap! Everything is adjustable on the shoe.  The  straps  aren’t  digging into my ankle nor is the flesh rubbing on the  top box area of the shoe nothing is irritating me there’s also  a slight toe grip built into the bottom of the shoe.  These shoes fit like a glove and you really don’t feel like you have a shoe on that’s what I call comfortable  since most of the time I am barefoot.

top_reviews.title: Comfortable all day with plantar fasciitis
top_reviews.text: I tried to buy these locally and they were not able to get them back in stock.  I needed a pair of sandals with a back for work and I liked the removable foot bed and look of these.  I have not needed to insert my own orthotics, however, and throughout a typical day of teaching I have had zero issues with these, even from the first day wearing them. Since I've worn these in place of my Birkenstocks, my plantar Fasciitis is doing better - not sure if it is on part because of these shoes, but they certainly do not exacerbate the condition like traditional flats would. I do wish they came in a narrow width, as I have a narrow foot, and I've got the straps as tight as the velcro will allow.  For the price I am very pleased with these shoes.

My Ecco sandals were my back up to a Europe trip and when my tennis shoes failed halfway through, I turned to them and forever I shed I had used them at the start of my trip for their comfort and durability.  These sandals are a dream, I absolutely love them.  There is only one point I want to make about the shoes to be sure that others are aware; the heel strap and ankle strap is adjustable but the top of foot strap is not adjustable.  I have a narrower foot so the top foot strap is big for my foot although having the heel and ankle strap adjustable makes it a fairly well-suited fit overall.  I am looking to buy this sandal in other colors.

top_reviews.title: That tongue...ouch
top_reviews.text:
I love the look, light weight, breath-ability and cost of this shoe. It's almost perfect, except....
The base of the tongue, where it stitches to the rest of the shoe, is like having a rock pressed against the top of your foot. It seems they could have padded this area or moved the first shoelace a little further away so this area is pressing down so much. To avoid this, I just loosen the lace considerably for the first few eyelets from the base. This relieves a lot of the pressure to make them wearable, but I wouldn't work out or run in the shoe as this makes them too loose on the feet.

top_reviews.text: I wear 4E asics, have for years.  Bought these in "X-WIDE."  Thought I had bought the wrong shoe when trying them on, but realized that I had forgotten to remove the insoles before adding custom inserts.  Still fits small, and can't thread the laces past the tongue loop cross, but that's just because of my fat feet.  Definitely not a shoe I'd ever want to competitively run in, but it feels well made.

top_reviews.title: Good running shoe except for the heel counter
top_reviews.text: I don't jog often, but when I do, I use these New Balance Men's Ventr V1 running shoes. Even though I'm a slightly bigger guy (close to 6'1" and around 195 pounds), these generally feel comfortable for jogging. They're lightweight and the cushioning is good. Also, although jogging isn't my favorite thing to do, these shoes make it a decent experience. The size was a little larger than I expected, but not uncomfortably so. The only reason I didn't rate these shoes 5 stars is because of the heel counter. Part of it could just be me, but the heel counter would dig into my Achilles tendon sometimes and irritate it pretty badly. I took a pair of scissors and cut down the heel counter so it's not so pronounced. It's not pretty, but hopefully that fixes the issue. If you have Achilles tendon issues, this might not be the shoe for you. Otherwise, although I don't plan to buy these again, I think these are solid running shoes.

top_reviews.title: Allen Edmonds all the way.
top_reviews.text:
Great shoes! This is my first pair of leather-soled dress shoes... definitely a lot less comfortable than rubber-soled shoes, particularly if you are planning on standing for a long period of time. Also a bit less comfortable for walking, mostly because leather soles do not really have traction. This is also part of the reason why I bought them, because they're better for dancing.

One other problem I've had with both these and the Kennett (essentially a rubber-soled version of the Delray with slightly different vamp/toe) is the fact that while most of the shoe fits well, the heel feels a bit loose. I'm not sure if I should downgrade to a 10.5, as some 11's in AE do feel large on me (and I usually wear a 10.5), but it's not a big enough problem to lessen my appreciation of the shoe. Otherwise the fit is fine...

Overall: These are great shoes, and I don't have a lot to complain about. They are relatively comfortable, attractive, and are, I expect, going to last me quite some time. Impeccable styling! I also take pride in supporting quality American manufacturing. If you have any doubt about the price tag, Amazon and-- more so- eBay offer some great deals on some AE shoes, but it's worth every penny, especially over the junk sold these days by formerly reputable companies like Florsheim or J&M.

top_reviews.title: Great comfortable Shoe for Elderly
top_reviews.text: My 98 year old mother wears this shoe and it is the most comfortable we have been able to find her.  She hasn't had any traction problems with it.  It's easily adjustable and she took her normal size 9M.  She has these now in both black leather and tan nubuck.  She has problems with the edge of her big toe, so having this open toed shoe solves that for us.  We put a regular shoe or boot on her when she travels to day care, but send these along for her to change into once she gets inside.  As soon as it warms up a little more, she can wear them round the clock.  One of the best features about them is the heel.  It has a closed heel just like a shoe, which offers more protection for her foot - and can't slip off.like a strap might.  I wish they came in more colors.  The foot liner is very comfortable and cushioned also.  It has two adjustable straps for proper fitting and if your feet swell as the day goes on, can be easily adjusted with the velcro straps..  Propet makes great shoes & sandals, I just wish their orthopedic shoes & sneakers didn't have such slippery hard plastic like soles.  Fortunately, these sandals aren't as bad as those and she gets decent traction in them.  Hope this helps.

I usually measure them against other Pedic Walkers I have.  The straps are honestly getting shorter.  Darn!  I love these shoes.  They fit beautifully everywhere else and support very well.  I will keep ordering them, and buying extenders.  I wish they wouldn't skimp.

top_reviews.title: Somewhat stiffer and more supportive than pureboost go
top_reviews.text:
The Adidas Boost material was a game changer for my running. I guess it's just perfect for my weight and running style. I'm a man, size 9.5-10, but I swear by the fit of 11.5 womens. as well. The Pureboost Go and Ultraboost are my sweet spot. I picked these Astrarun shoes up as a trial, for a good deal.

Running shoes are highly dependent on a person's foot, gait, strike pattern, etc. I don't need to tell you that. Nonetheless here's my first impressions.

They're definitely stiffer, through the midsole and toes, but boosty and cushy at the heel (where I need it). I can't tell if I like it or not. Probably need to give it 20 miles to break in.

This is not a sock style shoe. It has a traditional tongue without a high-up loop to keep the tongue in place, but id didn't move around too much. I noticed a little rubbing on the inside of the ankle when the highest laces were added. Took those out, but the opening feels a bit too large for my foot (perhaps this is why as a man, I tend to like the ladies shoes?). The top is slippery and there is a bit of a feeling of movement, but it's arrested by the stiffer upper (non-sock).

top_reviews.title: Super Cute, moderately comfortable, and incredibly loud
top_reviews.text: First of all, these shoes are super cute. No qualms about the appearance other than perhaps the obviously fake wood appearance of the outsoles - but I'm going to assume they that's an intentional part of the style. Comfort wise, the in sole is soft and there is a subtle but functional arch support. The front of the leather upper rubbed on my big toes after walking around for a little over an hour the first wear, but I assume they will break in. The biggest detractor for me is the material of the outsole. They are HARD plastic with no rubberized tread at all on the base of the foot. This makes the shoes somewhat precarious on hardwood and I occasionally skidded on metal carpet strips and the like. Also, these were VERY noisy on hard floors. While this is probably to be expected of mules, the noise was definitely a hard plastic versus a wooden shoe sound and a few customers in the department store made passing glances as I clunked by. All that said, I made it through an 8 hour work day (moderate walking around)  with only minimal discomfort during the first wear.

top_reviews.title: Longtime fan of Salomon
top_reviews.text:
I've been a fan of Salomon's shoes for a long time. As a former Special Operations Soldier, I needed shoes that could stand up to harsh field conditions while still being comfortable. I used to wear an earlier model of these shoes before switching to the Speedcross, and while I liked the Speedcross, I've come back to the Pro 3D because these shoes are more well-rounded for a wider variety of terrain and conditions. They also have a wider toe box that accommodates my need for a little more space due to two separate foot surgeries.

I am particularly fond of the GTX (Goretex) lining because it allows for a low level of waterproofing without causing my feet to overheat (read: sweat and stink), and it helps to keep the sand from permeating the shoe. When paired with Salomon trail gaiters, I rarely have any debris or sand in my shoes after long hikes, trail runs, or trailjoring with my dog.

Although I am a female, I tend to prefer the darker, more subdued colors of the men's line of shoes to the bright neon colors available in the women's line.

top_reviews.title: Awesome grip!
top_reviews.text:
Finally got to take these out today for a 5 mile run. I bought them for exactly what today’s conditions threw at me: slushy streets, icy side walks, crunchy snow covered trails, and wintry mix stuff falling from the sky.

My feet stayed dried and locked in. The laces stayed tight, and I could adjust them on the fly with gloves on. The soles gripped whatever it could, and mitigated whatever slippage occurred whenever it could not.

I bought these sneakers because I have a boot by salomon with the same sole, and I liked how well they performed.

Great shoe!

top_reviews.title: Extremely disappointed
top_reviews.text:
Extremely frustrated. Until now the Salomon Goretex XA Pro shoes have been my favorite and preferred shoe for an every day activewear. Thus when my 2rd consecutive pair wore out I ordered another pair of the same XA Pro shoe, in the same exact size, eagerly looking forward to their arrival just in time to break them in a week prior to my vacation (now). I ordered the same USA men's size 11.5 I have had in my two previous extremely comfortable, right-out-of-the-box XA Pro shoes. Unfortunately it is absolutely evident these shoes were mistagged somewhere in the pipeline as they are clearly a half size smaller in the toe box from both my previous 11.5 XA Pros! I initially chalked up the tight fit in the toe box to requiring some standard breaking in time, however after just one day's wear I'm extremely frustrated with my first Amazon shoe purchase ever. These are not the right size shoe for that which they are tagged as my bigger left foot big toe is banging against the hard rubber of the toe causing cramping (& I fear potentially hammertoe could develop if I continue wearing them). Is this a Salomon error, an Amazon thing, a day of the week manufacturing error?

This was a big $ purchase for me as well as a self birthday present that I've looked forward to buying for many months. Given that I was buying the same shoe model in the same size I didn't think I needed to pay extra for free returns. Though at this point I have a pair of nice looking door stops (thanks Salomon).

Having bought both previous pair of Salomon shoes direct from REI w/ zero issues I know not what recourse I have to remedy this situation aside from never buying another shoe from Amazon & cancelling my Prime account (for which the convenience of prime ordering was what convinced me to buy these shoes from Amazon in the first place) the minute I return home from my vacation.

Without some way to remedy this situation I will definitely think twice before I ever buy any shoe via Amazon.

Other than the inaccurate fit of this shoe the shoe looks nice and seems functional, although I must say if the shoe is inaccurately sized then I am left to wonder what else might be less than upfront about this shoe.

Having not ever returned anything to Amazon - I will update this review once I figure if possible to return these shoes and receive the correct fit. All new to me.

top_reviews.title: I love these shoes
top_reviews.text:
I love these shoes! I had been searching for the perfect winter/all season shoe for a long time. The most important feature to me in any footwear, cheap or expensive, is comfort. I still have to use the Superfeet insoles, but there aren’t any shoes where that isn’t the case. 2nd being appearance. These shoes have both! I received a comment on these shoes each day at work for the entire first week ! That and a lot of looks! I researched online for the best materials used in footwear. The quick “sensifit” lacing system is a huge plus to me. Also the Gore-Tex allows me to slip these on and run around in any weather condition. I live in the Pacific Northwest and it is wet a majority of the time.

This is my first pair of Salomon shoes, but it won’t be my last.

top_reviews.title: Best shoes I've ever had
top_reviews.text:
Ahhhh how much can I praise these shoes! I found these shoes around five years back and have bought a new pair every year since. I wear them every day and run them into the ground before getting my new ones. I have always had issues with my feet and most shoes I wear need Smartfeet insoles, not these however, I can cinch them up every day and not worry about my feet being in major pain at the end of the day.

The soles are high quality that last for a long time and give you plenty of grip on all surfaces. The insoles are fantastic too, give good support and stand up to everyday use no problem. The signature feature of all Salomon shoes are also there amazing laces, which aren't actually laces but an easy pull to tighten system that takes less than a second to tighten. Very quick and easy.

I use them for everyday use even though they are trail runners, I can use them for anything at anytime though and highly recommend them to everyone I meet.

top_reviews.title: Excellent tactical-looking footwear, mediocre running shoe
top_reviews.text: More of a low hiker than a running shoe. It is too heavy for good running but provides excellent protection for trails and the like. I found the bottom to be hard and mediocre in cushioning comfort. The speed-laces are nice but I hope they will last with the constant abrasion from tightening and loosening. I presently use them as daily footwear with tactical cargo pants and find them better looking than tactical boots.

top_reviews.title: Impossible to Find - 10-Year XA Pro 3D GTX Veteran
top_reviews.text: So glad I could find these. The XA 3D PRO V8 GTX are terrible. Have worn this model since 2010, this is my favorite of all. More durable and aggressive sole makes it for me. Also, the black/black color makes it attractive with everything. At first I thought they were counterfeit, because the Goretex logo is different than the 2019 production run - but if you check Salomon's website, their newer model hiking boots have this same logo (i.e. the diamond + Goretex instead of a line under Goretex). I also checked the sole cusions, looking for shoddy construction and they're definitely ortholites. The only interesting thing to note is that the actual sole specified "08042022" and my older ones from 2019 note "06052019" - I wonder if Salomon is producing these strictly for Amazon now (or at least in the UK)? I can't find them anywhere else.

top_reviews.title: My "go to" shoe for winter walking.
top_reviews.text:
This is my 3rd pair of these shoes, over the past 8 or 10 years. It may be the model names have changed a bit, but this Salomon trail runner is a very comfortable walking and work (casual office) shoe for the wet pacific north coast where I live. I do replace the Salomon orthotic insert with a green Superfeet insert, because of my plantar fasciitis. The shoes are rugged, good looking, and comfortable. After about 3 winters of daily wear, the goretex "bootie" develops small holes, and they lose their waterproofness. If you live where it's hot and dry, these may not be your best option.
These are called a trail runner, and some people probably use them for that. For me, they don't have enough cushion for running, and they're too stiff.

top_reviews.title: Cheap
top_reviews.text:
Unfortunately in this case you get what you pay for.

This shoe is great off the shelf. Five stars for looks, comfort, and heel height. It fit perfectly right away and I was impressed. I have moderate bunions on both my feet and usually I have to do some procedure where I stretch them at the big toe joint. No need with this shoe. The lining eliminates any rubbing issues I normally have with other heels. The styling is slim not clunky, and walking in them is very easy.

On to the bad. This shoe is plastic. Not only plastic, but thin plastic. I have worn this heel to work at my office job on only 4 separate occasions. Already there is a long scratch across the toe, scuffs at the back, scratches in the middle near the arch, and a dent with scratch on the heel. I have these in plain black. The outer material is very thin and covers a base layer of white plastic, the meat of the material. Every scratch shows white through in a very obvious way. I have touched them up with a sharpie 3 times today, two spots you can see in my photos. The heel is wrapped in the same material as the upper, meaning any time you walk on gravel, step in a sidewalk crack, or drive a car, you run the risk of tearing up the heel.

If you plan to wear these for a special occasion, great. If you plan to actually wear them in regular life then don't expect much. I would not expect more than a season out of these shoes, and per my mileage only a handful of wears. This explains why other reviewers have a pair in every color - less wears per pair. I have asked myself how many cheap shoes do I need to toss prematurely to realize that it's worth it to get a nicer pair of shoes that will last me two years or more with proper care and maintenance. I intend to purchase a pair of cole haan pumps to replace these. On sale just under $100 vs three pairs of cheap shoes, in the end, is cheap really the better deal? I would say no.

top_reviews.text:
After years trying (unsuccessfully) to find footwear for my Diabetic feet, I did a search for slippers for people with Diabetes. These slippers popped up right away. I was impressed with the description/pictures of them. They are totally adjustable across the top half of your foot, due to a wide section of velcro, that you can totally adjust to fit your feet. I immediately ordered 2 pair, in pink and in blue. A month or two later, I purchased a 3rd pair in, grey. They are the most comfortable slippers I have ever had, I have absolutely NO pain or discomfort when wearing them! I love them, and recommend them to anyone with foot/toe issues. Also, I put these slippers in the washer and dryer when they get soiled from every day wear, and they come out of the dryer, looking brand new!

If you have painful or mishapen feet/toes, I recommend you buy a pair of these slippers. You will love them! They are so comfortable, and they even come in pretty colors!

top_reviews.title: My absolute favorite slipper of all time!
top_reviews.text:
I love these slippers and am so glad that Daniel Green brought them back after a few years' hiatus. I wear size 11N shoes and use orthotics, so finding a slipper that works with my long narrow feet and the orthotics is a real treat. I have gone through probably 15 pairs of these slippers over the past many years! In winter, I wear them with socks to keep my feet warm. The velcro closing allows me to do that, while at the same time allowing me to wear the slippers with no socks in the other seasons.
The hard sole is great; I even wear these to the mailbox at the end of the driveway and have been known to rake leaves with them on.
I just can't say enough about them. Thank you, Daniel Green for making them again, and thank you, amazon.com, for stocking them in my size!

top_reviews.title: Classic appearance and fits comfortably
top_reviews.text:
I have been wearing these for a few weeks now and feel ready to write a review. I am a mom of 2 (1 an infant) in the quest for simple black canvas shoes that I can slip on in a few seconds and be out the door for school/store runs or other errands. I also wanted a vegan shoe that would last a couple of years with regular wear. I don't have an extensive shoe wardrobe and finding quality shoes that last and are comfortable is very difficult.

I am so glad that this is a vegan shoe company. The shoe has a nice, solid look (not scuffy or trendy, more classic) and seems to be made of a robust material. The sole is thick without being heavy. It took a few days to settle in (I did have some pain for the first week, but that's diminishing now), but now I wear it to the school and store. When I return to work, I will wear it there as well.

I bought an 8.5, which is my usual size, but it is a more snug fit with socks. Without socks it is perfect. If you need to wear thick socks I would go up 1/2 size.

As for durability that remains to be seen and I will update later. I will wear it more often than the typical customer since I don't want or have very many shoes. I intend for this to be my go to shoe in Northern California (maybe except the two-three winter months).

top_reviews.title: Versatile trail running shoe
top_reviews.text:
This is my third pair of ASICS Gel-Fujitrabuco trail running shoes. I was turned on to them several years ago through a fitting at a running shoe store and they are still my favorite running shoe for mixed road and trail runs. I do a variety of road races, triathlons, trail runs, and OCR events, and these shoes are just what I needed for all around training and racing. Since I know I like them, I will probably just keep buying them!

I really like the updated colors for the Gel-Fujitrabuco 6. The black and navy blue go well with just about any workout clothes and the pop of turquoise blue makes me happy when I look at my feet.

The tread on these shoes is great for slippery and rocky terrain. I feel confident going quickly down steep descents knowing these shoes will bite down as needed. The soles are thick enough to keep my feet happy and protected without feeling heavy or weighed down. My only complaint is that the heel padding does tend to break down eventually, but only after putting a LOT of miles on these shoes.

top_reviews.text:
***UPDATED***
So, these shoes are surprisingly comfortable once they break in, and they get a compliment EVERY SINGLE TIME I wear them. The first day with these things on IS a little on the brutal side, but after that, you can actually forget they are even on, they break in so nicely. I still don't exactly have HIGH hopes about the durability of these things, but they have grown on me enough that I have a pair in every color now.....I guess you DO get a second chance to make a first impression.

So, I'm nearing the end of my first full day with these shoes, and I gotta say; I don't know what all the hype is about. Granted, it's only been a day, but I'm pretty underwhelmed with these things, and am kinda gobsmacked at the amount of glowing reviews. FIRST off, just upon pulling these things out of the box, I noticed that they are STIFF. Like, are they entirely made of plastic? They are SUPER RIGID. This is why so many of the reviews mention "creases." Of course they are creasing, they are like cardboard. This has led to the second problem, and another contradiction to what I was reading in the reviews. The toe box is NOT "wide," as many reviews stated. The toe box is in fact narrow (look at the damn pictures!) and because the shoe is so rigid, it has been KILLING my toe today. I'm positive that I will have some form of callous or blister on the top of my middle toe. I know that this shoe was cheap, but I was REALLY, REALLY expecting something a LOT softer. This isn't a casual business shoe so much as it's a dress shoe that LOOKS like a casual business shoe. The shoe is not a soft fabric shaped like a dress shoe; thus giving a casual feel with that dressy look, it is a thin veneer of fabric, stretched over a hard shell of a dress shoe. The only saving grace is that they DO, LOOK nice. They LOOK like they would be casual and comfortable, but they are not. I was wearing the Ralph Lauren Vaughn style shoe, almost exclusively, and those are light years ahead of these for about twice the cost. Even the Calvin Klein Kadon/Kellen style is more comfortable than these. I had planned on getting these in multiple colors, but it's back to the drawing board, as I'm pretty unimpressed with these.

top_reviews.text:
It’s a good looking shoe but I wore it while walking around the city and found my feet to be super fatigued. They don’t have a lot of cushion and arch support isn’t great. I’d recommend an insert.

Edit: customer services reached out today and offered to provide a replacement pair of shoes/boot in a different style and shape. I offered two choices of shoe or boot. top_reviews.title: Nice shoes at a great price!
top_reviews.text: This is a great product for its price range. I will definitely recommend this pair as a great office-wear or even for a casual outing. However, if you are going to walk a bunch then avoid them. I put them on for an entire day and walked for about 4 and a half miles and it wasn't comfortable but obviously this is not a runner shoe!

top_reviews.title: Large and narrow
top_reviews.text:
Ordered the blue 1/2 size down (9) than I normally wear (9.5) and they are way to big. More like a size 10.5
Going to reorder a size 8.5 and hope that works. I would suggest ordering a whole size down from what you normally wear. They are also extremely narrow so I would pass altogether if you have a wide foot.

UPDATE: After reordering a size 8.5, the sizing is still completely off as seen in the pics compared with my old 9.5 tennis shoes. Quality is substandard at best with areas not properly glued straight out of the box so as other reviewers have said, these won’t last long at all and are so long and narrow they look ridiculous. What really gets me the most is they can’t even keep their own sizing compatible from shoe to shoe. In the last pics are another pair of “Bruno Marc’s” that I also had to reorder due to sizing and when compared, there is a good 1.5 size difference in the exact same size! Both 8.5 but the boot is more like a 10.5 and the oxfords closer to a 10/9.75. So getting a proper size of “Bruno Marc” shoes is like throwing darts blindfolded. $20 shoes at best. Returning of course.

top_reviews.title: Great styling, true to size, very sturdy construction, and comfort in a very well priced shoe
top_reviews.text: Finally, a keeper! Size is right on. I've lost track of how many pairs of shoes I've bought on Amazon and returned this year- most because they are not the stated size. The casual rugged wing-tip styling is fantastic. Time will tell for long term durability and comfort, but the construction and attention to detail seem to be surprisingly good in this price range. These seem very well made of some really stout leather, which is fully stitched and lined. Everything is nicely finished with no uneven cuts or loose stitching. The weakest link is probably the sole, but it is a material which makes them very quite light despite the stout construction of the uppers. It also makes them very comfortable to walk on. It is the typical EVA type foam alternative to heavy rubber or stiff traction-less leather soles. I've had several pairs of Ecco and Bostonian shoes with the same sole material and it has held up fine. As for the stout leather, it may take a bit to break in- primarily around the top edges where the stiff leather is, well ,a bit stiff. I loosened some of the stiffness of the edges by flexing and rolling the edges outward and down where they felt like they might cause a little irritation below my ankle bones. I used the handle of a wooden spoon to roll the seams near the back of the ankle outward a little (flexed it outward several times to loosen it up a little). This seemed to work fine, as I had no irritation after the first day of wear. Oh yeah, and they're very comfortable!

top_reviews.title: I'm surprised to be honest....
top_reviews.text:
I was skeptical. These shoes are cheap in price, and often on Amazon you really do get what you pay for, but I really like this "Keds" style, and given that these are cheaper than the shoe they are styled after, I figured i'd give these a go first. I bought one pair. I read the size reviews and opted to go a half size up (9 instead of 8.5). When they arrived they fit well (I go sockless but I could probably where a thin sock and still be pretty comfortable). I live in a city and do a lot of walking all day...a few weeks in the shoes are still like new honestly.
They are lightweight, very flat, no arch support....but I have very flat feet so i'm used to this, thus the discomfort that some users have stated after long term use, I do not suffer from. I can wear them all day and never feel uncomfortable. They breath pretty well too, something I was worried about due to not wearing socks. I bought two more pairs in different colours about a week ago because I was so pleased with my first pair. When they arrived they were packaged a bit differently however. They had those plastic shoe expanders which morphed the mouth of the shoes a bit wider than I would like. I was worried about blisters as a result but it wasn't as bad as it looked once putting them on and walking around, so it hasn't been an issue.

All in all, this is a good summer shoe. Being that they are cheap and lightweight, I wouldn't be surprised if by the end of the summer they are pretty much done for, but again, because they are cheap, I have got 3 pairs so their life might be a little longer than if I was wearing the same pair day in and day out. So far they've held up really well though, and I can't picture them falling apart for quite awhile. It's worth the purchase in my book. Grab a few pairs.

top_reviews.title: Lightweight, Prevent Slipping
top_reviews.text:
I took a tumble down the our hardwood stairs two weeks ago, wearing socks. Instead of the usual fall (because of course, this isn't my first), where I just slide down a few steps and end up none the worse for wear, I hit one stair with my spine, and another with the base of my skull. Injuries aside, I'm now a big fan of footwear with rubber dots, the very socks I used to make fun of before. That's karma for you.

These little shoes are excellent. I'm a 5.5 US shoe, so I ordered size 5-6. They're wide, and fit as comfortably for me as a slipper, but the rubber dots and lines, as well as the overall rubber sole, give a good grip for any yoga I might do with shoes on, as well as going up stairs. And thanks to the design, they stay on without trouble.

I generally do yoga barefoot, and spend the day around the house in socks, but now I have my shoes next to me for when I go up and down stairs - no more household accidents for me. These shoes are lightweight, an easy fit, comfortable, great for yoga, and make me feel safer on hardwood floors.

top_reviews.title: Comfortable, Stylish, Durable but Expensive. Worth it?
top_reviews.text:
So let's get right to the crux of this flip flop. The price.
Is it worth it?
That's really up to you, the specifics of your body & what you want out of them.

FYI, this is a 1 year review & I wear these EVERY day for at least several hours.
Sometimes all day but not all day every day.
*apologies for how dirty they are in the photos*

The Good:
• Very comfortable to me & my size 12/13 wide feet
• 100% leather touches your skin, it feels great... to me
• Supportive enough but not overly so. This is very important to me as I wear flip-flops to allow my feet to move freely as compared to boots or shoes
• Very Durable for what I use & wanted them for. Which is mostly as: house shoes, walking around town, shopping, beaches, & light trails - very light; minimal elevation changes & well kept. At 1 year of everyday use you can see that there is very little wear on the leather or the treads
• Super Stylish - love the way these look! I mean just look at the details in the leather, the stitching, even the treads. Just beautiful

The Bad:
• Expensive!!! The most expensive flip-flops I own BY FAR.
That said, I certainly have/ have had sandals that are right up there & they haven't lasted & weren't nearly as comfy
• Inconsistent / Quality Control Issues:
▪︎This is my 2nd set of these. To be fair, maybe they just run big as my nominal size is 12.5 wide so I normally go for 13s when companies don't offer 12.5s but the 13s of these were HUGE. Didn't fit at all. Again, this may not be a fault of the company or the flip-flop
▪︎ Inconsistency between each flip-flop. As you can see in the pictures. My left flip-flop has much more pronounced/deeper etching in the leather, which I prefer for visual & functional (more on that later) reasons
• NOT for water use - going back to those etchings in the leather. The right flip-flop has no grip at all on your foot while it's wet. Very slippery. Even the deeper etched left flip-flop has very poor foot traction when wet. Also, I'd strongly warn against using these for water anyway because you risk damaging the leather unless you're very careful about not soaking them too long, drying them, & then treating the leather. Actually the only damage/ wear these have is from water damage. The right flip-flop's leather has cracked right behind the ball of my foot but it's still very serviceable.

Conclusion:
These are a very well made, beautiful, comfortable & durable flip-flop depending on your intended use for them.

These are best suited for: walking around your house, on well maintained terrain, & for strolling the sands on the beaches but you should kick them off before getting to the waterline.

These things are EXPENSIVE & they aren't made for hard work or tough terrain so keep that in mind.

I'll try to update if anything changes or at the 2yr mark. Whichever happens first.

Hope this helps someone decide.
Take care everyone. 🙂

top_reviews.title: Buyer beware of sizing
top_reviews.text: I love Reef sandals. I have been wearing them for nearly 20 years. I have been buying Reef Ginger sandals for over a decade. My old pair is, well, old, so I needed a replacement. I have been a size 9 for my entire adult life, never bigger and never smaller, so shoe shopping is usually very easy for me. Similar to prior reviews, the pair that arrived looks the same as my old sandals, but was substantially smaller in both length (26cm vs 28cm) and width. I will sadly be returning them. Future buyers, beware. I would not recommend buying this product unless they update the website to include the full dimensions of the sandal and/or provide some other side-by-side comparison to their prior products.

top_reviews.title: I LOVED THEM. They were so comfortable I would wear ...
top_reviews.text:
I have been through three pairs of these flip flops in the past ten years. I LOVED THEM. They were so comfortable I would wear them all the time (and I walk a lot), and they are simple so I could wear them with most outfits. HOWEVER, I recently ordered a new pair on Amazon because my old ones are about to break, and they are totally different. The material is different - much stiffer and less flexible with a more pronounced arch - and worse yet the sizing is different. I have always worn size 9, but I ordered the exact same size and they are too small. This is not about my feet as of course my old ones still fit (and my feet haven't changed size). See the pictures for the difference (not great photo quality and my old ones look kinda gross I know hah)
I was hoping they may just have been a poor product from Amazon but I checked the product on the Reef website and saw that the photos do match this exact new design (at least back part of the shoe is identical). I also saw that other people have complained on the Reef website reviews about this change as well.
I'm only bothering to write this in the hopes that Reef sees and goes back to their original design. Please return to the old style as I really loved them and haven't found any other flip flops comparable in comfort (and these new ones definitely don't cut it). I am so disappointed.

top_reviews.title: these are not the Reef sandals we've known and loved for years
top_reviews.text: Disappointing fit--like many other reviewers posted, these are not the Reef sandals we've known and loved for years. I normally wear a 7.5 so I ordered a sz 8. My toes barely fit width wise (pinky toe is half off the edge) the length is just ok--could be a bit longer. Straps are tighter on the instep than is comfortable. top_reviews.title: Love
top_reviews.text:
I have been in pair after pair of the black Reef Ginger flip flops for well over a decade now. When I first saw their skinny, comfy little strap and the cushiony, arch-supported footbed with durable rubber bottoms I was in love. I even love the little rubber Reef logo tag along the strap. They make me feel like a cool surfer chick even though I've never seen a surfboard in person. I live in the South and I pretty much wear mine from late spring through summer and into fall when I start feeling self-conscious beginning of October and have to switch over to proper shoes. I can get by with one pair every couple years, but they really start to look rough around the middle of that second summer. They casual up a flowy maxi dress and go perfectly with jean shorts or cropped jeans...and pretty much anything else.

These seem to have been slightly altered from the models I've had in the past. Little difference in the fabric strap pattern and the pattern on the bottom rubber piece. No biggie.

They come in whole sizes only. I'm almost always a 7.5 in shoes so I wear the seven and they fit to my foot great. My mom is an 8.5 and wears the size 8 Reefs and they look great. I don't think your heel or toes will fall off if you get the half size down. But I guess that is personal preference if you like to go up and get a roomier pair, say if maybe you have really long toes or wide feet. When I first slip a new pair on the straps are a little snug but they stretch to fit perfectly after one wearing.

Just about as lady-like as a pair of flip flops can get.

top_reviews.title: A bit tough to break in but very well made and perfect for running or cross-training
top_reviews.text: These shoes are designed for running but I think they will work very well for cross-training also. They are very well engineered with thick rubber sole treads, even distribution of support around the foot, a reinforced rubber toe below the breathable mesh fabric, good stitching around the laces, and an external rubber heel counter below the molded sock liner. The position of the heel counter falls about mid heel so during the break-in period, the edge rubs on the mid heel which can cause blisters. However, by loosening the laces a bit during the break-in use, it took the pressure off the heel just enough to be comfortable. I definitely recommend these for anyone looking for a well-engineered running/training shoe.

top_reviews.title: Great traction. Drained beautifully. And wide sizes!
top_reviews.text:
Searched all over to find a good trail shoe for my relatively wide (size 2e) feet to use in my first Spartan rave. Visited a couple of running stores, REI, and bought 5 pairs here in Amazon. These were the only ones that fit, going up just half a size and getting the 2e wide size.

The shoes were fantastic in the mud and on slippery trails. Great traction. Drained beautifully. Couldn’t have finished without them.

top_reviews.title: Excellent trail running
top_reviews.text:
I was waiting a long time for these to come out. The first run I got in was an 8 miler and I had zero issues. I was worried about the tongue because of other reviews and I did not like the feel of the tongue as I put the shoes on, but it held up great.
The second run I did in then was a ten mile in very technical trails and they were excellent. They drained really well after running through rivers and the weight of them is exactly what I was waiting for.

top_reviews.title: I’ve ran in 1400 for years in a 9 and they were fine aside from extended downhills (toes jammed)
top_reviews.text:
I highly suggest going up 1/2 size. I’ve ran in 1400 for years in a 9 and they were fine aside from extended downhills (toes jammed). The shoe is narrow enough that going up half a size (not width for me) made them the best fitting shoe I’ve used in a long time. Performed flawless at a 12 mile, 4,000 ft gain, and super technical outing.

The tongue does slide down a bit and I didn’t like this. I cut two slices into the tongue where a normal tongue would have a sleeve/loop for laces. This fixed it. Just make sure to use an ultra sharp and skinny blade and be careful. Added a photo of the slits I made.

top_reviews.title: Flat Insoles--no support
top_reviews.text:
These shoes fit as described, however my son and I were shocked at the complete lack of support in the shoe. The insole is completely flat. Unfortunately we didn't discover this until almost two weeks into the cross-country season when he was limping quite horribly. Our mistake. We have had such good experiences with New Balance shoes in the past that we didn't even think to look at the insole. A change in shoe (thanks to a very helpful local running store) and he is back to running like his old self.

On the plus side, if you're looking to remove the insoles and put your own in, these insoles remove easily and leave zero residue, making it quite easy to replace them. That just wasn't a workable option for my son.

top_reviews.title: Wide is not Wide. Buy one size larger
top_reviews.text: I trusted Newbalance to make Wide shoes and have bought many pair of wide shoes from them over the years. The predecessor to this shoe is the Vazee Summit V2 which fits my wide feet perfectly. The Summit Unknown is too narrow. The shoe tag says EE and it even had a paper "Wide" tag on the laces. The shoe is also one size too small. It is a waste of time and money for everyone when Newbalance makes a shoe that is not consistent with standard shoe sizes. Looks like I will have to find my wide shoes from another shoe company.

top_reviews.title: Good and ugly
top_reviews.text: These shoes are ugly. But very comfortable and my feet did not get hot hiking around Yosemite during 90 to 100 degree days. The tongue tends to slide down into the shoe, but it pulls back into place easily. They were also very grippy for clambering over rocks. No sore feet nor blisters after dozens of hard miles. Runs a bit small, but thinner hiking socks keep feet cool and improve fit.

top_reviews.title: No arch support at all
top_reviews.text: Regular 10.5 - 11. I got the 11 and still too small. Runs narrow for a new balance. No arch support at all and paper thin in soles. I bought new insoles but there is not enough volume in the shoe to accommodate. I have arch support now but it's an all around tight fit. I don't think an 11.5 would have helped to much as there still no room for a good in sole. Would not recommend.

top_reviews.title: Shoe are great for uneven terrain like an off road tire
top_reviews.text: My superfeet carbon insert fit well. Shoe are great for uneven terrain like an off road tire.

top_reviews.title: Great Trail and Water Activity Shoe. Keeps you Cool.
top_reviews.text: Great trail and water shoe. Has inner sock liner that protected the bare foot from chaffing from the top of the shoe. Comfortable to be worn with socks or barefoot. Keeps my feet cool in the summer heat and humidity here in Key Largo. I work for a large scuba diving company. Got plenty of compliments on their style. Bought them for home, daily use and use on our dive boats to prevent slipping on wet decks.

top_reviews.title: Made for really narrow feet!

I'm regulating these to dog walking. Swing and a miss NB.

top_reviews.title: Great boots!
top_reviews.text:
I looked for quite a while to find a boot this size that was waterproof (thanks to the Gore-Tex)... I have Danners (which I love) but they are a much larger boot & as a pilot, I need the room for the pedals! They took a little while to break in but I've had them for a month & so far I have been happy... Actually considering buying a second pair...

Update 2016:
I just received my second set! I am admittedly VERY hard on my boots. I wear them day in and day out for work, play, etc. I've had these Bates for over 4 years & 3 of those years these were pretty consistently daily-worn. This includes work on hard surfaces (concrete/asphalt), hiking, yard work, etc. You name it, they've seen it and they've really held up great! I washed them about twice a year and used Danner boot dressing each time and I ended up adding a sole liner for additional padding but even now, they're still pretty much water proof. If my new set lasts half as long as these have, I'll be more than satisfied! The pictures show them as they are now after the 4 years of hard use. As far as I'm concerned, you can't go wrong with these!

Its only been 10 months and the sole is separating allowing water to get in and soak my socks.
Although these boots are slip resistant, they are not as good as my old Timberlands.
The comfort of these boots last about 6-8 hours if you're constantly on your feet. After that the insole becomes uncomfortable.

Update: Purchased a second pair and the outer sole is beginning to separate. No water is getting in so far, but I suspect it'll show the same signs as my last pair. One other thing I've noticed is that if you're on your feet constantly 8-12 hours, the treads on the outer sole also wear around 9-11 months making the shoe more prone to slips. I've decided to try a different brand until bates develops a boot that lasts longer than a year with heavy usage.

top_reviews.title: Waterproof
top_reviews.text: Let's start by saying I run through boots. I get new boots yearly as I work in harsh conditions in Florida as a law enforcement officer. I run through swamp land and am on my feet 9-12 hours intermittently throughout the day. I a need waterproof boots and yearly purchases add up. I've gone through Danners, Timberland Pros, Magnums, New Balance, Under Armor, etc. So on to the boot. These boots fit to size nicely. They absolutely are waterproof so far. I added a couple of insoles (which I always do) and they feel like a pair of sneakers. They are light weight and dont go half way up your calf which is a bonus. They are holding up well as I've ran through many wooded areas through mud, canals, swamp areas, and around urban area. I will definetly be repurchasing these boots as my go to boots.

top_reviews.title: Perfect for Patrol.
top_reviews.text: These boots are excellent for the price.  I've been at traffic collision investigations for hours in the rain in these and no water seepage whatsoever.  While it doesn't rain as much in Los Angeles, when it rains, it -really- rains.  I originally purchased these in May 2016, wore them through the Police Academy, on Patrol, ran in them chasing suspects on tile flooring without sliding as well as dry dirt and mud and still maintaining traction.  These are my only pair of boots, I wear them everyday doing basic patrol and they still hold up.  They are extremely lightweight which makes it great for running and jumping around. They do squeak a little, but unless you're on tile flooring all day you won't even notice.  Fit is spot on.  They will hold a shine and have no issues with the shine at the 'toe-bend' area up front cracking the polish and I even wear them for special occasions in my blues.  There are areas on the sole of the boot and the sides around the ball of your feet where the siding is beginning to come off -- certainly not as quickly as some others have stated. This is only beginning to happen about 13-14 months after initial use. They support well, especially since they are only 4" boots, and i've had great ankle support right out of the box.  I've worn these on the pavement in heat waves without feeling like the bottom of my feet are on fire.  The insole will eventually need replacing (just like any other), but for the price and considering weight, they are "most excellent!".

I had no idea what their Wide and Wide toe box would be, which is why I went a half size up when ordering. I couldn't find their size chart anywhere before ordering. Not docking a star for no size chart since these are nice light shoes that don't make my feet hot and are wide as described.

You can see right through the weave of this material so you can rest assured that you will get air flow to your feet in these. The sole is soft and spongy which is great for absorbing shocks and to my surprise was quite stable when doing side to side hops in them.

For the price these are a good buy. Had I gotten a larger size they would be really great. As it is I'll wear them around barefooted for a while and see if they stretch out some. They are comfortable enough with no socks and not hot at all on my feet.

If you have wide feet you might want to give these a try.

top_reviews.title: Comfort over style
top_reviews.text:
One of the good things about getting older is that many of us are not really worried about style—it’s more about comfort.

I remember when I was a kid and my dentist was wearing something that looked like this—wide in the front, for comfort on his feet all day. I never forgot that and always wondered what that sort of footwear would feel like.

Ordering these, I knew they would look “different.” I was thinking they might look like clown shoes but I have wide feet, and, lately, have been squeezing my toes into shoes or sneakers. In warm weather, I generally prefer sandals for that reason.

In person and on my feet, these do not look as unusual as I would have thought. Their contour kind of reminds me of earth shoes, a pair of which I did have back in those days. These look okay (I chose the gray).

I’d ordered an 8.5, which is my actual size; I usually order a 9 due to the width of my foot. I got a “41,” which is the equivalent. They looked big to me before I put them on, and there is a little room in the toe—probably because of the width, but it is a good fit and they feel comfortable. Let me just say this is a preliminary/early review and I have not walked a mile in these shoes.

They feel cushiony inside when I walk. These are warm-weather sneakers; the uppers are kind of a mesh, really, so I would not wear these in the rain or the cold. I bought them specifically for warm weather. The sole is neither very thick or very thin; they are, as the vendor describes them, lightweight footwear. And I like that! I don’t like heavy shoes.

While they do feel good on my feet, they do not offer arch support. I’m used to that in many inexpensive shoes, so I often put an insert in the shoes or sneakers. However, I do find them very comfortable when walking around. They’re not necessarily for hiking or for much off-road. They’re casualwear.

As far as price, it’s really difficult to find a decent pair of sneakers for less than, say, $45, so—at this point, I think this a fair price. The question will be how long these last and how they wear; both the uppers and lowers. Right now, it’s not the weather to wear these extensively where I live. I promise to come back in the summer or fall and report how they’ve worn and weathered.

But first impressions, they’re very comfortable and look better than I would have thought!

Regarding the photos: My camera adds red to some portions of photos. The gray of these sneakers is pure gray—their color is good. And… I also rolled up my jeans so you could see the footwear!

top_reviews.title: Goofy, lightweight, breathable.
top_reviews.text:
The toe of these shoes are rounded in such a way that it gives them a slightly goofy appearance but they fit my feet really well without squeezing my toes, and the cushioning provides a good amount of support.

The fabric is very lightweight and breathable. I can actually feel the wind on my feet when it blows, which is great because my feet are my thermostat: if they're hot, I'll get overheated fast. Since I have to work on concrete floors is pretty tough to find a pair of shoes that are comfortable AND cool enough to keep me from sweating, but these shoes fit the bill.

So far I've worn them around the house and they're really comfortable. They're so light and they bend and flex with my feet allowing ease of movement. The real test will come when I go to work for 10 hours on a concrete floor so I guess we'll see if these things can stand up to that kind of use, or if they're better for just running around on my days off.

Really good comfy shoes, you won't regret buying.

top_reviews.title: Wow! Great arch support, cushy insole, buckle straps….cute too.
top_reviews.text:
Wow! I am pleasantly surprised how comfortable these sandals are. I have never worn this brand before. First of all, these are relatively inexpensive footwear, and I had my doubts about the quality and comfort. So far….so good. These are the things I like and dislike about them.

They inflate my ego. I normally wear a size 7½, or occasionally an 8, but a size 7 in these sandals fits like a 7 ½ normally does.

The insole is nice and cushy, and it is also perforated. I was afraid all of those little holes would be irritating to my sensitive feet; however, they are not bothersome. There is enough cushion and heel height to make my heel spur behave and not complain. The heel is one inch which is perfect for summertime casual.

The straps are also wide enough to hide, but not irritate my bunion.

I bought the crazy horse desert color, and it is a neutral one that goes with about anything.

I like the buckles instead of the hook and loop closures that are usually found on sandals. They look nice and are easily adjustable if necessary.

The leather is slightly stiff, and I was afraid that might be a problem. Nope, I was wrong again because it does not feel stiff on my feet. The leather does show scuff marks easily, but I guess that gives them character….or something!

Oh yes, these sandals have a terrific arch support. When I first tried them on, I thought that it was entirely too high for my feet; however, it is not. In fact, it feels super terrific!

top_reviews.title: Most comfortable sandals I've ever owned --- after a break in period
top_reviews.text:
I now own three pairs of these sandals. The first pair is three years old and it occurred to me that eventually they'll need replaced, and may be discontinued by that time, so I purchased two more pairs. The three year old pair is so incredibly comfortable, it's easy to forget that I'm even wearing something on my feet. I have an issue with one of my big toes and these sandals put absolutely no pressure on my toes.

But... the first day I wore one of the new pairs, I wore them for 7 hours straight where I was on my feet the entire time, walking about 20,000 steps. My feet were so incredibly sore at the end of that day that I could hardly walk. Turns out that the very outside edge of the insole is a bit raised and put some pressure on the outside edges of my feet that I didn't really notice until it was too late. That said, after resting my feet for a day, I continue to wear these and still love them. I'm confident that, after time, the raised outside edge of the insole will wear down a bit and form fit to the way I walk and will be just as comfortable as my three-year-old pair.

As for the size, with pumps, boots or cross trainers, I wear 8-1/2. For these I wear a size 8. Don't worry about the width. They're pretty wide but the buckles let you tighten them up if you have skinny feet.

top_reviews.title: These are "Nubuck" leather -- how to remove oil stains
top_reviews.text:
Some reviews say these sandals are not real leather. They are real leather, but not smooth leather like you'd normally think of. It's kind of a cross between leather and suede. It doesn't seem to get spotted by water (like suede would). However, I found out that an OILY substance does leave a dark spot. I wore these sandals while cooking and a tiny bit of melted butter dropped on the leather. Dishwashing liquid and water did not budge it. Per a tip on the internet, I tried rubbing the oil stain with talcum powder and letting the powder sit overnight. (Later I realized this tip was intended for smooth leather, not leather with this brushed texture.) This method did lighten the stain a little, but the powder also sort of ground into the surface and lightened the entire area around the stain.

So then I wondered about applying leather conditioner, but found those say "not for use on suede or nubuck." Hmmm... what's "nubuck"? A leather that has been sanded to produce a velvety texture -- that's the type of leather in these sandals. I found a tip on Hunker that said to clean nubuck, "Dip a cotton swab in vinegar and rub it into any difficult wet or dry stains. Wipe the white vinegar away with a soft cloth." I did this (and followed up with a damp rag), and now that the area has dried the oil stain is pretty much gone (see photo). This article also recommended that nubuck be sprayed with "nubuck protectant" every 6 months in order to prevent stains. I didn't think these sandals would require maintenance, but maybe it would be worth it to prevent future oil stains?

The oil-staining issue is my only complaint about these sandals. They have great arch support and are very comfortable -- exactly what I was searching for. I also like that the buckles make the width adjustable. I would add that the "Reggae footbed" took a little getting used to (the arch support seemed very tall at first), but I quickly grew to like it. As far as sizing, I usually wear a size 7.5 in regular shoes and a 7 in these sandals fits perfectly. Overall, I am very satisfied with my purchase.

top_reviews.text: I have odd-shaped feet and rely on Crocs' wide toe box to keep me comfortable whatever I'm doing. I also like to take long walks and sometimes don't make it home before dark. These nifty little headlights are awesome! I can see where I'm walking at night, and for quite a distance ahead, as the lights are super-bright. top_reviews.title: Useful in the dark
top_reviews.text:
Originally bought some for my husband and initially thought they were as ridiculous as the Crocs they go on. But hey, even though I think they look like clown shoes, I wear them - a LOT. lol
So even though I thought headlights for Crocs sounded insane, I thought about it...I wear them to the dog park, and in the summer we're there at night. No more worrying about stepping in poop! And not just for the dog park - in our semi-rural area it's great to have some added security against critters at night while walking around.
These are fairly cute, being shiny silver. And they're much brighter than I thought they would be. They have a dual function, one being a continuous light, and the other being a flashing light. I may not use the flashing light, but it's a nice idea if walking down the street at night. I haven't tested whether or not they're really waterproof, but it's a nice feature so I don't have to worry.
So yeah...headlights for Crocs. Why the heck not?

top_reviews.text: No issues with order fulfillment and the actual shoes were great looking and appeared to be well made for the price. My dissatisfaction is due to the size of the shoes. Everything I read on Amazon said the sizes on these ran true. Since I'm a size 11 in every shoe I own, that's what I ordered.  After receiving, I tried them on and they fit more like a 12+. I liked the style/design so much that I figured I'd take a chance and order a size 10 hoping that would work and then I'd just return the earlier purchase.  To my disappointment, the second order was lost by the shipping company so I canceled that order and got a refund. Then, while shopping locally, I came across a pair of Keen's that were the right size, price and style so I went that direction instead and sent the original pair back to the seller.

top_reviews.title: So Far So Good--Better than Expected
top_reviews.text:
I have wide feet and am usually against buying any kind of footwear online. If I can find wide sizes, I can wear a 9 1/2 EEE. If it is medium width, I have to get at least a 10 1/2. It was recommended to go a size down on these, but I ordered a 9 1/2 anyway. I did not expect them to be a good fit, but they fit almost perfectly right out of the box-- length AND width. They may have been just a tad tight on the width, but after wearing them for a full day, the fit was absolutely perfect.
Two other reasons for buying this particular brand was (1) I have always wanted a pair of Keens but wary about spending so much on a shoe that will be repeatedly abused month after month-- right now Keens are NOT getting good reviews The price on these are pretty good at this point. (2) I don't know how many times I have slipped on a muddy creek bank due to boots or sandals with insufficient grip. These sandals are GRIPPY.
So far so good. I hope to do an update after trying these in the field for a couple months.

top_reviews.title: Roomy, lightweight, soft
top_reviews.text:
An excellent shoe. I'm very impressed with Propet shoes.

I'm at the age where comfort is more important than being stylish. But I still don't want to look dorky. These shoes are not bad looking at all.

Propets are the most comfortable of the sport/casual shoes I've tried. They seem to be correctly sized for my feet although I ordered a half size larger than shoes made in the USA--this was just to be sure since other brands I've tired sometimes run a full size smaller than marked. These shoes run wide, so take that into consideration if ordering. I wear an E/EE but the wide size for the Propets are EEE. They are a little too wide for me with regular socks but not enough so my foot slides around inside. A thicker sock and all is well.

They are very light in weight--something that is a plus when you're on your feet a lot. While other shoes this light have proven to wear fairly quickly, I've had good luck with other Propet shoes. They hold up well for me. They are pretty well cushioned inside and the leather is soft to the touch. All this makes for a very comfortable casual shoe.

In addition to the comfort factor, Propet says the Nollie is machine washable in cold water, air dry with paper wadded inside the toe area. I haven't worn them enough for them to need this level of cleaning but that's really icing on the cake. What else can you say? Propet shoes are well made, supremely comfortable, easy to care for, look good and they don't cost a whole lot. No brainer.

top_reviews.title: Love..a bit wide and long. Great for summer growth
top_reviews.text: Just got these and haven’t worn them yet but I’m giving 5 stars for fit and style/color. I bought all three colors available. My son is 20 months old and we have a hard time finding shoes that fit as it seems he has a wide & thick foot. I bought a size 8 toddler and Love that these shoes have an adjustment strap on the top and the back. These were wide enough for his feet to fit in and had spare room to grow this summer length wise.  I bought another brand that looked similar at the same time again in size 8 and I couldn’t get his feet even into them. I stuffed his feet in and his toes were almost at the toe and his heel was off the back of the shoe with his foot being to wide to get them in any further. So I’d say these shoes run a bit wide and long which is perfect for what I was looking for especially with the two adjustment straps giving even more tightening or growing room. Great price for the shoe and they came with a little pair of socks as well.

top_reviews.title: Ran a little large
top_reviews.text: Bought these for my grandson that has been in size 9T for quite some time. I worried that they'd be too small but actually were a little loose. Plenty of room for a wide foot and/or high instep. He'll get lots of wear out of them. Adjustable straps across the top and around the heel for extra fit. One thing I looked for in a sandal was the heel strap that was also attached to the foot bed and the adjustable strap goes on the outside of the foot bed sewn in heel material. Last year he had a pair with just the strap and it rubbed his heel raw. The extra padded material stops that from happening. If that makes any sense.

top_reviews.title: Good Shoe for Climbers who Value Comfort
top_reviews.text:
After trying on several different brands of climbing shoes at the local REI and EMS, I purchased these through Amazon, because only Amazon had my size. As I've only been climbing for a few weeks, I was not interested in a hyper-aggressive shoe with a sharp downturn and a tiny toe box. That said, if you're climbing 5.11 routes and beyond, maybe you'll want something more aggressive. For me, however, these are great. In the end, it came down to a choice between this - the Scarpa Helix, and the La Sportiva Nago, and I ended up going with these due to the *slightest* advantage in comfort. (I would not hesitate to purchase the La Sportiva Nago, if the Scarpa Helix didn't exist.) My fiancee went with the La Sportiva Nago (women's version, of course), and she's pleased with them, so your mileage may vary.

First, let me describe the shoe: All of the shoe is leather except for the sole, the pull strap on the heel, the stitching, and the laces. Stitching is remarkably sturdy-looking throughout, and if memory serves, the shoe is stamped "Made in Italy" on the inside. Being an Italian shoe, sizing is European... (with US equivalents) but get this... for me, comparing the Scarpa Helix to the La Sportiva Nago (another Italian shoe), I was a FULL SIZE BIGGER in the Scarpa Helix... so keep that in mind when ordering. (Just to be clear, put a US 10 Scarpa Helix sole to sole next to a US 9 La Sportiva Nago, and they will be pretty much identical.)

Seriously - you are probably thinking "This guy isn't buying shoes that are tight enough," but you're wrong. I did my research and talked with several super-experienced climbers, so I know-I know-I KNOW that just about everyone says that you should buy climbing shoes a little smaller than your street shoe size, but THROW THAT LINE OF THINKING OUT OF THE WINDOW when sizing yourself for a Scarpa Helix. I say this because even if you use your street shoe as your starting point for fitting, you are probably going to find that the Scarpa Helix is way, WAY tighter than you're expecting, and you'll end up moving up half a size or more.

In my case, I actually ended up with a size slightly LARGER than my street shoe size, and trust me - they fit perfectly - SUPER snug like a climbing shoe should be... with no room at the toe, and tight to the point where a little breaking in / stretching would be welcome, but still not painful to wear. I'm telling you, the Helix IS a quality shoe, but Scarpa's sizing is WAY off. Still, don't let that dissuade you from buying these, or at least trying them.

A huge factor in the comfort of these shoes is the toe box, which is a little more ample than you'll find in other climbing shoes (except for the Nago, which also has a somewhat ample toe box). Honestly, some climbing shoes border on being 19th century foot-binding devices, but not the Helix (or the Nago, for that matter). The thing to look for (if you're NOT one of the climbers who thinks that they should be in pain the entire time they're climbing, or who secretly desires mountain goat feet) is a normal-ish looking toe box; specifically, note that the laces in the Scarpa Helix and the La Sportiva Nago DO NOT extend all the way to the end of the toe. That, my friends - along with the leather upper and overall quality construction - is probably why this shoe is so comfortable. Less lacing also makes for a quicker on-off procedure, which saves you time before and after you climb.

As for how they perform - again, I'm definitely a novice climber, and not even remotely advanced - but I haven't slipped since buying these. Standing on a 1" ledge, I'm noticeably more secure than I would've been in the gym's rentals (mostly well-worn Five Tens and Mad Rocks). Also, the sole didn't seem to require an initial break-in climb like it did on my fiancee's Nagos. (Her Nagos were slipping on her first day of use, but for her second day and beyond, she loves them.) By contrast, the Helix seemed to grip from the beginning, although that may be due to individual differences in weight and movement style.

So, in summary, I recommend the Scarpa Helix for non-advanced climbers who require a decent toe box. If you order, I suggest starting at your US street shoe size, if not, half a size up. Once you get that pair and try them on, note the European size and adjust up or down from there, and don't bother even referring to the US number.

If you get the Scarpa Helix and you don't like them, I suggest giving the La Sportiva Nago a shot.

top_reviews.title: Comfortable, not aggressive, doesn't last
top_reviews.text:
I bought a pair of these about six months ago. Some thoughts:

* They're designed for wider feet. I have long, somewhat narrow feet, and I find the sole a bit too wide. You can partially correct with the laces, but you'll lose a little confidence on smaller holds.

* The heel doesn't slip. I chose them over La Sportiva's Naga shoe for this reason.

* The leather expands significantly. My in-store size (10.5; I wear an 11.5 street shoe) was almost unbearable to stand on for any length of time. After six or eight climbing sessions, the shoes expanded to be the ideal length. I can wear them for about fifteen minutes at a time before I want to chuck them off. Here's how to size a new pair: extend your foot to a ballet point. If there's any clearance or looseness at all at the tip of the shoe, it's too big. The toe box for a new leather shoe should feel very snug with your foot in a point and very uncomfortable with your foot flat. Go up a half-size if the shoe is synthetic.

* The rubber is decently sticky, not great, and the inside edge isn't that sharp. At a gym 5.10 level, I found them adequate. At 5.11/5.12 with thin holds, there isn't enough feel to be confident.

* I've managed to wear through the rubber in front of both toes. I don't scramble up routes and rarely do any sort of foot dragging. I retired my previous pair of shoes undamaged after climbing for twice as long. This shoe will be totally unforgiving of poor foot technique.

On balance, not a bad shoe, and significantly stickier and more comfortable than the gym rental shoes. It's definitely for mid-range use though. If you're a novice climber, you're liable to wear through the soles quickly. And if you're accelerating to the harder routes, you'll probably want a sharper toe.

top_reviews.text:
Maybe it was sold out, but 7.5 was the only half size that wasn't available to choose. Unfortunately for me, I tend to wear a 7.5. I can wear two pairs of socks and it seems to be fine, but I just really wish they had a 7.5.

I will say that these really are EXTREMELY light. Usually when reviewers say that, I find that it's not true. In this case, it most certainly is. It's because the sole is not made from rubber, it's made from a foam-type of material. It does make me wonder how it would hold up to any moisture or long-term wear. It did smell like cheap fake leather when I unwrapped it, but that personally didn't bother me. The included shoelaces are far too slippery and don't allow me to really tighten the circumference of the shaft of the shoe (remember, skinny shins), so I'll be buying my own.

Overall, not a bad purchase, but for the price I wish it was just a *little* better quality.

them the point snagged on the lace which caused me to look and feel what it was caught on before my daughter slid her foot in.

Other than the defect which could have easily been overlooked due to location these shoes were good quality especially considering they’re priced low for a split sole design. The split sole allows for much greater improvement in the flexibility of the shoe with the foot in motion.

The shoes were lightweight and the taps sounded good. Shipping was super fast. The insoles were a bit papery feeling but I can’t attest to if they’d hold up to repeated use.

top_reviews.title: I wear all New Balance, this is a great shoe!
top_reviews.text:
[[VIDEOID:f48eda1cdb0880bb1866d3976e8efa61]] I adore my New Balance Rebels version 1 and version 2, which are "speedy" non-carbon-plated shoes using gel-like Fuelcell foam that is fast and smooth. When New Balance ruined the Rebel version 3 by adding foam and making it a "daily trainer", I began a search for a new version, low-profile fast shoe, willing to leave my favorite brand to find what I was looking for.

Fortunately for New Balance, I found the SC Pacer. Although the online video reviews are luke-warm on this shoe (mainly dinging it's lack of cushioning and lackluster carbon "propulsion" compared to similar competitors), I found the shoe speedy and lightweight. It's upper is literally webbed, seeing your sock right through the holes. The tongue has no padding. The sole has little extra rubber for outsole protection, so the longevity of the shoe will almost certainly be less than most. One must buy this shoe knowing its intended purpose: speed work. I will use it for tempo runs, repetitions, hill repeats, and 5K 10K races.

The one knock is that the fit is slightly sloppy for a low-profile racing shoe. I always wear the same size New Balance shoe, but for this particular model I needed to add a thin insole over the supplied (and glued-in) insole to take up a small amount of top-to-bottom space in the shoe. It's as though the shoe is a little too generous in that dimension, likely due to the U-shaped tongue opening that interferes with cinching it securely; a V-shaped opening would allow more user fine-tuning. The fit is one thing mentioned by many online reviews. For me, the added thin insole did the trick, give it a try.

Overall, a shoe that will serve me well for my 2023 season. I think, however, that the SC (SuperComp) model line, and in particular this Pacer model, will eventually fall into obscurity. New Balance, if you are reading this, please re-make your Rebel into the shoe it was intended to be in versions 1 and 2....and add a carbon-plate for a Rebel Comp model.
