top_reviews.title: If I didn't know better, I'd say these are counterfeit!
top_reviews.text:
I have purchased and worn-out Reef Flip Flops for decades. I am loyal to this brand because of their consistent quality, durability, comfort, and feel. This particular pair, however, have fallen way short in everything I have learned to accept as a Reef product.
First, they hurt. No, it is not the usual break-in with the toe strap - it is the lack of resiliency in the heel cushioning. Both of my heels are bruised as a result of stepping on half-dollar sized stones, which are common in my neck of the tropics. I never had that problem with any of my other Reefs!.
Second, they stink. I am at the point now that I have to spray them with a bathroom cleanser with bleach every evening because they reek of something awful. Please don't go assuming I have a foot odor or sweating problem - I don't, and again, this was never a problem with any of the other dozens of Reefs I have owned.
Third - they have a terrible friction coefficient - I slip on almost every substrate with this things on my feet! My others, you guessed it, had great traction!
Seeing how out of the ordinary these feel, smell, and perform, I can only conclude that these are NOT genuine Reef Flip Flops, unless the company made a dramatic change to their manufacturing processes and/or material sourcing. Or perhaps I receive a factory prototype that went wrong? Either way, if you are expecting the usual greatness of a Reef Flip Flop, do not buy these. I am replacing them ASAP...

The BIG DRAWBACK is that these sandals aren't meant for use around large amounts of water. If you walk through water or get them submerged in another way the tight cell cushion foam will absorb water, then when you walk they actually spit out foamy water as you walk as the water gets agitated coming up from the foam bed. They seem to take at least overnight to dry out so can be pretty annoying. Pretty hilarious since the brand name "Reef" would imply their brand was made to be used around salt water which was my purpose this week down on Ft. Walton Beach.

So good sandals for around town in the summer but avoid them if your primary purpose is lake or beach wearing. I'm going to the beach for another week in October and plan to get another pair of Sanuk's.

top_reviews.title: Great Flip Flops - Super Comfortable!
top_reviews.text: Have been wearing this Reef Cushion Phantom model (pictured) daily for about three years. The white marks in the photos are reflections. You can notice some expected wear, but still going strong! Soft without losing foot or arch support and a long-lasting sole. Very comfortable. I wear a 10 Wide (EE) on a normal street shoe (44 EU) and wear a 9 (42 EU) on these flip flops. My heel is at the back of the flip flop without extra material showing behind my heel, which I like. The straps attach to the outside of the sole, which makes them a wider fit without the sole being wider (nice detail). The color shown in the photo - tan thongs (the straps on top of foot) - with brown soles is softer and more pliable than either my brown thongs or my black thongs of the same brand and model. The tan thongs (straps) are a heavy cotton-like fabric material (looks like leather) with a padded jersey fabric liner beneath (that makes contact with the top of my foot); whereas the brown and black thong tops appear to be leather (definitely thicker and stiffer than the tan) with the same type of padded jersey liner beneath (as the tan). Odd the difference in material on the same model. While I wear all three pairs regularly, for me, the tan pair is by far the most comfortable because of the top-of-the-thong material being more pliable (while still maintaining its shape). The bottom of the sole (that makes contact with the pavement) is a chevron patterned and excellent wearing sole (see photo after three years of wear) that is stable on most wet and smooth concrete. I live at the beach and do not baby these flips flops. I wear them often onto the sand, into the salt water, and come back with mud caked and ground in from walking. They hold up well and don't stretch or blow out. After a coarse rinse and drying time it's just like they were the day before. Great for casual wear complementing swimwear, shorts, khaki pants, and jeans. I just bought a backup pair in tan and hope Reef will continue making this model (Cushion Phantom). Summary: You can't go wrong with tan, brown, or black. Highly recommend without reservation!

Update July 2020: These are flat worn out. Not near the quality of my previous pair. Within a month I could see where the very thin coating on top had worn through leaving a perfect imprint of my foot. Soles have worn out, and these soak up water if you walk on wet surfaces. top_reviews.title: cushion phantom is the number one slippah for me
top_reviews.text:
I live in Waikiki. Which means a couple of things. I walk a lot, and I never wear shoes. There are few things more important to me than a good pair of slippahs. The number of other ones I've tried are an embarrassment to admit. They include Olokai, Sanuk, Cobian, Teva, Nike, Skechers, Hurley, Rainbow, and Scott. I suppose everyone's feet are different, and even other models of Reefs have been only marginally acceptable.
But the Cushion Phantom by Reef is hands down the best. I can walk for miles in these, and they are as comfortable as a pair of walking shoes.
A couple of things: when I get them, I take a razor blade and remove the little decorative tag they put on the strap. What genius thought of putting that there? It causes a rub mark, or if I walk far enough, a blister. Dumb.
Also, if I'm headed to the ocean, these stay home, squishy soles and water are a bad combination.
I wear a size 13, and size 13 in these are a tiny bit too big, but the 12's are a tiny bit too small. I'll take the 13's any day. They have just a little arch support, which fit my feet like a glove.
The straps on the tan and brown ones are softer than the other colors, but the platform is slightly firmer.

I was going to buy the fugly looking shoes with the toes in them.  Luckily I saw that my sister bought a pair of Minnetonkas.  They are the ankle boots.  She told me they are really comfortable and people who do "earthing" swear by them.  Earthing?  You can look it up but basically you are allowing more of the earth's magnetic field into your body through your feet.  All I know is that yesterday I wore these shoes out to go shopping and my knees did not hurt.  Sure, I'm stiff but I did not have the usual stabbing horrible pain I get when I go out in tennis shoes.  I thought for sure this morning I would be crippled but no.  My knees and legs were stiff but no pain.  I usually wake up in the middle of the knight with shooting stabbing pains in my knees but not last night.  I'm ordering more of these shoes.  They are amazing!

top_reviews.text: I normally wear a 6 1/2 or 7.  I ordered 7 in white smooth.  It was delivered 3 days late and then was way too long and wide.  I had 1/2-3/4" behind my heel in length, so I returned.  Then, I read reviews saying they ran large.  I then ordered a 6 in natural smooth and could hardly squeeze my foot in it, so I returned.  By this time I was in a time crunch for when I needed so I ordered both 6 1/2 and another 7 in natural smooth.  The 6 1/2 was a little tight lengthwise and fine width wise.  The 7 was the same length as the 6 1/2 but was wide.  I knew they would soften up and stretch some so I kept the 6 1/2 and returned the 7.  I have worn them the last 3 days and pleased with the shoe.  Quality made, they just need to get their sizing under control.  I have reduced 1 star for sizing issues.

I will say, that I wanted them to fit snugly because I knew they would break in and stretch out and I wanted them to conform to my feet. I returned them and ordered the 8s instead. The first time I wore them they felt perfect. The second time I wore them (out of the house, for more than 30 minutes) they gave me blisters on my second to last toes. This price is quite reasonable compared to showrooms.  My wife commented on them coming back and how she remembered trudging through the woods wearing them as a kid at camp.  Imagine her surprise when I found them on Amazon and ordered them as a surprise.  Now she wears hem with her favorite $200 jeans and only for it is not gonna rain.  What's old is new again. top_reviews.title: These run large, not as durable as I would have hoped. Consider your climate before ordering.
top_reviews.text:
I'd love to try 4.5 or 4 to see if they fit better (5, my normal size, felt like big floppy slippers). But they were great quality and super cute. May order again.

UPDATE: I normally wear size 5 in everything. I ordered again and purchased a 4. Perfect fit. I love them and wear them often. They definitely bleed orange dye all over your feet if they get damp or wet, though they recover just fine when they dry again. I have a severe dye allergy but didn't react to the color coming off of these.

UPDATE 2: I liked these while they lasted, but almost 1 year later to the date, there are holes in the bottom. Next time, I'd probably get Manitobah Mukluks (also available on Amazon, and I'm not affiliated in any way) because of the rubber soles. I'd probably order the Minnetonka brand for house slippers, or in a climate with no moisture. With the heat, humidity, and rain in the South, my poor moccasins just couldn't handle it. While in my first update I felt they recovered fine from water exposure, at a certain point, weather exposure was too much for them. I didn't wear them in the rain on purpose, but the climate where I live is very unpredictable, and we can get intense summer storms out of the blue.

It will change the look and color, but I love the Sno-Seal waterproofing product on Amazon, and may try that next time around. Or reserve them for use on sunny days or indoor use only.

top_reviews.title: Nice mocs, super bad delivery -- Amazon needs to stop using Ontrac
top_reviews.text:
I've had a number of moccasins from Minnetonka through the years, and they are always good quality and nice styling. Next best thing to being barefoot. I love that these sole-less mocs are so quiet when I walk around my wood floors. The foam insert is comfy. They fit true to size -- order a half size larger if you want to wear them with heavier winter socks.

BUT -- Because there is no place to complain about ONTRAC delivery, I'm doing it here, hoping the sellers have a way to complain to Amazon Fulfillment Service or to ONTRAC. My building has entrances on two sides -- one close to the street and for the other you have to walk around the building or come in from the parking lot /pool side. It's not that big a building, only 2 units on a side, so only 8 in the whole building. Takes less than 2 minutes to walk to the other side. ONTRAC consistently leaves packages on the wrong side of the building. These mocs are the 4th wrongly delivered package from ONTRAC this year while FedEx and USPS can manage to read the label and get the correct unit's door. Having nice neighbors who bring the package around or let me know it there is not the point -- It's like ONTRAC delivery can't be bothered with accuracy or security of your delivering orders. Minus 10 stars to Ontrac. Plus 10 stars to Minnetonka.

top_reviews.title: Sizing is Huge!  HUGE.
top_reviews.text:
I felt compelled to review these shoes because of the large amount of time I spent reading other customers' reviews before ordering them. I was very concerned that the majority of the reviewers talked about the unusual sizing issues with this shoe. I ordered them for both of my boys and the other reviewers were absolutely correct in that the Youth shoes run huge. Absolutely HUGE. There is truly no way to accurately convey the extent of this until you order them. However, I will try. My 10 y.o. son normally wears the equivalent of a woman's size 6.5 (I buy him unisex looking Merrell sneakers because he has a narrow foot). Therefore, before reading all of the customer reviews, I had planned to get him a Tom's Youth 6. However, after reading the customer reviews, I ended up ordering him a Youth 4.5 even though it seemed totally silly. But, sure enough, the other reviewers were spot on--even the 4.5 is enormous! I wear a Women's size 8 in my own Toms shoes, and the Toms Youth 4.5 fit ME! I was laughing when I took the Youth 4.5 out of the box. I even took a photo of my red size 8 Women's Toms next to the black Toms Youth 4.5 and they are almost the same size--see attached photos (also, please note that is my women's size 7.5/8 foot next to the Tom's Youth 4.5!!!). So, I just ordered the Youth 4 instead and I am sure my son will still need to wear them with socks.

My 7 y.o. son normally wears a Youth 3.5 in other brands and his last pair of Tom's (this same style) that I bought a full year ago, were a size 2. Therefore, I went with a size 3 and when they came I saw that he will need to wear two pairs of socks with them. The difference even between half sizes is incredible!!! I should have gone with a 2.5, which would still have been a full size smaller than his shoe size in all other shoe brands.

Therefore, my sizing advice since these are such unusual shoes is to start by going down at least one full size, with the expectation that you will probably need to return them and go down another 1/2 to a full size on top of that. Strange but true. Please note that these shoes also run wide since they are not very structured and, being cloth, will stretch.

As for the other features of the Youth shoe, it is nice looking, supportive (more so than the women's version), and durable (this is our second pair by growth). My only other complaint besides the incorrect sizing is that the shoes pick up a lot of lint due to the material they are made of and have to be maintained regularly and not just tossed in a shoe basket. Therefore, we carefully save ours to use for "non-sneaker occasions" since they can totally pass with a pair of black dress pants and a nice tee in the summer months if your boys protest about wearing proper dress shoes, as mine do. Overall, the black ones make for a nice looking, dressy-casual, summer shoe.

HOWEVER, this is such a great looking shoe that I will pay the $19 to have my local shoe repair shop cut a half inch off of the heel. Then I will use some clear liquid latex (like flex seal) and paint two coats onto the flocked bottom. Liquid latex gives shoes great traction. Lastly, I will put some good gel insoles on the inside and that should make them a pretty perfect pair of shoes. This means I  will have to invest about $45, after tax, to make them work for me... but I WILL make them a beautiful and comfortable pair of shoes.  If I fail, I will come back and update this. If I’m successful, I will purchase two more pair in different colors, IF they ever go on sale for at least $10 or $12 off. top_reviews.title: Cheap shoes....but may work for some people
top_reviews.text:
I love comfort shoes. I love heels. I love block heels. And I love black patent leather. So thought I'd love these. Was hoping to nab a nice looking, comfortable pair of heels for quick and easy "throw 'em on and be out the door" moments when I'm carting kids around or running errands. Didn't minbd the fake leather because the point was to spare my nicer shoes from unnecessary wear. I also thought this shoe looked like it had a good grip sole. None of my assumptions turned out to be true. The sole does not grip well at all.....I have to walk carefully just on the dry tile inside of my house. Comfort is OK....but it runs a tad too big so my feet need to "grip" them as I walk. Just for reference: I ordered size 8.5 W.....I wear 8.5 W in almost everything. In Clarks and Stuart Weitzman I'm usually an 8 W, in Cole Haan or Naturalizer I'm always an 8.5 or 8.5 W (the "W" preferred). Nikes, Sketchers.....always an 8.5.

Overall, I don't recommend these shoes unless you're on a budget and can get them for way less than $40. If you are on a budget and this fits what you're looking for, then make sure you get the sizing right, check on return policy, and maybe plan a trip to shoe repair shop to have real rubber grip soles added to them.

top_reviews.title: I like them but they make my feet look super wide
top_reviews.text: I tried a pair of Easy Spirit mules a few years ago but they were too wide even in the narrow size. But when I saw that these shoes could be cinched down with the laces, I decided to try them. I normally wear a 9N or 9 1/2 N in all brands. The 9 1/2N fit me in this shoe. Usually, even size narrow or AA shoes are slightly loose on me, but wearable.  This 9.5N shoe was a little tight on my right (larger) foot, but it loosened after one wearing, so it’s fine now. They are too wide across the instep and at the foot opening, but I will be able to cinch them down with laces. I have ordered replacement laces, as the ones on the shoes are not meant for tying. But the eyelet holes are fully functioning and there are even 2 extra holes on each side of the tongue (see pic), so tie-able laces should work well. One thing I don’t like about these shoes is that they make my markedly skinny feet, which have never looked wide in any pair of shoes in my life, look super wide. It’s really quite hilarious. I can only imagine what they would look like on feet that are medium or wide width. Even when I pull the elastic super tight and hold it, they still look wide. Oh well, I have so little selection in shoes due to my feet being so narrow, I’m not going to worry about it. They are comfortable enough due to a nicely cushioned footbed, but they have no discernible arch support. So I will either wear arch support wraps or glue some arch supports into the foot bed (in my experience, the adhesive ones don’t stick to this type of surface). I ordered navy and black, and both colors look like the pictures. I am not crazy about the easy spirit logo prominently displayed on the tongue or the “walk run” caption on the sides. Looks tacky if you ask me. Lastly, on the right blue shoe the tongue is stitched in crookedly. But I don’t think it will be noticeable to anyone else. I want this style of shoe more than I dislike the imperfections of these, and I don’t get many choices, so I’m keeping them.

top_reviews.title: CAUTION
top_reviews.text:
First off: if you are genuinely looking to start pointe, be sure that you have been approved by your teachers and that you are professionally fitted! Secondly: I ordered these purely for experimentation and, was hoping, that I could use the soft shank to build some strength, but they run so unbelievably small both in the box and in the length that even sizing up twice was not completely to solve the problem. These can be fun if you're just looking for some cute ballet shoes for your small dancers for a costume, but even then I highly encourage you to purchase either ballet slippers and sew on ribbons for the look, or to buy Demi pointe shoes, but absolutely not real pointe shoes for playing in unless the child has dance and ballet training. Pointe shoes can be extremely dangerous if you are not ready for them, and you can do something as serious as break your ankle, or even rip muscles in the bottom of your feet(in the arch) so please, do not get these for costume play! Go to a website like discount dance or sodanca and order canvas ballet slippers and ribbons for very young dancers, or semi pointe shoes if the child is slightly older if all you want these for is the look.
However, if you are classically trained, these can be good for building muscle if you know what you're doing, but size up a lot, especially if you have a high instep, a wide foot, or both. I hope this was helpful!

top_reviews.title: I've eschewed all of my conventional padded footwear since discovering Xero shoes.
top_reviews.text:
So far I own a pair of the Z-Trek, the Hana, and the Prio. These shoes have allowed me to throw out basically every other pair of other shoes that I own, besides my Merrell gloves, which I use exclusively for running. The Xero shoes fill in all my other shoe/sandal needs, but I can certainly run in them. After fully adapting to barefoot footwear I really hate to wear any "normal" shoe with pointed toe box, foam, heel to toe drop, and stiff uppers. My posture, balance, core strength and running technique are all drastically improved. I no longer suffer from hip, knee, or shin pain. I am now basically a zealous opponent of conventional padded shoes with raised heels and the biomechanical deficiencies they facilitate.

I love that they now make the Hana and Prio in all black and it's what compelled me to finally buy the Prio. The patent-pending design of the sole is simple and great. The rubber does conform to the foot a bit and has proved to be quite durable. It is however, not anti-slip. The only uncomfortable shoe I am still forced to wear on a regular basis are my work shoes with anti-slip soles. The front of the toe box on the full shoes and general design is very nice, and the strap system allows the shoe to move and stay with your foot. The Hanas are more comfortable than any slippers I have worn but even with the slip-on sort of style, I can run with them because of the straps.

As far as sizing I'd recommend erring on the larger size. All my Xeros are 11. As comparison my Merrell vapor and trail gloves are 10.5.

I started trying to run "barefoot" years ago when Vibrams were first a thing and I will say it took quite a long time for my feet and biomechanics to fully adapt, especially while still mostly wearing other conventional shoes. It wasn't until I found closed toe, zero-drop/padding shoes that I could really convert so I'm glad it's becoming more widely available and Xero seems to be really leading the way on how to build them nicely.

top_reviews.title: Bought after KoT recommended. Go down a size
top_reviews.text:
Bought these after they were recommended by Knees Over Toes Guy.
Typical shoes (unnaturally) bunch your toes together and give you a raised heel.
I think narrow toe boxes are meant to look better as they make your foot appear slender and they also *seem* to emulate and create an ideal pushing motion of your foot.
Raised heels are likely to be used to exaggerate your foots position to push off the ball of your foot.
These are just my thoughts.
The PROBLEM with narrow toe boxes is that they deform your feet and cause bunions.
Raised heels on shoes shorten the length of your Achilles’ tendon, since it does not have to be elongated as much when the heel is raised.
These aren’t opinions. Raised heels also makes you more vulnerable to rolling you ankle AND the rolls will be worse, as your heel is further from the ground. This is proven, see KoT guy and SquatU videos on this.

Now that I explained how typical shoes work,
Here is how these shoes function:
These shoes do Not Have an elevated heel. They do have a toe box that is shaped to fit your foot in a more natural shape.
This enables you to use your foot like a tripod and get maximum stability from your foot. This is great for weight lifters.
The flat bottom profile returns your Achilles’ tendon length to its natural state and promotes better ankle mobility, which is pivotal to a deep squat. (If your ankle mobility is less than ideal, try elevating your heel on some plates.)

I have always ordered shoes too big because I did not like the feeling of my toes touching the sides of my shoes. I used to wear 11-12 shoes so my I could get a wider shoe at expense of having extra space at the end.
I ordered 11’s of this shoe and they had far too much space at the end.
I returned for 10.5’s and they fit much better. I don’t need extra space at the end of the shoe. Also, the extra space causes your foot to slide in your shoe, creating unnecessary calluses.

Cons:
These shoes certainly aren’t the most stylish. Could be worse but they aren’t anything to brag about.
The wide toe box looks unnatural since most ppl wear narrow shoes.
The shoes are quite thin. This is great for foot awareness as much of that is lost with shoes on, but I cannot wear these walking on rocks or roots, as you’ll feel every one. Concrete is not terrible but your feet weren’t really made to walk on such a hard material so more cushion would be helpful.
Running in these shoes puts a great deal of force on your calves.

I wear these at the gym and walking around the store and flat areas.
My feet are noticeably stronger and I can actually feel the ground under my feet with them on. I’m much more aware of how my feet are moving and reacting. My balance has improved drastically.
KoT guy said he used these for basketball. I thought he was crazy until I tried it. I’ve never worn low top shoes for basketball due to my previously weak ankles. Now these are my basketball shoe. They have great tread. (KoT guy is currently developing wide toe, zero drop basketball shoes with a YouTube sneaker head that will have a thicker sole. I will buy them when they are released).

I recommend these for everyone, but I do think it’s important you understand the “why” of the shoes, their use cases, and how they react on some terrain.

top_reviews.title: Mostly Hype. You don't get what you pay for
top_reviews.text:
So I started into the Minimalist shoe world 5 years ago. But got serious about it 3 years ago. I was a Wing Chun Teacher and Feiyue were very popular in the Kung Fu crowd. So the shoes were something I would wear while training then switch to sketchers walking or running shoes at work or out and about.

3 years back I started with minimalist shoes full time after wearing them working out at home for a month to give my Brain time to get used to them. I started with Marrell because they partnered with Vibram and I of course tried a pair of the 5 fingers. Good shoes but quite expensive. And if they are your only every day all day shoe... Getting 3 months from a pair you spent $120 on is NUTS

Xero seemed cool but I worked for years in sales in small business with products built and shipped in from various countries. I hate to break it to Huge fans of Xero and the big companies... But WITHIN is one brand you can find here on Amazon (with a few smaller copies, but I like what the Within store puts out) that have similar designs for a lot less money.

This prio was $60 more shipped than my WITHIN sneakers (103.73 vs 43.67 to the door).... And I am sorry but they are not worth the extra $60. I would say an extra $30 at best. Yes the materials are slightly better. But... The Prio is trying to be a "look at me ask me about my shoes because they look different" shoe. In reality the upper feels like a store brand upper from a Walmart sneaker they just tweaked a little. There are patterns and extra materials that will age and fade in different ways so what already stands out like a house with weird color choices for it's exterior trim will look more off over time.

It's funny in attempts just to make a cheaper product the Within sneakers come off as better minimalist shoes. A simple stitched all one material upper and an unassuming sole. The Within just look like shoes and mostly I get no questions about them. Except from people who own all the popular brands like Xero wanting to know what mine are. The Within come in a Bag with no markings. The Prio come in a fancy box with full color manuals and a note from the owners like they are reinventing the shoe game.

top_reviews.title: Nice Look and Feel, but Not so Durable
top_reviews.text:
Perhaps it is because I have wide feet, or maybe because I bought them a half-size too big, these shoes lasted only about six months before they started developing cracks in the outer layer of material at the toes.

The initial quality is fine, and the laces never got frayed at the lengths where they pass through the top ring loops, but if you're looking for work shoes that can last you for a while, these aren't your best choice. They are inexpensive, and until the cracks form they look good, but once that outer shell of material by the toes begins to crack, it's game over. Not sure how I would repair them, and it's not worth the trouble in any case.

One thing I noticed is they have decent grip on ice in the winter - the walkway to my office is notorious for icing up fast in wet weather in the cold, and these let me walk with a good deal of confidence, even when carrying heavy objects and not able to see where I was stepping. A good deal, but don't expect them to last much longer than six to eight months.

Update: The above was a few months ago. For the past two weeks, I have been using these as house-shoes, to wear around the house yet still be able to go outside or something without having to look for your sneakers. They fit a bit loose, so they're easy to slip into, and they're very comfortable. Wouldn't mow the lawn in these, or go out for the night, but if I gotta go somewhere quick, I don't have to find my sneakers, I can just bounce.

top_reviews.title: Excellent trail shoe but the sole material wears out way too fast for the money
top_reviews.text:
This is maybe my 11th straight pair of Saucony running shoes and the third of the Peregrine generations I've purchased. I suppose because it's a trail shoe, the material used in the sole cleats/knobs is very soft and wears out super easily if you run with these on a treadmill, sidewalks or streets. For the price, that's just not acceptable. The same holds for the non GTX (non Gore-Tex) version as well. The previous Peregrines had a slightly different composition and bigger/thicker knobs on the soles so they wore out much slower.
Long story short, if you plan to use these only on unpaved trails, they're great and water resistant. If you are thinking about road running, while they're very comfortable (thus making you want to use them often) they're going to wear out really, really quickly.

top_reviews.title: Shoes are ok, but have not solved all my comfort issues
top_reviews.text:
I have walked about 35 miles so far in these shoes. I purchased them to replace a pair of New Balance MW840BK athletic walking shoes (4E). I bought a pair of 10.5 X-Wide and they are about the same width and size matches exactly. I have neuropathy in left foot and need a wide width and depth for custom orthotic. I have a night arch and custom orthotic fits fine. I actually can put the custom orthotic on top of the insole that comes with the shoe and there is still enough room for my toes to spread out (I do have relatively small feet though).
Pros- shoes fit well and have rigid sole which I also need for my neuropathy. Shoes arrived quickly and appear to be good quality (so far, only had them a week, but I walks 5 miles a day).
My custom orthotics fit exactly right in this shoe and the size matched the New Balance 10.5 exactly. I would have to think the 10.5 size is right on since the orthotic is made to fit that size exactly.
Cons- there is minimal cushioning on the bottom of the shoe. There are two inserts, but one of them is paper thin so basically nothing. I have had to try multiple other insoles to go under my orthotic to provide sufficient cushion for the ball of my foot to feel comfortable (I do have another issue with my gait where the ball of my foot hits hard so I need extra cushioning there). I bought a pair of generic foam insoles (1/4") that are OK and put them on top of my custom orthotic, but I'm still searching for something to provide more comfort for long walks.
The shoes were laced incorrectly so I had to re-lace them in order to tie them tightly.
The tongue and ankle cushioning for me could be better and softer.
The eyeholes for the laces seem to be missing a pair of holes toward the top and the shoes don't lace tightly to push my feet back into the heel area of the shoe without the laces feeling too tight.

I did find that if hair conditioner rinsed onto my slipper I needed to rinse it off fairly quickly because my feet begin to slip around inside the slipper. They don't collect water thanks to the holes and they dry fast, I store mine on the towel rack inside my shower. As the picture shows, there are little tiny nubs on the slipper that at first irritated my feet, I am sure they are part of the reason these stay on your feet. top_reviews.title: Extremely comfortable but also extremely smelly boot!
top_reviews.text:
I ordered these before going on a trip to Europe last November and wanted to be prepared for lots of rain if necessary. I ordered an 8.5, which is larger than my usual, but the shoe was too small so I ordered a 9. These boots were mostly perfect for the trip, where I walked/hiked 90 miles in them over two weeks, straight out of the box. They felt great on concrete and dirt, however don't expect a ton of traction in these if you're looking for a designated hiking boot. These are definitely more style oriented than true utility. Also, the green suede swiftly lost its luster, and 7 months later, the suede is very dull army green with lots of scuffs now. Also, the top of the boot itself is pretty open if you don't tie it real tight (which really restricts the ankle too much), so if you are stuck outside in a downpour, your foot will get wet. Regardless, if it wasn't for one huge issue, I would have rated these a 5 because I love the style and am crazy for suede in general.

HOWEVER, these are without doubt the most foul smelling shoe I have ever experienced in my life. The waterproofing must have worked too well because no heat or moisture could escape the boot AT ALL during the day, so when I get back to my hotel room after walking around for 12 hours, the smell was so pungent that I literally had to put the boots in the hotel freezer or string them outside the window because the smell was THAT offensive. I've never had other shoes that have smelled this disgusting, even in other work boots that I've sweated in a ton. Something in the inner material of the shoe coalesces so hideously with sweat, and catalyzes into unspeakable horror. I removed one boot for about two minutes on a plane to rearrange a sock, and the person in front of my audibly gagged.... My poor brother was disgusted the entire trip because he was stuck in the hotel rooms with me.

So, if you want a cute street boot for light walking (under 3 miles) in cold cities and don't have sweaty feet, this is the perfect shoe for you!! But if you want a waterproof boot for actual hiking for longer distances in non-cold regions, this is NOT the shoe for you, keep looking!! Your nose and friends will thank you.

You should not use one pair of work boots/shoes as you WILL develop discomfort and in extreme cases foot and back pain. Switch them out every 6 months. Most companies that require steel toe shoes even have truck shops show up and give you a credit of $100.

I work in the Heat Treat department of a steel company. I walk on the steel grates in my photos every day for 10 hours a day. I walk 7 miles a day on average. These shoes have not split, nor have they cracked yet. They are still comfortable, and they are pretty slip resistant.

top_reviews.title: The original, with a nice upgrade
top_reviews.text:
At the peak of Toms hype a decade ago, I picked up a few pairs when I worked for a retailer that sold them for free. I've been pretty sold on them—they're incredibly comfortable, look good any way you wear them, and are great around-the-house/yard/neighborhood slip-ons.

My one detraction is that the outsoles were really flimsy. Something organic like jute if I remember. I put a lot of miles on my shoes and they wouldn't last long, so I'd only buy them when I'd get them discounted from work.

I bought another pair recently for slipping on around the yard, and I'm pleased to see that while Toms has branched out to other styles, they still make the original, and to my excitement, finally upgraded the soles to a more hard-wearing synthetic material. They're still soft and flexible as I remember, but I think I'll get a lot more wear out of these. Oh, and the price is still great.

top_reviews.title: MIXED THOUGHTS...
top_reviews.text:
THE SHOES WERE RECOMMENDED TO ME BY MY FOOT SURGEON WHEN I WENT TO HIM WITH EXCRUCIATING PAIN IN MY FEET AND ANKLES. HE SAID I NEEDED ARCH SUPPORT EVERY TIME I GOT OUT OF BED AND IF I DIDN'T WANT TO TAKE THE TIME TO PUT ON SHOES, THESE WOULD BE A GREAT OPTION AS A SLIP-ON FOR THAT SUPPORT.
I LOVE HOW THEY LOOK AND THE FIT THAT THEY HAVE. THE VELCRO ON THE TOP IS ADJUSTABLE FOR COMFORT. THE COLOR I PICKED IS AS GOOD IN PERSON AS ADVERTISED. I HAVE CHOSEN NOT TO TAKE A PICTURE OF ME WEARING THEM SINCE MY TOES ARE SO WONKY (TRUST ME, IT WOULD BE A NEGATIVE VISUAL THAT ONE WOULD NOT GET OUT OF THEIR HEAD AFTER SEEING THEM!)
THEY ARE EASY TO CLEAN IF WORN OUTSIDE OR IF THEY SIMPLY GET DIRTY FROM BEING WORN AROUND THE HOUSE.

ALL THAT BEING SAID, I WANT TO MAKE PROSPECTIVE BUYERS AWARE OF SOMETHING THAT I LEARNED. INITIALLY, THEY WERE HARD TO BREAK IN. THEY FELT STIFF AND ALMOST LIKE WOODEN SHOES WHEN I WALKED IN THEM. BUT GRADUALLY THEY BEGAN TO SOFTEN UP SO I COULD ROLL MY FOOT WHEN WALKING.
AFTER A WHILE, I BEGAN TO HAVE INCREASING DISCOMFORT AND SHARP PAINS IN MY INNER ANKLES. WHEN I HAD A FOLLOW-UP VISIT WITH MY DOCTOR, HE STATED THAT SOMETIMES THE SUPPORTIVE ARCH IS A BIT TOO HIGH FOR PEOPLE WITH MY PROBLEMS. HE SUGGESTED THAT I WEAR THEM ONLY FOR BRIEF TIMES (LIKE MIDDLE-OF-THE NIGHT BATHROOM VISITS) AND USE MY OWN DISCRESSION FOR HOW LONG TO WEAR THEM IF I CHOOSE TO USE THEM FOR OTHER OCCASIONS.

I WOULD HIGHLY RECOMMEND THESE TO ANYONE WITH FLAT FEET. THE PROS LISTED ABOVE ARE REALLY NICE AND I DON'T REGRET PURCHASING THESE AT ALL. I WILL (AND ALREADY HAVE) FOLLOW MY DOCTOR'S SUGGESTIONS AND CONTINUE TO WEAR THEM SINCE THEY ARE SO STINKIN' CUTE. BUT I ALSO WANT TO MAKE OTHERS AWARE OF WHAT I LEARNED SO THAT THEY CAN MAKE AN INFORMED DECISION. HOPEFULLY MY REVIEW WILL HELP OTHERS IF THEY THINK THE SHOE IS CAUSING THEIR CONDITION(S) TO BE MORE COMPLICATED. MODERATION, MY FRIENDS. MODERATION!

top_reviews.title: Nice soft suede, very comfortable, toe box is roomy, fit is excellent, great value for the price.
top_reviews.text:
I was very tempted to spend $110 on UGGs Ascot that look very similar, and I usually go for quality, but for the money I thought I'd give these a try at $23 because after all they are house slippers. Glad I did, because they are very comfortable with soft suede exterior and the Chestnut color is very nice. Surprising for what I paid they feel like much better quality than I expected because after reading some other reviews, several spoke of poor quality. I don't see any defects in the stitching, the color on both shoes match perfectly and they arrived in perfect condition. The inside faux fur is soft, but it mats down considerably in a couple days. I'm not sure if the UGGs "genuine shearling linings" would do that so maybe if that's important to you then consider that. However with that said the initial very snug fix relaxes to a much better fit in a day yet they are not loose and do not come off on their own. I am happier with the fit now that they loosened up a bit. I wear an 8 1/2 shoe and ordered the 9 US size and they now fit perfectly with at least 1/4 inch spare toe room. If I were a 9 I might suggest ordering a size up to a 10 though. I like the rubber bottoms as they are very thin and flexible giving that comfy slipper feel, not like a hard sole shoe, but they are not slippery on wood floors like a soft suede sole can get. Other reviews commented on the soles being uncomfortable with not enough padding but I have not noticed a problem yet. There is no arch support but if that becomes an issue I can probably just add a gel insole. I have worn them briefly out in the snow to get mail and they did a great job keeping the bottom dry. Overall I am very happy with these and would recommend them. If they last at least a year I will be happy.

So to wrap up on my dilemma... go low cost or high end? I think maybe the Faux fur matting down so fast is where the "genuine shearling lining" in the UGGs might do better but these are house slippers, so if that's all there is, then not sure it is worth an extra $87. They keep my feet warm, don't make my feet sweaty and they are surprisingly comfortable if you are OK trading the soft flexible feel for no arch support. I figured I can buy 5 of these for the price of the high end ones and throw them away when they get worn out or smelly as you cannot wash suede. I cannot comment on durability in this review as I only had these a week or so. Hope you find this helpful.

Sure, I'm wearing them literally all day long cuz....COVID!!  WFH!!!  I go nowhere and I see nobody so I only wear slippers.  All day.  Every day.  Now, I'm sure that Dearfoam didn't plan on their products being worn 14-16 hours per day but in all fairness to me, it's not like I'm walking anywhere.  I'm sitting at my desk for a good chunk of it.  The rest of the time, they are on the floor next to me while I lounge on the couch.  Most workout they get is the daily traipse to the mail box to see if I got anything interesting.  I would expect that even with that, it should take longer than a month to get holes in the toes.  For $70, I'm less than impressed.

top_reviews.title: Cheaply made!
top_reviews.text: Wore these once. Pulled them on gently and the paper-thin suede ripped. Needless to say, they’re going back

top_reviews.title: Couldn't fit my foot into them and they shed like crazy!
top_reviews.text: Okay, I feel like I'm in an alternate reality here?! I was so excited for these slippers and even ordered a size up so I could wear with fuzzy socks, and I literally couldn't get my foot in them. I thought I had forgotten to take out some cardboard, but no—I couldn't pull them on. My sister tried and she couldn't get them on either? Also, clumps of the fur kept flying off/shedding while I tried. I've owned Uggs and Minnetonkas before and have never had shedding this badly. I'm SO confused how everyone had such a positive experience, but hey, needed to share?

top_reviews.title: Size up if you buy these at all...
top_reviews.text:
Buyer beware.

These run small. I’m a very average size 8, and the 8 on these pinched my toes so bad I had to exchange for a 9. My heel now floats a bit when I walk, but I’m not going to be climbing any mountains in these, so I’m willing to deal. Regardless, that was strike one.

There was a cosmetic blemish on the cuff, but since I was planning to wear them folded down, I figure I can deal with that too. However, that’s strike two.

Two days, t-w-o days, after wearing them lightly around the house, the stitching tore on the right boot. I’m beyond bummed. Strike three.

These do not have any support whatsoever, and the sole is glued in, so it’s not like you can exchange it for a sole with some fluff to it.

The suede is very thin and the over quality is on par with $15 slippers you’d find at target. Like, why didn’t I just get another pair from there?? Because I was hoping for quality, last me 5 years, grown up pair of slippers, that’s why. Alas, these aren’t them.

They are at best “ok” and look good on paper. However, in practice they are flimsy, sub par quality with an expensive price tag.

The one pro: they are in fact warm.

My advice: keep searching.

top_reviews.title: Yes, buy these
top_reviews.text:
These are amazingly soft and so comfortable. I wear a size 91/2 and I bought the 10’s and they fit nicely with socks or without, I prefer them without socks. I would say size up if you’re a half size. I won’t be taking these off unless absolutely necessary! They are worth every penny, and really keep your feet warm without sweating.
They’re mid priced slippers, which I had a hard time finding - all I could find were really cheap ones or super expensive ones. Glad I sifted through the myriad of slippers that Amazon has and found these.
I’m not sure why Amazon no longer allows me to post photos? But, they look exactly like their picture, so.....just buy them, you won’t be disappointed.

Update: I’ve worn these slippers now for 7 months -every single day and ALL day long . I’ve given them quite the workout - I mean I’ve spilled all sorts of stuff all over them, including bacon grease! So they look a little beat up, but they are still going strong ! I do think new wool insoles are in order.

Btw, in the meanwhile I purchased two pairs of Uggs - the Tasman and the Bailey Button 2 - both pairs went right back. They weren’t nearly as comfortable as these.

top_reviews.title: Great slippers
top_reviews.text: I have several pairs of wool slippers, but for some reason my feet have been cold for the last couple of weeks. All my slippers are from LLBean.  It has been cold in North Carolina and I have a lot of tile floors. I decided I needed to buy a  warmer slipper. These are great. I wear a size 6W and purchased these in a size 6. They fit good in the foot part, but are a little tight on the upper part of my foot. I can stretch them a little, but I will just see if this happens naturally. Leather does stretch with time. My feet are  toasty warm. I know these will stretch out as time goes on and I am glad that I went with my usual size. Some people said they went up a size.  My only complaint is the tag that is sewn inside on the heel. It is a little annoying. Can’t understand why they would do that. It is stitched in and there is really no way to take it out. The tag would be much better on the outside of the slipper. I am happy with my purchase. I would order again.

I will start by saying that I own an entire back of the door shoe rack of dance shoes. Most of them are now TT Dancewear shoes. I love them! I am slowly weeding out the other brands.

I have these practice shoes in nude and now the black. I needed shoes to practice in that did not have rhinestones All over them. I can get on the floor without discomfort or scratching the floor. I typically dance in 2.5 inch heels, so I wanted a practice shoe in the same height (Most practice shoes are a Cuban heel), so these shoes are perfect!

I love the fit. The size chart is great! Because I fall in between sizes I have contacted customer support for help with sizing. They are very prompt in replying and extremely helpful. description: Once you slip your foot into the Klondike from L.B. Evans, it may be hard to wear anything else. Its soft suede upper, faux fur lining, and cushioned insole are pure comfort. And with a sturdy, treaded sole, this slipper is as durable as it is cozy. In 1804, T. & A. Evans (Thomas and Amos) were running a small shoe business connected with a general store in the town of South Reading. There was no shoe factory as we know it today, just a small shop where Thomas and Amos cut the leather for their shoes. The actual shoe making was farmed out among the people of the town, while Thomas and Amos supplied them with uppers, soles, counters and heels to be assembled into shoes. All shoes were sewed by hand whenever the shoemaker-farmers could spare the time. Today L.B. Evans is owned and operated as a division of Daniel Green Enterprises. Many of the traditional gentleman's slipper styles are still part of the line, but the business has grown to include new updated classics, premium products including elk and deer, and an array or rugged, warm outdoor styles. Daniel Green Enterprises remains committed to the quality and comfort guarantee that the Evans brothers established over 200 years ago.

top_reviews.title: Size is bigger
top_reviews.text: I will edit my review if there are any changes, as I just received these today.. they are very comfortable, light weight, and appear to be well made. I did read some other reviews that mentioned the seems coming undone, if that happens then I will redo them myself with fishing string, as that is very durable for sewing. I’ve taken multiple photos to show the different angles and the flexibility of the Mocs. They are extremely flexible and I think they would be perfect for grounding/earthing, as they are completely cow hide, except for the inside bottom, which can be removed if you needed to. I highly recommend that you read all of the description and maintenance, and use the products that are mentioned to keep them protected from the elements. These are fine for wearing indoors and outdoors, as long as you seal them with the correct products they mention. I wear a size 7 1/2 in regular shoes, but after reading the other reviews I decided to get a size 7 in these, as they are looser than a regular shoe, and they do stretch over time. So you want them to fit like a glove; very snug at first until you break them in. I will be returning these for a size 6, I believe. had I known they were going to be as loose as they are, that is probably what I should have purchased to begin with. As a Native American myself, who has “the walk” (almost a bounce to my walk, somewhat on my toes), I feel that is very important to have the correct size, since the area around the opening is much looser than they should be. Definitely measure both feet, and purchase the length of your smaller foot. Normally with regular shoes, you would get the size of the bigger foot; but with the way these are made, that is definitely not the case. You may feel some slight rubbing on your toes at first, but as stated, they will loosen up as you break them in; so wear them indoors and outdoors at first, to get a lot of use out off them and they will break in faster. These are very light weight, which I love because it’s a lot like being barefoot. If this review was helpful, please click the helpful button :)

top_reviews.title: TRULY THE BEST EVER
top_reviews.text: I have wanted a pair of moccasins since I was a young girl in the late sixties and early seventies. At long last I finally have a pair and I absolutely love them! I could have gotten them cheaper from another company but I am a firm believer in the Minnetonka brand and I wouldn't have anything else. Check their website for instructions on how to 'set' your shoes before you start wearing them. Unfortunately, you can't just take them out of the box and start wearing them or you will ruin them quickly. You will need to wear them around the yard first for a few weeks, in dry grass before you start walking on concrete or gravel. There's a little more to the preparation process than that, but please, do yourself a favor. If you're going to purchase the good stuff, which in my opinion is Minnetonka, then take the time to go to their website and print out the instructions for how to "break in" your moccasins before you start wearing them out in public. Be sure to read about getting them wet, which is not a good thing. They also have an excellent tip on how to keep the shoe strings tied permanently so that you don't have to keep tying them over and over. So if you want the true moccasin experience, buy Minnetonka brand and follow the instructions on their website to a "T" and you will get years and years of enjoyment and wear from that single pair of moccasins. Oh...and buy them a half size smaller than your 'normal' size. They will stretch quickly enough & before you know it, you'll be walking around in floppy, poorly fitting moc's if you buy your regular size. I wear gel inserts in mine due to knee and back problems. But if I'm just going to be walking for a short period of time, I skip the inserts & go for the pure 'barefoot feeling' of a great pair of mocassins. 😀

I have widish feet, at least more wide than narrow. Though regular width is usually fine. These Mocs are very narrow. They do stretch, and knowing that, I stuck with them. I wore no socks, then socks as they loosened up a bit. The sizing is still just a bit off compared to every other shoe of this size I’ve ever tried on. Toe needs to be less pointy, and needs a little more width.

Tan color is good. I have had the darker ones in the past but the stain would come off on my feet if they got a little damp.

Laces. The leather straps don’t stay tight and came untied all the time. There was a weak spot in one and upon tightening it one day, it finally broke. So I got 36” tan cord laces. They about 4” too long, and were very hard to get in. But work so much better than the leather. To get them in I taped to existing leather lace and slowly pulled. That worked on one side but the other side I ended up taping the new lace to a small crochet needle and pulling it through.

Now that they loosened up and laces are better, I wear them every day, all day. Still wish for a bit more on the width, but a great house slipper, especially in warmer weather when you don’t want all the fuzzy inside that most slippers have.

top_reviews.title: Libero Loves These

I would suggest going up a size higher for people with wider feet like myself.

top_reviews.text: I have very lame feet from injuries and surgeries (scar tissue - ruptured fascia/now flat feet). I am constantly looking for shoes that I can wear that make my feet feel better. I bought these while traveling because I just wanted some good “airport” shoes and the price point was attractive (shoes for bad feet can cost over 100 dollars, generally). Well, imagine my surprise at how doggone comfortable these were - I wore them all day and into the evening the day they arrived at my location. I then wore them the rest of my trip. They are so comfortable! If I had one negative, I would say that I tend to slide forward in them so after many hours of wear, my toe was sensitive to the front of the shoe - but for the price and comfort, these are great. I am buying another pair :)

top_reviews.title: Super cute very well made waterproof but NOT comfortable for walking all day for me
top_reviews.text:
I really wanted to love these shoes because they are so cute. While they are not bad for how high the heel appears, they are definitely not my go-to comfortable walking shoes. I walk about a 1.5 miles every day to and from work and was hoping these would be fine for the journey based on reviews for sorel shoes. Not so. They're fine if you are not walking too long. But they do have the walking on tiptoe feel you get with heels after about 20 minutes in them. They feel is also somehwat hard on the heel and really hurt my feet after a while.

Pros - they are very warm, supppeeeerr cut, waterproof and true to size. I also wore them in super snowy conditions and my feet were well protected and the traction was great. I will keep them for shorter days.

top_reviews.title: Very unlike any Sorel's I have ever owned. VERY Stiff
top_reviews.text:
These are obviously stylish cute and all of that. Easy zipper is fantastic for quick off and on, I love the extra lift that is given with this shoe compared to some others that I have purchased.
I have owned probably 12 or so pairs or Sorel shoes these by far are my least favorite. They do not seem to break in at all. They are extremely stiff and seem to stay that way.
Style and overall appearance I easily give a 10
comfort is a 7 because sure we can tolerate a lot on our feet, but Sorel is known for making cute comfortable shoes that you can work/stand/walk in all day. These are not them.
I have had them over a month and I have been waiting to post a review to see if maybe they would be broken in already- not the case. :(

top_reviews.title: Gorgeous, comfortable!
top_reviews.text:
Sorel has amazing fit, comfort, and quality.

Snow, rain, cold, or heat these boots look great and perform well.

They fit true to size. I went up a half-size because I wear thicker socks with boots.

No break-in required: wore them nearly 10 hours the first time and my feet were not sore, no blisters, no red marks on my feet.

Yes, they are expensive but protecting your feet while looking great makes it worth every penny!

top_reviews.title: Break Them In
top_reviews.text: The first time I wore these my feet were stiff and sore. Now that I've worn them about 5 times for extended periods, I've broken them in and managed about 6,000 steps (don't judge me) with very little discomfort. I'm up and down all day. I have plantars fasciitis by the way. They are super cute, great in rain, and grip well. Have not tried in ice/snow and wouldn't personally push that.

top_reviews.title: Dispointted
top_reviews.text:
I've worn this shoe style for quite a few years and have always been very happy with the shoe. Not so much this time. I bought them to wear on a trip that was going to last about a month. I noticed that after only two weeks of wear (and not daily either) the sides of the shoe actually started breaking down and caving in. I was amazed.

I don't know what is wrong with this shoe as when I came home I pulled an exact pair out of my closet that's 3 years old and they still fit my foot perfectly. I should have taken an old pair on my trip as I would have been better off and far more comfortable.

If I buy this shoe again, it lwill be locally so I can return the shoes if the same thing happens. Shoes shouldn't break down after only a few weeks.

top_reviews.title: Not Slip Resistant
top_reviews.text: I bought these shoes for a job in the restaurant business. They are NOT slip resistant; if anything, I have slipped more wearing these than any other shoes. They also run a bit small. If I would have to buy them again, I would go .5 size higher as they're narrow.

top_reviews.title: Made in the USA
top_reviews.text: My wife has a hard time finding shoes that fit her as she has very narrow feet. I have been unable to find any shoes made overseas(China) that fit and are comfortable. These shoes made in the USA, fit great and are very comfortable. I just hope that they will always be available. I always buy a couple of pair at a time, just in case they become unavailable.

top_reviews.title: Not the same shoe as they used to be.
top_reviews.text: Not sure exactly what happened to these Easy Spirit shoes. This style used to be a nice soft comfortable leather.  This pair is stiff and uncomfortable. They are now made in China. I don't know if that makes a difference to the quality of the leather, but I ma extremely disappointed in this purchase. I would send them back if I had not already worn them, but I was hoping to "break them in" that will not happen, I can tell.

top_reviews.title: Horrendous heel slip
top_reviews.text: I purchased these shoes because they came wide, and I have a wide forefoot and bunions. Unfortunately, the heels on these shoes are as wide as the front of the shoe, and I could not lace them up enough to keep the heels from slipping. I have never seen such a wide heel on any shoe. Why do shoe makers assume your entire foot is wide? These shoes might work for someone with swollen feet or a very wide foot all over, but they did not fit me at all in the heel. They are not as clunky as many wide shoes, and the leather was soft. I am returning the shoes, and continuing my quest for a wide, decent-looking shoe with a normal heel width.

top_reviews.title: Very disappointed.
top_reviews.text: This is usually my favorite style of Easy Spirit. It's supposed to be super light and comfortable, but the one I received is oversized, stiff, bulky and uncomfortable. It's more like an orthopedic shoe than a light walking shoe. Unfortunately, I wore them outside the first day and couldn't return them. I bought another of the same model from another vendor on ebay, and it is exactly like I remembered, so this one is either mislabeled or not manufactured the same.

top_reviews.title: Poor Quality
top_reviews.text: I have worn this style Easy Spirit shoe for years.  The last 2 pairs are not usable as they pinch my toes and cause numb feet.  I don't know if it is the toxins in the preparation of the leather or if they are just shorter and more narrow than usual that is causing me  foot pain.  I am now using a pair that I have worn for years.

top_reviews.title: Heel has changed
top_reviews.text: I have worn this brand and style of shoe for over 20 years now. Originally you could order size and width and heel width for a really wonderful fit. Now you can't order the heel width at all. Because of feet issues I now need a WW shoe but an N heel width. Can't get it. So the shoe slips up and down off my heel with every step.  I don't have a WW heel but that's what you get now with these shoes. Also there used to be some arch support but not any more which is okay for me as I use professional orthotics.  I do like that the sole isn't real thick and heavy.

top_reviews.title: the best sneaker/shoe
top_reviews.text: I've been wearing the ap1 easy spirit shoe for years, over 20. I am over 55 and am very flat footed and have trouble finding a pair of shoes/boots that I can wear for long periods of time. I would recommend these!

Just too wide at the top for most applications except boot cut jeans  or a skinny/legging tucked -  but it's a big gap depending on your ankle size. Also if you are considering the chocolate, it's a deeper chocolate than pictured. The leather for both the black and chocolate is very flat/no sheen and I believe they'd show scuff marks easily as a result.  At $179 I'm going to keep looking. Footbed/arch felt good though...darn.

At first, I did not like the wide width of the boots  around my ankles.  Most women will probably opt not to wear this boot with a skirt; the proportions are awkward, especially if you have thin ankles. This boot looks great with boot cut jeans or narrow leg pants. The long tassels are the zipper pulls and are a fun element that draws attention to your feet when walking. The upper of the shoe is all leather. The inside of the shoe is buttery soft and feels very comfortable against the foot.  I walk around in these boots all day with no foot or back issues.  The heel is pretty high, but very sturdy and comfortable when walking.  I love them!  I bought them in the black and chocolate brown, which is really dark.  For some reason the black pair were reduced to $45.00 at the beginning of the new year, so I bought another pair as backup.  As of now, the boots are $71.00 for a size 11. top_reviews.title: Buy these asap!
top_reviews.text: I am writing this review five months after purchase. We are having a wintery winter, and these oboz sawtooth waterproof are warm and dry when I walk in snowy streets. I am in love with oboz....I bought a pair of low oboz sawtooth last spring...I have a foot tendon injury and I need to wear sneakers carefully, not roll my foot (it has slowly healed from an injury)....after it is fully healed and I have no pain, I will STILL wear my oboz low, in the summer, and the high ones for warmth and waterproof in the winter. They cushion, they support, they have great traction. They aren't as heavy as they may look. I liked Merrill and Keen okay...but Oboz is my brand.

top_reviews.title: Comfy but falling apart
top_reviews.text: I love the fit and feel of my Oboz but they are falling apart way too quickly. The boots pictured are 2 months old with less than 150 miles of hiking on them. The rubber toe caps peeled off both shoes in the first month.  The boots look much older than they are, and seriously beaten up. I contacted the vender; their response was that they do not warranty "wear & tear".  Do not buy these boots! They do not stand up and the vender does not stand behind the product. By comparison, my previous hiking boots lasted 3 seasons and over 1000 miles before they fell apart.

top_reviews.title: Many good qualities
top_reviews.text: I did not buy this shoe (10.5 Women's Wide) from Amazon, but another dealer.  Since I have significant problem feet - plantar fasciitis, posterior tibial tendonitis with fallen arch, Morton's Neuroma, Hallux Valgus & Tayor's bunions, and arthritis in the ankle, toes and spine- it's been a struggle to find the 'perfect' shoe / boot.  I've been the route of New Balance, Merrell's, Lowa's, Keen's and thought I'd try the Oboz Sawtooth II Mid Waterproof Boots - Wide.  The most comfortable shoes / boots for me up to this point has been the Keen Targhee III Men's 8.5 Wide.  The Keen shock absorption for my spinal issues has been superb coupled with Aetrex Memory Foam orthotics with Metatarsal Support.  But the Keen Targhee III 8.5 Men's wide had begun to bother my Taylor bunions and I always noticed some discomfort with my posterior tibial tendonitis especially while wearing the low version.  In my opinion the Oboz Sawtooth II offers excellent arch support and is a benefit to my fallen arch, posterior tibial tendonitis, and the women's 10.5 wide actually feels wider than the Keen's 8.5 men's wide so my bunions are happier.  However; the shock absorption although good isn't nearly as good as in the Keen Targhee III so my spine isn't as happy and my foot fatigues more quickly in regards to the plantar fasciitis.  If I could blend the shock absorption of the Keen's Targhee III with the Oboz Sawtooth II arch and general support, heel stabilization and width, I'd have my perfect shoe / boot.  FYI:  I'm keeping the Oboz Sawtooth II since at this point although my spine isn't the happiest it makes my ankle and bunions happier.  I'll just switch off between the Keen's and Oboz until I find a shoe / boot that accommodates both issues.

top_reviews.title: Disappointing for an expensive boot
top_reviews.text:
I really wanted to love these. A friend has a pair and raves about them. She's significantly taller than I am, so perhaps it's a height issue? My short legs hated these. I bought them from Rei, but the ad blockers wouldn't allow me to leave a review there.

Comfort - 5 stars
I tried on about 5-6 pairs of boots. These were the only ones that fit out of the box. NOTE: I have wide feet, and even had these stretched. I bought them a size bigger to allow for thick winter socks.

Tred: 1 star
These are probably great in a dry climate, but not a wet one like New York. A friend of mine was wearing Canadian kodiaks; she effortlessly clambered over wet rocks while I slid on my rear end. It got so dangerous we switched trails. This wasn't a demanding hike by any stretch of the imagination, but these boots made it feel unsafe.

Gait - 1 star
One reviewer described them as "Wearing 2 bricks on your feet" and I would agree with that. I felt exhausted after what can only be described as a casual stroll in the woods. I wasn't even carrying anything. I asked my hiking buddy if we could turn back. When I got home, I realized my hips were killing me. It happened the next time as well during a city walk. This didn't happen in my sneakers or old pair of Keens (which these replaced) so these are definitely the cause.

Very disappointed in a very expensive boot. Don't believe the hype.

top_reviews.title: Springy/spongy midsoles, two-tone camo design on PU leather
top_reviews.text:
These are somewhat warmer than my open sandals, which only have three straps counting the heel straps. These cover the top of the foot and have more cover on the sides too, plus the covered toes.

The light gray midsoles are soft, springy, even spongy feeling. It's comfortable, like some sneakers I've tried, but may not wear well, as soft foam tends to compress or wear away.

The outsoles are very grippy, no slipping in these. The tread rubber is moderately hard, so they've got some wear in them.

I usually wear 9.5/10, but I ordered size 12 so I could wear extra socks with these in cold weather. With two thick pairs of winter socks and one regular pair under those, which is what I like during winter, these fit snugly. Because of the toe caps, and maybe the style, they're 5/8" longer than my size-12 open-toed sandals.

They have a two-tone decoration, flat gray on shiny black, on the faux leather (see attached photo). It looks fine close up or in strong light, but in some light it gives these a dusty or worn look.

The sizing is a perfect fit. What he likes the most is the insole comfort and the protective cover over the toes. His little piggies 🐖 are protected from the elements.

These are ideal for any type of outdoor adventure. From land to sea, boating, hiking or trecking.

Since then the sandals have been broken in and my ankles have toughened up a good bit. Now I can wear them all day and be extremely comfortable! top_reviews.title: These are nice hiking sandals

What was most impressive to me is the bungee closure.  No adjusting of the straps, just pull it tight and tighten with the bungee closure.  I found that walking around in these sandals was also comfortable.  I wore them with socks on and without socks.  The sandals feel cushioned and comfortable to walk in. top_reviews.title: The comfort of a slide with the support of a tennis shoe
top_reviews.text:
These are very comfortable even without my typical arch supports (I have flat feet). They wrap my feet well around the ankle so that my feet aren't sliding; without cutting into the skin. The sturdy sole provides great grip and traction on wet and slippery surfaces (rocks, leaves, mud, etc) and combined with the closed toe make these ideal for hiking in the woods. I wish the heel were all black, as I could have perhaps gotten away with wearing these with more casual/dressier outfits. The grey accent just reduces them to a sportier look. Not a huge deal, as I will definitely get my wear in; just an observation and "wish".

As aforementioned, they don't feel tight around the ankle; and there's plenty of room for my toes to spread out and wiggle. top_reviews.title: Extremely functional for the price and look great too!
top_reviews.text:
I was worried about whether these shoes would do the trick. They were fairly cheap ($25 ish) and looked cool, so I was worried they might be "form over function".

I purchased them anyway for a river rafting trip down the Colorado River through the Grand Canyon and I was wrong - they were absolutely perfect!

Unlike many water shoes/river shoes, they look cool. But they work really well too - there are holes in the bottom that water drains out through. The soles are some kind of rubber and have some traction so these were great for short hikes on trails and through vegetation or on rocks - my feet were completely protected. But I could also walk through streams and have the water drain instantly. They dried out quickly too whenever we were in the sun for a bit.

In some shoes I am a 10.5 and in some shoes I am a 10. I ordered a 10.5. It felt just the slightest bit loose (since I didn't wear with socks), but that wasn't a problem because the piping you see at the top of the foot hole is actually elastic and holds the shoe on. I think a 10 could have even been too small. These were super comfortable and never felt like they were falling off.

My brother wore serious hiking shoes and he was able to climb some rock faces that I wouldn't attempt in these. But for hiking, I was more than comfortable. And my feet dried quickly due to the draining ability of these shoes.

For $25, these are practically disposable and did the trick for the trip, functioning WAY better than I expected (I'd have paid more). I'd order whatever size you usually are, and if you are often between two half sizes, choose the large one because the elastic properties of the shoe will allow them to mold to your feet and stay secured.

top_reviews.title: Great shoes with 1 MAJOR problem...
top_reviews.text:
I bought these shoes for my trip to Zion National Park, particularly for the Narrows hiking trail since I will be in the river for pretty much the entire day. These shoes are very light weight and provides very good support for a flat-footed guy like me. Grip was pretty good underwater as I was able to maintain my balance most of the time other than when I kick the invisible rocks underwater.

However, these shoes have 1 major problem, but it was resolved pretty easily by a couple simple modifications. The stitching at the bottom of the tongue, where the colored stripe runs across the middle of the shoes, is EXTREMELY thick. 4 layers of material thick!! When wearing the shoes barefooted, the stitching does not really pose a problem. But once you wear socks, your feet will be pushed into that stitching which would first feel like a minor discomfort but quickly turn into major feet pain. Since I was short on time and really needed water shoes, I decided to just keep them. By removing the insole, my feet were not pushed into the stitching as much, but still was. The 3 elastic bands aren't tight enough to keep the shoes on my feet while in water so I added some laces to it. The added bonus of putting laces on was it relieved the pressure on the stitching completely, such that I was comfortably wearing these shoes for an entire day of hiking.

I think these shoes would be great if not for that stitching problem. If I had to repurchase water shoes, I would have gone for the other Aleader water shoes that does not have a tongue nor the stripe that runs across the middle.

top_reviews.title: Perfect Water Aerobics Footwear
top_reviews.text: I'm a senior citizen and just started a group aerobics pool class at a local gymnasium.  Some of the hour-long drills can get pretty intense, especially when foot grip is needed for speed and agility, not to mention the beating raw feet will take from a standard pool surface.  Outside of swimming fins, I never heard of footgear for the pool.  Style meant little, so that was just a bonus.  Finding a men's size 13 was a challenge.  The soles are thick enough for comfort but light enough to maneuver under water.  The tread of the soles are grooved and vented to allow safe and comfortable non-slip movement.  The entire shoe is ventilated so water does not collect in it.  They're easy to slip on with the elastic laces on top and yet stay comfortably and securely attached to your feet throughout vigorous underwater exercise.  They include ventilated footpads which tend to come out when you take them off, but are easy to reinsert.  It seems I hit it lucky with my first purchase of this type of footwear.  Finding them took a dedicated online search to keep looking until I felt I found the product to meet my needs.  Now having used them, I am not disappointed.  And they dry out quickly too.  This product met or exceeded all of my expectations and at a very fair price.

top_reviews.title: GREAT SHOES!  OUTSTANDING MERCHANT!!!
top_reviews.text:
My husband and I are rafting the Colorado River through Grand Canyon in August. Because of the excellent review by most people about these shoes we purchased a pair for each of us. After we received the shoes, they were so comfortable and fit so well, that we ordered another pair. The post office "lost" our package and in typical post office mumbo-jumbo excuses, I was desperate because our trip was only five days away. I sent the seller an email hoping that they might contact the post office to see if they could get a better response. Instead, fifteen minutes after I wrote the email, the seller contacted me and told me that she had mailed identical shoes that we ordered and we should receive them on Wednesday. When I told her I probably would not be home when our first order arrived at our residence, she acted very unconcerned for her merchandise but expressed great concern for our trip. "Send them back when you get home or if you get the chance just refuse the shoes when they are delivered."

These shoes are great! I wear a size 8-1/2womens and the Men's 7 fits me perfectly. My husband wears a 9-1/2 Mens and the Men's 9 fits him to a tee. We both have slender feet but because the shoes have so much "stretch" to them they fit great...like a good pair of gloves for the feet! We are in our 70's and think the soles will be much better than the Teva sandals that we normally wear in the river. Perfect river shoes!!

top_reviews.title: Worked Great!
