top_reviews.title: Promate Beach Dogs
top_reviews.text:
I wanted a pair of simple black hightop surf sloes and these Promate delivered just that. Some low profile shoes collect too much sand inside, hightops work best when you're humping your gear across deep, fine dry sand. This model had a snug neck which kept the inside from filling with fine sand. The styling was understated but not cheap looking. In the water they struck the right balance between weight and protection. I suppose the thickness of your ankles matters the most here - mine are thicker than average.

They're not so good for long walks on wet sand and poor on hard surfaces like boardwalks or pavement. The soles have no arch support and are thin and soft. They're built well for water and dry sand. Small rocks, shells, pine cones and the like will be a challenge. They do look good though.

top_reviews.title: I Want to Wear Them All Day!
top_reviews.text:
After many years of buying cheap Wal-Mart water shoes, and having to endure discomfort and constant slipping off in the water, I decided to bite the bullet and get something decent. Wow - what a difference! After reading the many good reviews on this shoe, and the oft mentioned caution to go one size smaller than usual, with some trepidation, I ordered a size 7. When I unpacked them, I thought, I'll never get these on, and at first, they did feel very tight - but after getting them wet, and spending a day in the water, I didn't even know I had them on! They are wonderfully comfortable, and I have to remember to take them off now.

Great shoes.

top_reviews.title: Perfect!
top_reviews.text:
I wear a women's 7 1/2 - 8 depending on the manufacturer. I like my watershoes to fit snugly but not tight and the needs to be flexible and not too rigid. After reading the posted reviews, these sounded like they could work for me and to order a 1/2 size smaller that they run slightly large.
I ordered women's 7/mens 6 and hoped for the best. Usually unisex mesns "too wide".
Received the shoes, tried them on... Perfect!!! Nice and snug but not tight, my toes just reach the end of the shoe but not bunched up.
Definitely recommend!

top_reviews.title: First impressions
top_reviews.text: I normally wear a men's size 9 1/2, but even after reading all of the reviews, I wasn't sure about what size to get, so I contacted the Get Wet Store. They answered quickly and recommended a size 9, which fits perfectly.  They seem to be just the thing for snorkeling and water sports.  The only thing that I noticed is that as soon as I put them on, my feet got hot, so I would not wear them out of the water on a warm day.  I am glad that I got them and didn't have to pay $30 or more like the other water shoes that I saw.  I will update my review after I have put them to the test, but they look like a winner.

top_reviews.title: Highly Recommend
top_reviews.text: I was leery about sizing on these and heeded the reviews of others; so, I offer this in addition for those seeking to buy.  I ordered a size "men 10/women 11" even though I wear size 11.5 sneakers.  I normally wear the heavy duty white socks found at Costco stores so that bumps up the size of sneaker.  Base on other reviews I selected a size 10 and it fits perfect.  My measured foot is 10 3/8" heel to big toe and 4.5" width through the ball of the foot.  I simply stood on a metal tape measure to find these measurements.  I also have a high arch and was worried about getting the Beach Dog on; no problem. I put them on and walked across my backyard which is 3/4" aggregate (broken rocks) and determined that the sole was thick enough to protect my feet; I weigh 260lbs.  I ordered one day and received the item the next day.  I live in San Diego and they came from north central Los Angeles; Rosemead, Ca; to be specific.  Highly recommend!

top_reviews.title: Awesome Water Shoe!

top_reviews.title: Quality boot at fair price
top_reviews.text:
These boots are well-made; the quality of the materials (even the laces) is excellent, and they are very comfortable.
I have marked them "fit as expected" -they actually run about half size larger than my usual size, but their website clearly states this, so I ordered accordingly, and got what I expected. While we're talking about expectations, I like them because I don't need a big clumsy work boot, but do want something a little more robust than a dress boot; they fill this gap perfectly, just don't expect something you can chop down a forest or spend a year on an oil rig in. Right out of the box they felt a little tight across the toe box, and I considered exchanging them for a Wide but the leather is so supple I thought they would adapt to my feet, and within a couple days they had relaxed and were super comfortable. The price point is fair; they cost more than the run-of the-mill cheapo "work boot"-looking imports which will fall apart in 6 months, and you'll still save some bucks over the industry icons (some of which have been hit with QC issues lately). I know $200 is not a lot of money to some people these days but, in the age of the disposable, if I'm laying down that kind of cash, I want a product that says somebody cared about the design, materials and construction.These boots shout that.

.

top_reviews.title: Got many compliments, however, they are not perfect
top_reviews.text:
Got a pair in Brown over a month ago. I really like them and I get compliments on them more often than with any other shoes I have owned before, even random people on the street. However, they are not perfect. Honest thoughts:
-The look: great, a bit dressier than your regular captoe. Clean lines, and sharp. I think that is what make people like them and offer compliments on them. From a random lady in the elevator the other day: "I wasn't gonna say anything, but man, those are some really nice looking boots". Conversation starter right there.
-The fit: I usually wear 9.5 in sneakers and ordered a pair in size 9, following the company's advice. They fit well lengthwise, but the right boot feels narrower than the left, making the it a bit uncomfortable. I am hoping this will go away once the boot breaks in. No space for extra insoles in this case, if you want extra insoles, or thicker insoles, order your regular size.
-The confort: they are rather stiff. Again, I am hoping this goes away once the boot break in. Other people say they feel like sneakers, but I don't think they feel remotely like that, at least not yet.
-The weight: they are heavy. Get ready for a different sensation when you wear them, if you are coming from lightweight shoes.
-The color: it looks more like burgundy in some lights, which is great, I think that gives the boots some character. If they scratch, that will reveal the underlying color, which I believe is the natural leather color, so it will contrast.
-Some people complaint about creases, but my pair is doing ok for now. I don't have shoes trees, but I do avoid stepping on them.
-The laces: they are stiff, I may change them at some point.

Value for Money: These are priced a little too high for me, I spent $350+ on a pair of red wings that lasted several years of daily use. The $200 for a pair of Thursdays that only last a year or so isn't worth the money. These are $100 boots at best.

Will not be purchasing a third pair.

My feet are closer to 4E than 5E, but the extra room in the boot allows me to wear thick socks so I can keep my feet warm. They could use just a little more room in the toe box, but there is enough to keep my toes from crowding and rubbing together. My feet are almost flat, so the low arch in these boots provide enough support to keep my feet from hurting after being on them all day. If you have a high arch that needs lots of support, you're probably going to need arch support inserts with these boots. One word of caution - these are hiking boots and have a pretty aggressive tread on the bottom that mud (and other sticky stuff) will cling to. top_reviews.text:
I bought this shoe because my smart watch (also my leg pain & shoe sole wear pattern) made me aware that I was beginning to pronate a lot on one foot while I ran, making my stride asymmetric. This caused some mild tendonitis, and I made the decision to pull the trigger on these shoes. Let me be clear...

THESE SHOES ARE INTENSE

There is a hard piece of TPC plastic for medial arch support and it WILL feel uncomfortable at first on the foot/feet that have issues. This plastic support is intense. It drives right into your arch and doesn't budge. I was genuinely concerned that my ankle would sprain while I ran, but I trusted the shoes and it felt like learning proper stride all over again. Within 2 weeks my stride is back to being perfectly symmetrical, my pronation is gone, and the shoes feel 100% comfortable. Trust me when I say this, the shoes being uncomfortable is probably a sign that you need them lol.

I have tried a couple different shoes and some inserts to no avail..until I found the guide 14. When I first put them on I did not feel the support I was use too, normally in the arch but as soon as I started walking I felt the support more in the ankle area. I could tell this was the best shoe I have bought in a long time after only 2 or 3 of my daily walks...my knees feel much better, no pain! Thank you so much!

top_reviews.title: Much Improved
top_reviews.text:
I have worn Saucony shoes for twenty years, but the Guide 13's I bought in 2021 were a disappointment. They were fine except that they started to tear at the collar after a few runs and they really looked crappy. But I decided to give the Guide 14's a chance, and these have been great. I've got over 200 miles on each of the two pairs I own, and they're holding up just fine. I think they do provide some extra support without feeling stiff. Very comfortable shoes and they don't feel clunky at all.

I read the review talking about resisting the temptation to replace the laces. Before the I received these shoes, I wondered what they were talking about. I must have missed the memo about these new stretchy laces. I'd never had anything like them before, and I wondered what was up the first time I tied these laces up. But I really like the laces. No need to double knot them when you tie your shoes, and they never come untied. Pretty neat.

Once again, I ordered a half-size larger than I would with any other brand of shoe. For whatever reason, Saucony shoes seem to run a bit small. But going with a half-size larger seems to work for me.

top_reviews.title: Firmest Guide since the Guide ISO
top_reviews.text:
These are a great looking version of Saucony’s Guide series, with a simpler, cleaner look and thick, spongy laces that AREN’T TOO LONG (Guide Iso), and don’t easily come untied on their own.

But they are also the firmest footbed of any Guide since the Guide Iso. Significantly firmer than the Guide 13, Guide 10, and Guide 8.

If you’re coming directly from the 13 like I was, you’ll notice the difference right away, and it takes some getting used to. It was so firm at first that I seriously thought about returning them, then looked online into whether or not I should try breaking them in, and if the ride would soften over time.

Thankfully, it has, and they’re proving to be a good running shoe. The uppers are very lightweight and so breathable that they remind me of Nike Huarache type uppers. The upper is soft and comfy, though, and needed no breaking in, while providing excellent ventilation and good space in the toe box.

The heel counter on this one is pronounced and so soft and almost squishy that it’s easy to crush down if you don’t hold onto it while inserting your foot. I prefer a bit more stiffness back at the heel, but I can’t argue with the comfort and softness. We’ll see if it holds up over time.

I’ve been very happy with Saucony’s Guide line of shoes over the years, and the fact that they’re available in different widths as well as sizing. They’ve always been a quality shoe for running thats worth the money.

top_reviews.title: great for flat feet!

Comfortable on the first run right out of the box. The heel lock is slimmer than the 13, which I like. I found the 13’s heel to be unnecessarily bulky. This model (14) is still good but…
(1) the biggest difference is the back of the heel. It has noticeably changed where it feels much more open and doesn’t secure the back of the foot as well. Thus, not as supportive.
(2) They changed the laces from flat to round. It may be cosmetic, but my experience is flat will cinch easier and stay tied better. Plus these round laces look like something on my 9 year olds shoes.
(3) Seems like there’s more “space” across the mid foot which feels looser for my narrowish foot. This may be a good thing for normal feet.

Overall, its good. The heel has changed this shoe from being a “do everything” shoe for heavy joggers like me to something less supportive on longer 7+ miles.

top_reviews.title: Great Motion Control Shoe!
top_reviews.text: This review is for the ISO Redeemer, not the ISO Redeemer 2.  I was looking for an alternative the the Brooks Beast that I wore for many years and landed here.  The last couple of iterations of that shoe just did not work as well for me as the previous versions.  The first thing I noticed is that due to the wider toe box of the ISO redeemer, I was able to go back to my true shoe size, rather than going up a half size as I recently had done with the other brand.  For me these required less effort for toe-off during that phase of the gait cycle, which was beneficial.  The support is good, but they seemed to be a little more flexible, which I grew to like. The cushioning is very good. They are orthotics-friendly. The sole rubber compound seems a little softer and may wear a little quicker.  They sometimes squeak when walking on a polished floor.  Overall I'm pleased with the shoe and have stocked up.  It has been replaced by the ISO Redeemer 2.  Some reviews of it appear to not be quite as favorable as this original Redeemer.

top_reviews.title: True Stability Show for Plantar injury
top_reviews.text: Full disclosure: I am a physician.  I suffered a severe foot injury to the plantar muscles (bottom) of my feet.  I've scoured footlocker and the internet for shoes that prevent plantar flexion (toe down) to relieve pain.  This shoe is  truly as close to a therapeutic shoe that you can get.  Let's be clear:  It is RIGID as a piece of granite.  Please consult your physician BUT this shoe would work for anyone suffering from foot pain or plantar fascitis.  It's comfortable but you really can't flex the foot.  That's the key to this shoe for therapy.  I have no advice for runners.  This post is to help people suffering from foot pain.  It's better than the BEAST.  Again, talk to your physician or therapist before buying.

top_reviews.text:
I've been training for my next marathon for the last 2 months and needed new shoes. My usial choice the cs3 was not available in my size at the time so I opted to buy these after reading some reviews. I should have known better, the moment I put them on I thought they felt hard like I had just strapped on some wood shoes. I went out for an easy 8 mile run which hurt a lot more than It should've. top_reviews.title: Finally a shoe made for my flat feet - UPDATE 390 miles later
top_reviews.text:
UPDATE 1/14/2019 - After 390 miles of jogging and walking on my Redeemers, the rubber on the outer edge of the soles has worn all the way through to the foam. I started to notice at around 350 miles but I kept going with them because they still felt good. Now, the cushioning of the insole has lost its bounce so my impacts are harder and I have experienced some occaisional heel pain (plantar fasciitis?) as I am a heel striker. I am replacing these shoes with a new pair of Redeemers I just bought. I still love these shoes and will wear them as long as I can find them. I considered going to Redeemer 2 but I've seen mixed reviews. My original review of the Redeemer from 9/2016 follows below.
--------------------
If you're considering this shoe, you most likely have flat arches and over-pronate. If this is you, keep reading.

Most shoes I try on are too narrow for me where I can feel the midsole pressing against my flat arch. Once I saw the shape of the outsole of these Redeemers I was intrigued. Compare the outsole shape to other running shoes and you'll see what I mean. Its the first thing I look at when buying any shoe. I tried these on at a run shop among several others and they felt softer than the Brooks Beast yet had more stability than the massive Hoka Constant 2 (which felt like big pillows).

The size 11(my usual size) fit me perfectly. No need to buy a wide size because these were already wider than most running shoes. It has a sock liner (ISOFIT) that hugs the fore and mid foot and the tongue is sewn into it. Not really Huarache levels of sock liner but it does a good job of locking in my foot and provides an even amount of pressure all around my foot while still being breathable. No pain or blisters during my runs so far.

The impact of my foot strike could be a bit softer but that may be due to my weight. Also I wish the shoe had a pull tab on the heel but that's nitpicking.

I recommend this shoe to all flat footers. I might have to buy a second pair while its still on sale.

top_reviews.title: Converse convert*
top_reviews.text:

[My Boomer Mom gave up the ghost chastising me for that a looong time ago -lol] and that will cause a red, sore spot on the outside of my little toe within an hour or three. MUST WEAR THE NO SHOW SOCKS with this style.) I have highish arches. If I wear these shoes for a lot of walking or standing, at the end of the day when I take them off I will get a foot cramp as there is zero arch support. I did have to buy a pair of my old brand when my kid ended up in ICU because these are never gonna be 'standing around or pounding the pavement' comfortable. These are cute shoes first. Finally, I wear the white for every day activities. So they need washing a lot. You gotta have some sort of oxi additive and you just about need to soak or they come back yellow. Bleach worsens this, well water (how I started) or county water that is purified with chlorine (where I am now) - the white will yellow without a whitening laundry additive. So I'm down to like a 4 on my review because these shoes are too expensive to be this high maintenance.

I've worn nothing but Skechers for 12+ years. Got my first pair of Chuck Taylor Shoreline and was hooked. This was my second pair (my white pair are versatile but I needed black to match the majority of the rest of my wardrobe). Comfortable shoes BUT you will need the Chuck Taylor compatible socks, otherwise you may get a blister on the outside of a toe.

top_reviews.title: Very nice boot for the price paid
top_reviews.text:
Rocky boots are always comfortable in my experience. This boot is as well. It's light, yet supportive enough. It's perhaps a bit less waterproof than some of the other Rocky boots I've had, but on the other hand it's very breathable. It's definitely not a heavy duty though.....so calling it a construction boot might be stretching things. Outsoles have good traction, and there is plenty of cushioning in the midsole, and the ridiculously thick and plush removable insole!

This boot flexes more than I would like....I like some flex, but not so much that it creates a kind of pinching down effect while flexing. That pinching down is amplified by the extra long toe section. That is to say.....the tongue area is shorter, which in turn makes the section from the bottom lace to the tip of the toe a little longer.

A relatively minor nit, though.....I would definitely recommend this boot for overall comfort and lightweight design. My feet do not get sore after a 10 hour day working outside. That is an automatic 4 out of 5 stars. Also, Amazon had a smoking deal on my size.

top_reviews.title: At first the boots seem like decent quality for the price
top_reviews.text: At first the boots seem like decent quality for the price. Sole is nice an think, has plenty of grip, and the exterior leather finish is nice. However, there seems to have been a lack of quality on the inside with the left boot. It seems a piece of plastic was sewn inside on side of the upper boot. It kind of sounds like wrinkling plastic when you touch it. top_reviews.title: Not great but not bad (long review)
top_reviews.text:
TL;DR-- Cute slippers, good insoles and comfy but poor materials, odd fit. Don't pay more than $30 for these.

Glad I bought these at such a low price. These slippers are not the quality I expect from Vionic but they're decent slippers and if you paid under $30, I'd say that's a fair price. For me, there's good and bad aspects to these slippers. These are not suede like they appear. They aren't even felt. They kind of look like a felted canvas and feel a little stiff and rough, like something you'd make a kids project out of. Looks like it will pill and definitely a lint magnet if you buy black. Despite that, I do like other aspects of this slipper.

Looks: I was mainly attracted to the design, along with the supportive insole. I dislike how clunky and unattractive so many slippers are. The seams on the sides and higher heel collar create more flattering lines on the foot, so these don't make you look like you have yeti feet and give a more lifted appearance. The heel collar hits me at the back of my ankle, as opposed to a normal slipper or shoe that would come up to the back of the Achilles tendon. If you measure about an inch higher than where a normal shoe hits you, that's where the top of the heel collar will come to. The ribbons don't adjust and are for looks only.

Fit: definitely on the narrow side and slightly longer in length than I'm used to. I am between a 6.5 and 7, have slightly wide feet and toes that are all about the same length. I ordered a 7 and while the width is a bit snug, its still comfortable. They do feel a teeeeeny bit longer than most size 7s I've tried but its not bothersome. As for width, these felt a bit tight around the instep but felt fine around the width area at the ball of my foot. The tightness at the instep was mainly while pulling them on, creating a bit of a struggle, but the cheap crafting material they're made of will undoubtedly stretch, so I'm not bothered by the snug width. A thick seam on the sides where the faux shearling attaches to the shoe actually hurt while pulling them on but once my foot got shoved in the right position, the seam no longer came in contact with my foot, so no issue there. I panicked a little looking at the sole of the shoe, as it looked so narrow but oddly when I wear them, it doesn't seem to be an issue.

Now, about that insole-- Vionic shoes require some getting used to. I have a pair of their sandals with a molded footbed due to occasional bouts of plantar fasciitis. The support is fantastic but contrary to popular belief, orthotic support isn't supposed to be like walking on clouds. It's supposed to be firm, so it takes some time to acclimate. These slippers are no different. Having said that, the outer sole of the slipper is flat, a bit thin and a bit too flexible. So while the insole offers good support, it can only do so much when the outsole doesn't have much to offer. If you have foot issues or need major orthotic support, these slippers aren't for you.

Overall, these really fall in the category of most other slippers in that they look cute and are functional but lacking in key areas. Because they're "just slippers", we accept the flaws and try not to spend too much on them. So while these aren't the perfect slipper, I'm still satisfied with my purchase since I saw these slippers last week at major retailers for almost 3x's the price they are now.

top_reviews.title: Both Feet Are Happy, So I Will Keep Them
top_reviews.text: I love the style and color of these shoes and I also like the warm, breathable, water-resistant Gore-Tex.  They will be great for cooler and wetter weather.  However, I’m happiest with the fact that I actually found a pair of shoes to suit my fickle feet.  For a neutral shoe, they are pretty accommodating.  I used to have high arches, but not anymore.  From years of my arches falling and my feet getting longer, I now have two completely different feet.  My old lady feet have taken a beating and are—now—seldom in agreement.  Normally, if my left foot likes a shoe, then my right foot complains; and, if my right foot likes the shoe, then my left foot complains.  Each foot wants not only a different type of shoe, but also a different size.  My left foot is a half-size longer, and it is slightly thinner and flatter than the right foot.  While it still has a pretty good arch, it wants a neutral shoe.  Unfortunately, my right foot wants a curved shoe with support for supination.  It would also prefer a wider shoe with more room at the top to accommodate the arch.  I always wear a longer size shoe to accommodate the left foot, but it leaves the right foot sliding in the heal a bit.  When I go with a neutral shoe to accommodate the left foot, my right foot supinates and puts a lot of weight into the lateral side of the shoe.  When I go with a shoe that makes the right foot happy and supported, my left foot aches.  After a long search for shoes, I settled on these.  My left foot really loves these shoes, and my right foot is OK with it.  This is one of the few types of shoes where my feet are somewhat in agreement.  The wider toe box is nice too.  The only thing I would like better would be to have a little more room at the top of the shoe to accommodate those with slightly higher arches.  I do measure the length and width of my feet and check the manufacturer before buying shoes online, and I would say that these shoes run slightly narrower than expected.  I have pretty decent—but not high--arches and these barely accommodate the top of my feet, so there is a bit of pressure there.  It is not bad though and I’m fairly certain that this will ease up as I break in the shoes.  The cushioning in these shoes is superb and makes up for a lot.  I think it will do a good job of protecting my right knee from any damage from supination.  However, a person with higher arches might want to look elsewhere for stability and/or room.  Right now,  I can’t vouch for the durability of the shoe, since I just got them.  However, they appear to be well made.  I have had Brooks Ghost shoes in the past and they held up over a year.  I’m pretty rough on shoes and can easily go through a pair in under six months, so I am pleased with my last purchase.  Hopefully, these will hold up too.

The heel, too, is a little lower than the Pamela's & I liked the height of the Pamela better.  But there's hardly any weight to the shoe, & it's very soft & comfy. top_reviews.title: Tenuous at first, great in the end!
top_reviews.text:
I bought these shoes to replace my Chacos, which have always been too bulky and rubbed in odd spots, and I couldn't be happier. Xero has a lifelong customer out of me. I was initially very worried that the size I ordered was too small, with my toes poking out all the way to the very end, but cut the tag off and moved on because there wasn't any stock in the size up. Frustrated but hopeful, I threw them into the deep end of field testing. They immediately went with me on a three day camping excursion, with a five-mile hike, a trip to the hot springs and some driving in between. After a few dips in the river, they stretched out a bit and were totally comfortable throughout the hike up and down Salt Creek Falls. Now that I'm back in town, I can safely say I love the feel of these shoes (I have a pair of Fivefingers and they're cool but weird with the fabric between my toes) and look forward to wearing them for as long as seasonally feasible.

Really, if you are between two sizes, just toss a coin. I don't think I'd be sad if I'd ordered a size up, but going a size down was just fine.

top_reviews.title: Ahhh to feel the ground beneath my feet
top_reviews.text: The reviews that mention there is no support and you can feel rocks under your feet are dead on, which is exactly why I wanted this sandal. A lack of stimulation in the feet contributes to a bunch of other physical maladies, and I love that this lets me feel what I'm walking on, while still giving me protection. They are a bit wide looking with the little lips that curl up on the sides of the foot, but that adds to the stability which has been a great feature. My feet muscles do all the work they should be doing, and they look like a Teva or something that has conveniently become a bit more in style lately, I think. I am a bit worried about the strap pulling out of the thin rubber where it attaches, but I think with their guarantee I'll get the life out of them that I need. They are quite thin, so if you're new to barefoot shoes I would recommend the z-trail that has thicker soles. I wouldn't hike in these yet, but I wear them everywhere. I'm going to have to find some barefoot shoes for the colder weather because my toes have spread out so wonderfully since purchasing these a few months ago, regular shoes are super uncomfortable. A good problem to have, in my opinion. I have noticed that I've had to put more effort into picking up my toes and the front of my foot; I caught the front edge of the sandal on more than one occasion, even when I tightened the strap, but I really don't like toe straps so for me it's been worth making the adjustment. I originally ordered a size 10, which is my usual size, but they were quite large. The 9 has been perfect. Overall, very happy with my healthier footwear purchase.

top_reviews.title: worth every penny
top_reviews.text:
I could swear I wrote a review for these last week. Did it get removed?

I've been wearing these boots for a week now, and they're awesome. I worried about wearing them in hot weather (I live in the southwest) before I reminded myself that I trained in the military to wear combat boots in the deserts of Iraq.

That's the thing, though. These boots are built with padding to help with moisture and allow your feet to breathe. So even if I ran out of foot powder, I still wouldn't arrive at work with smelly feet. The boots are basically designed to keep your feet dry.

They are also REALLY comfortable. Possibly the most comfortable pair of boots I've ever owned! Most boots have to be broken in, but not these padded babies.

They can be taken off and put on really easy, too, thanks to the side zipper. So when I come home tired after work, I don't have to struggle to get my boots off. I just step out of them.

Probably the most amusing thing about wearing them is the amount of respect I get from babbling fools who are afraid of getting a boot up their ass.

That's right. Respect me in my giant stompy boots.

top_reviews.title: Perfect except..
top_reviews.text: I was very excited to have a Chelsea boot, even more excited to have docs again. I haven't owned a pair in many years but I know that they are worth the investment and will last. The only downside to these shoes is they are not made for people with high arches, I've been wearing them for a month and am still trying to break them in. The tops of my feet are quite irritated from the rubbing. Sometimes with I sit with my legs crossed, the foot in the air loses circulation because of how tight they are... Other than that I adore them. Will update in the future but that is all for now!

top_reviews.title: For when you're too old for Blundstones.
top_reviews.text:
I've been wearing Blundstones for many years but they were just getting too hard on my knees. They're great boots, but the soles are firm, firm, firm without much cushioning elsewhere.

Saw these and thought it might be a good switch-out. Same chelsea boot convenience, similar looks (black leather boot) but far softer Dr. Martens shock-absorbing soles.

I knew they'd be a bit roomier than I wanted, and they are. Dr. Martens are just a tad wider than I like, especially toward the front. But I'm getting used to it, and in the meantime, they are much easier on my knees and ankles than the Blundstones were. So I'll probably stick with the Docs from now on!

top_reviews.title: SO happy with my boots!
top_reviews.text: I was a bit hesitant to order because of that one star review, but these boots are perfect!! The boots came super quickly and fit me perfectly. I am typically an 8.5 in shoes so I sized up to W9 and they fit with room for thick socks (which is what I wanted). They are pretty stiff but that’s to be expected at first! Overall I highly recommend this product and would consider anyone on the fence to just go for it!!

top_reviews.title: Men, wide feet don't size down.
top_reviews.text:
I am a fan of boots but often time have a hard time finding chelsea's that fit due to my wide feet. Just for reference when it comes to work boots I wear a Redwing Wellington 9, Wolverine 9 but in other brands such as Thursday Boots etc sometimes go to an 8 or 8 1/2 depending on the brand and model. For these Doc Martens I will say this.

If your a male and have E feet do not size down. Go with your normal size. At a size 9 these fit perfectly. Width/length is good. A little snug up top but that will change with time due to leather break in. Often people talk about leather breaking in which is true but only for the top area of the boot. They never get wider with break in. So take my advice and order your normal size. They will be a little snug up top but everything else will be perfect and only get better after the break in period.

top_reviews.title: Best purchase I’ve ever made
top_reviews.text: I got these boots months ago for work (I work in a warehouse) and I have to say these might be one of the best purchases I’ve ever made. My job involves me standing for 8-10 hours a day on concrete floors, so I needed something safe, durable and comfortable. I’ve always wanted some doc martens so this was my excuse. I normally wear a 6.5 but the reviews said to go down half a size and they fit so nicely. I have to say though, when I first got these I thought they were the most uncomfortable shoes I’ve ever gotten and I was like “why did I just spend so much on these shoes if they’re unbearable?!” Well bear in mind, this was my first time wearing leather boots and my first time wearing steel toes. Once I broke them in (took about 2 weeks) they never came off. I actually wear them outside of work all the time. They’re not too wide and the shoe box is a good width. They’re great to wear in the rain because your socks never get wet. Basically, if you need a good pair of work boots, spend the money and get these. They’re a solid investment and they’ll be a life changer.

top_reviews.title: These are not the work boots you’re looking for.
top_reviews.text: These boots were really comfortable for about two months but that was it. Now they are almost unbearable. I expect a $130 boot to last longer. Stay away from this shoe if you plan on wearing them daily for work. Stay far away. Not worth it. Not worth the pain.

top_reviews.title: Great!
top_reviews.text: I knew getting a size 9 would fit a little bit bigger than my usual 8 and 1/2 but the 8 would of been way too narrow for my wide feet. I have a men’s steel toe dr.marten and they are pretty heavy (i had hip surgery so now any weight bothers it 2x more)and after working 16 hour days 7 days a week I need a comfortable boot that'll hold up! These seem so perfect! I know I’ll be able to wear them with a thick sock in the winter (even with the steel toe) They are beautiful boots and the zipper is the best part. Nobody has time to lace up and down their boots working in this business. The worst part is coming home having to bend over, unlace and kick em off. Not anymore! Im wayyyy too excited for these! They seem of great quality and like I said I own many pairs already so this will be a great pick for me!

top_reviews.title: The best wooden clogs I have owned
top_reviews.text: Fit was perfect. They arrived in the time the seller said. I have plantar fasciitis and these give me instant relief as my arch (and plantar fascia) are fully supported. Leather is thick and comfortable at the same time. No annoying edge binding either that always seems to come loose on other brands and cause irritation to the instep. The price is right as well. I will be back for more.

top_reviews.title: Quite satisfied
top_reviews.text:
Item arrived about 3 weeks from date of order via UK Royal Parcel Post. The build quality and quality of the nubuck material looks top notch. The fit is a tad large by 1.5 cm compared to Sanita's men's clogs of the same size (43cm). It takes a few minutes to get used to the carved wood as it feels more firm when taking the first few steps (vs the dense foam of Sanita's). After 30 minutes or so it feels equal in comfort including use while driving.

I took away one star for the following reasons: the attached resin sole is a tad slippery on hard floor surfaces, so one needs to walk with care when the floor is untextured stone or linoleum; the wooden clogs produce more sound when walking on hard surface; the wooden sole may get soiled or dirty easily (I plan to apply a thin coat of matt polyurethane varnish). The clogs work well on carpeted surface (padded or non-padded).

Overall, I am quite satisfied. One just needs to be aware of the product's limitations as mentioned above.

top_reviews.title: A TRADITIONAL CLOG THAT ECHOES VINTAGE COGS OF THE PAST
top_reviews.text:
I used to wear clogs regularly in the 1970's and 1980's, then after a move, somehow, my clogs got lost in the shuffle... literally. I have gone "clog-less" for decades, always on the lookout either for a vintage pair that would fit, or for new ones, and here, I find Vollsjö Men's Genuine Leather Wooden Clogs Made in EU.

I do believe these are made in Poland, and the construction is solid and perfectly executed for the typical, no frills footwear. I have ordered two pairs, this is the first pair I ordered: An all-wood base with suede leather upper. These, quite simply are fantastic. The other pair I ordered (same price) has a smooth leather and is unique; you'll have to check out that review to learn more. The hardwood base is just that: No frills, and hardwood.

When I am asked about the comfort of these, I liken them to walking barefooted on a hardwood floor, only with these, the floor comes with you and is relatively conformed to supporting your feet with every step.

The treads on the soles and heels are typical for clogs, quite sufficiently "grippy" to provide good traction. The quality of the leather upper, which covers the foot from instep to the toes, is perhaps not the finest leather, but for the price, it is leather, the uppers are breathable, and with or without socks, the comfort again is right up there on top! I simply love these! Buy with confidence!
(Note: look at the photos carefully as you peruse types and styles/colors of leather, as some models feature the all wood base, some are the rubber base with wood veneer insert (I love those too, those are the other pair that I bought, and they are fabulous... check out my separate review for those.)

top_reviews.title: Solid, original quality. With the right socks, super comfortable
top_reviews.text:
Seem hard-wearing so far. Made just like the original clogs I wore decades ago. Nice, easy slip-on / slip-off. I feel my feet are kept cool. They are hand-made in Poland, as far as I could tell. I feel good about that. Worth the wait. Super comfortable with cotton socks. Clogs take a few days to get used to, but worth it, and very good for feet and posture, I find anyway. I wear them everywhere now. The size 10 fit was perfect. Stitching and stapling seem robust and I think they will last. The dark blue works well with blue jeans.
I recommend them.

top_reviews.text:
I got these TIOSEBON slip-on sneakers as an experiment into a style of shoe that I haven't had before (full-foot non-laced slip on loafer style). I have been mostly quite happy with them. I got them in the black color which is indeed a black denim, looks good in person.

Pros:
-Slip on easily with one hand assist.
-Fairly lightweight
-Comfortable footbed with slight platform/height lift. I find them to be good support because if the bottom is too squishy, it can feel like walking on sand.
-Nice style, gets complimented.

Con
-The length of the shoes for my size 9 feet is fairly appropriate, but the toe region is somewhat narrow. This means that part of my inner foot/big toe on each side hits a raised lip where the shoe transitions to fabric. It has gotten better with a little breaking in. I do have wide feet but the issue is limited to distal toe region. Center of shoe feels appropriate and supportive.

top_reviews.title: Minnetonka mocs - always a good choice
top_reviews.text:
These mocs look and feel great. They are soft and comfortable from the first moment you put them on. There is no break-in period with these. They do, however, tend to stretch with age, and you might have to tighten the laces every year or so. I also have a pair of driving Minnetonkas I purchased about 3 years ago, and I've had to snug them up a few times.

The insole is soft, the outer is perfectly finished, and the outer rubber sole is flexible, soft and grippy.

I have read several of the good and bad reviews on Minnetonkas purchased from Amazon's retailers. Some of you had trouble with the fit. I probably am an actual size 8.5 EE or EEE, but since never have the patience to hunt down 8.5 in double or triple wide sizes I wear size 9 in all my shoes and boots, and 9 has been my size for about 30 years. I also wear a 9mm heel lift on the right side, a suggestion from a chiropractor to even me out. These mocs fit perfectly, and my toes are right at the tip. Not too snug, just right. You might want to go a half-size over with these. Sometimes I buy size 9 shoes and I feel like my toes have a lot of room, but not these. These are perfect. And sometimes, like with my latest pair of Merrell sneaks, size 9 is pretty tight and I wish I had more room. Not every mfgr sizes shoes (or clothes) the same.

Those are a bit loose as regards to width in the heal, but the length is right.  Added note - I wear this as a slipper with no socks.

top_reviews.title: Did we all try the same boot?!
top_reviews.text:
I just got a pair of IC Longer Lashes boots in champagne, and I ADORE them. A few points about these boots:

1) These don't fit like an average shoe. Instead, they're a clog with a leather overlay. Therefore, the fit feels different than the normal, snug boot. It's completely inflexible, and the shoe is contoured with both a front and back resting area built into the sole. It's very hard to tip either forward or back in them - I couldn't do it.

2) The untreaded sole is just like what you'd get on your average pair of heels. Heck, even a stiletto boot would have a sole like these do! Most fashion boots don't have a thick tread. These aren't Timberlands, folks! If you have issues, I suggest you score the bottoms (slice them with a knife or scissor in a criss-cross pattern), or use a few pieces of double-stick tape to increase stickiness. Or, buy non-skid pads.

3) I don't even know what to say about not scuffing up the bottoms in order to preserve the branding. There's just...I can't. I just can't.

4) The upper leather is thick. This means that the boot will last a long time, and will turn butter soft with wear. The color will also mature and change, much like denim does.

In other words, these boots are gold, and I'm SO GLAD that I got them. I get a ridiculous amount of positive comments on these shoes, and I was able to wear them for ten hours straight the first day I had them.

Your loss, ladies...

top_reviews.title: Slippery
top_reviews.text:
This review is for the Steve Madden Men's Fenta Fashion Sneaker - Grey Fabric.

These shoes look good, but don't look quite as I expected. The fabric is a slightly darker grey and the soles are much more of an aged white than depicted. My pair didn't have any of the defects shown in other reviews.

My first complaint is that these shoes are very stiff. Sure, I haven't broken them in yet, but I have purchased plenty of shoes in my life and none were this rigid. If this changes after they are broken in, I will update my review. My second and biggest complaint is that these shoes are very slippery on tile flooring. They are worse than socks! Though they do have a normal amount of grip on carpet/sidewalks.

Bought these shoes on Cyber Monday. Looks like I saved $3 off the regular price.

Update: After closer inspection, the soles are coated with a fibrous material causing them to be slippery. After about a mile of walking on pavement, enough of this material will wear off to increase the grip to an acceptable level. Just be cautious about going to the grocery store in a brand new pair of these shoes.

top_reviews.title: A challenge to get on but worth the prize
top_reviews.text:
Pros:
These shoes are just gorgeous. I’m living out my 80s goth dreams in these. They’re super lightweight; I have platform heels and they can sometimes feel like you’re carrying 15lbs on each foot. They also aren’t slippery - very important for heels like these because one bad slip and it’s over for your ankle. The top of the shoe also isn’t too tight. I have a pair of boots identical to these that come all the way up to the knee and that band is too tight so it creates a bulge. Not with these.

Cons:
As you would probably know if you’re a fan of this style shoe, you will break a sweat trying to get these on. The ankle part has no stretch. My tip is to wear thin pantyhose or pantyhose socks with them. Your foot will slide in easier that way. If you’re looking for a pair of shoes to slide on quick and easily then these aren’t for you. But no one said being a baddie was easy 😪🫡

top_reviews.title: Glad I Purchased These Shoes!
top_reviews.text:
I purchased these shoes for a formal event, and I am so glad I did! The band close to the toes covered parts of my feet that I am self-conscious about. The ankle strap fit well (and slimmed my ankles!) and the zippered heel covering fit well too. I went with a 10 because some shoes that I wear are closer to a 10.5, but my left foot is a little shorter than my right. The size of the wedge and the security of the top strap, ankle strap and heel support made these the ideal shoes for my function. I did take them off when I hit the dance floor though because I did not want to risk twisting my ankle. Also, I would not wear these shoes for more than a few hours at a time, because while securing my toes in place, the band might have irritated the skin after a while.

The only real con was the material--I believe it's like a black suede(?). As long as you wear the shoes in the evenings, it could be worn year-round depending on your location.

The shoe itself is comfy, and the cut is perfect as far as how high it comes on the top of the foot and heel.  It's decently wide and the knit fabric gives just a little to help make it comfier.  I like how the knit is kindof laminated (not really, it's just not raw fabric) and the front toe area is a thick coating over the knit, so I feel like it's still waterproof but not as likely to start rubbing off as some of the other Sketchers I own that have the more traditional rubbbery toe. top_reviews.title: Hard to get foot into
top_reviews.text:
Whenever I purchase items online, I always try to read the reviews prior to making my purchasing decision. The boots arrived faster than expected. So, I figured I would leave feedback for others as well. I bought these a 1/2 larger than what I would normally wear based on review feedback coupled with the shape of the toe being pointed versus rounded or squared. PROS: super fast shipping, high quality product, very affordable price CONS: although the opening of the boot is wide, it is a royal pain try to actually get foot inside (I honestly believe a zipper on the inside would have been a great improvement to this product on the manufacturing side and they of course can be added later but are very
expensive to have put into boots), once I was able to get my foot inside all of the way the were not as narrow as I anticipated based on other reviews, and although these ARE Harley Davidson boots, the bottom part of the sole (excluding the heel) is very slick and slippery. I would not suggest wearing these for riding unless you add some anti slip strips to the bottom. To not to this could cause a slip or fall getting on or off of a bike, tipping the bike over or even risk it possibly falling on you. Do I like this product yes, will I fight and struggle to put these boots on YES (in private of course because I assure you the process was not pretty LOL)

top_reviews.title: Fit poorly - bad for water walking
top_reviews.text:
I bought these "water" shoes so I could walk in streams, lakes and beaches without hurting the bottom of my feet on stones or sticks or sand or gravel. Unfortunately, they do not do that. Firstly, the fit was tight. The strap in the back went on OK, but my toes felt a bit cramped in front.

The main problem was the open hole design. These shoes are full of holes, by design. As soon as I started walking in the stream, dirt, silt and sand slipped into the shoes, within seconds. I felt like I was walking on grit, and in fact, I was. It was horribly uncomfortable. I took off the shoes within a minute, and carried them while I walked barefoot. Returned them the next day.

They may be OK for a swimming pool, but for a sandy beach, lake or stream, forget it. They are terrible. Likewise, I would not try walking on solid ground (road, grass trail, etc.) with them. The fit was not correct for walking shoes.

top_reviews.text: There seems to be something weird about the way this shoe is molded- it doesn't want to fit a foot correctly.  We love croc shoes- their slip-ons out of cloth/leather are amazingly comfortable and always a nice fit.  These particular shoes seem to be mis-molded.  The insert hole for your foot forces your foot to be way back and your heel overhangs- we tried two sizes to no avail.  Your heel hangs off the back edge of the shoe and your toes never reach anywhere near the font of the shoe.  Love crocs, but we could not make these work.

top_reviews.title: Good casual work boot!
top_reviews.text:
This is my first experience with Australian style work boots. I can say they have a place in my collection, but they're not my favorite style. That's not indicative of the quality though, I think they're well made.

I wanted some boots that would be easy to slip on in the morning, and these fit that bill perfectly. They're comfortable and lightweight. My issue is the ankle support. top_reviews.title: Nice boots
top_reviews.text:
(Just wanted to state that I received these as part of the Amazon Vine program but I try to keep all my reviews unbiased and honest)
These are nice boots, but I am still on the fence about the comfort. They are well constructed with nice stitching and glueing. I tried to take very close pictures to display as much detail as possible. I have a wider foot but the size 9 fit fine. The 2 finger loops the boots have are in great positions to help with putting the boots on. When I put them on for the first time, I noticed immediately that they lack any type of arch support. The soles of the boots are soft and very grippy. I also noticed that the thin rim around your ankle starts to rub up against my ankle area. I will need to wear them for several days to see how this area will soften up. Also, shoes/boots are very hard to review since everyone seems to fit a little different. I do wish that they had more cushioning inside, but I am going to get some aftermarket insoles to see if I can add more arch support. I just figured for the going price, that they would be a little more comfortable. Again,,,it's very hard to review how the boots will feel to anyone else as I'm just describing my initial reactions. I really like the craftsmanship, the look and the features. I will update my review after several days of wearing.

top_reviews.title: Superb Customer Service !!
top_reviews.text:
Received these boots in good condition. Looks well manufactured. Inner sole is nothing special. Other reviewers talk about putting in their own sole - I will do same.
Outer seems quite durable but flexible enough to be comfy. Slip on design works well with strong elastic at opening. I chose these over other brands due to combination composite toe with rubber guard/EH rating/non slip sole.

However, I was expecting a size 10.5 to be a little on the large size but turned out to be perfect fit. According to size chart 10.5 = EU 44-45 but tag on boot has 10.5 = EU 43.5 ... If i knew this i would have probably gone with US size 11 or 10.5 wide ( i usually wear EU size 44).

Anyway time will tell how they wear in .. will update after few months. Bought these to use at work onboard ship so they are in for a good testing.

UPDATE: April 2023 - Goodville responded to my review and removed / updated their size chart. In addition they offered to send out another pair free of charge and with no return of first pair.
I gave them my EU size (44) and foot length (28cm) and they suggested size 11W which is what they sent. This new pair fits much better. Together with my "Superfeet" inner sole the boot fit is very comfortable with good toe room.
Thanks to Goodville for their astute customer service !

top_reviews.title: Great Price/Quality Ratio
top_reviews.text:
[[VIDEOID:6174bf02928d49a79f117a7bbc3c6a72]] Decided to buy these Goodville Safety Toe Waterproof boots for work. I am working in an industrail field and we are required to wear EH-Rated, ASTM-certified safety footwear at work at all the time. So far, I’ve been wearing these boots for a week and here are my 5 cents:

First of all is quality. Boots are very well-made, there is not a spot I found where it could be a production flaw or a glue mark. Leather is thick and heavy duty.

Second, is the fit. Fits like a glove (I am size 14) and boots are exactly true to a size. Easy on/off pull-on straps are durable and well-sewn.

Third, is the price. At this price category, these boots can definetly compete with other famous footwear brands and at some points, in my opinion better than them.

Forth is protection. Boots got a nose protection from occasional scratch. Also has ASTM-Certifited safety toe with EH-Rating. Many boots on Amazon say, that they are ASTM certified, but they are not. I’ve reached out to Goodville and they sent me copies of ASTM certification without any questions asked.

To finalize, I think I just found my new favorite, but the time will show. Will update my review in the month or so.

top_reviews.title: Amazing Full Rubber Work boots!  Lightweight steel toe!
top_reviews.text:
I really like these boots. They are really well made, comfortable and sturdy. They also have a very good heel cap (with a rigid 3-layered small "lip" to pry off your boots quickly with the other foot) and very nice lightweight steel toe.

My foot felt comfortable even though there is no significant padding within the shoe they go beyond the ankle and they’re good for about ¾ of a foot to maybe a foot of water, fully waterproof with very good soles. They also have very good two-finger "pull tabs" on the front and the back of each boot.

I am highly recommending the boots and I think you should buy them if you’re in the market for a waterproof safe work boot. They are very well made for the money considering what else is out there in this category, very strong choice with steel toe. This is the top choice. Highly recommended as a vine reviewer.

top_reviews.title: Look and Feel Quality Made
top_reviews.text: My first thought when unpacking these Goodville boots was the impressive build quality. They felt solid but not too heavy. I looked them over and didn’t see any imperfections, not even small imperfections. The gluing was clean, the double stitching was perfect; they are well crafted.  Putting them on was easier than expected. I have a high arches and big ankles which makes putting on boots difficult sometimes. The stretchy material and loops at the top made slipping them on effortless. I like that the loops are big enough for my fingers. So many times boot makers will put a tiny loop that’s too small to grip let alone put a finger through. The boots fit true to size. The included insoles have almost no cushioning which is the only way these boots failed to impress. I’m used to replacing stock insoles with high arch insoles for every pair of new shoes/boots. So not a biggy for me. With high arch insoles the boots are comfortable and have good stability. The soles are very grippy and look well suited for slippery surfaces. I anticipate they will do well when I’m working in icy conditions. The boots are easy to take off because of the nice grippy ridges on the heels.  I’ll be using these for gardening, splitting firewood; general outside work. I think they will be dependable for years.  I’ll update my review if the boots don’t perform as expected.

top_reviews.title: Good for hiking, overkill for walking
top_reviews.text:
I am a longtime KEEN shoe/boot buyer. I wanted some lighter weight waterproof boots for winter. Even though I live in Maine, early winters here are more wet than snowy, and we often have a thaw in January or February. I was looking for something comfortable for walking with our dog.

If you are a regular KEEN wearer, you’ll notice right away that the toe box is slightly narrower than the classic KEEN shape. I usually wear a 9/5 or 10, and in these boots the size 10s still fit me; it’s just that they aren’t as perfectly comfortable in the toes as the classic KEEN shape. The ankles of these boots are fairly stiff, to give you good support, but they don’t rub or chafe. The tread provides for good secure walking.

I wanted waterproof boots for the season. The waterproofing on these has worked through some of the early winter rains we’ve been having. The tradeoff I find with waterproof boots is that my feet tend to feel like they can’t breathe.

Now that I’ve had these for awhile, I have to say they’re not the first boots I grab when I’m going out for a walk. Most of the time, I’m not walking where I need the ankle support, so I prefer boots that are less constricting—and ones that I can just slip on while the dog fusses for me to get a move on. These are a good choice for hiking, but they seem like overkill for regular walking.

top_reviews.title: Awesome hiking boots
top_reviews.text: I got these hiking boots to use for all sorts of things - regular hiking, backpacking, etc. I got the chinois/dusty pink color which looks really nice in person and appears the same as in the product photos. If I'm being honest these boots were a little hard to break in - it took 4-5 hikes to break them in, but now they're great. I really like that they're waterproof - I've had them out in the rain or walking through deep puddles and have had no issues at all. I also live in a cold climate, and have had these boots out with thin socks in below zero temps and feet have stayed warm. I've used these for many hikes including one that was 15 miles and have no complaints at all. The grip on the bottom is good but if you're walking on a skating rink of ice you might slip, but aside from that they are as good as can be expected. Keen did a great job with these.

top_reviews.title: Fit well and look great
top_reviews.text: [[VIDEOID:4b4bd391b31a681fc657c25eaae90959]] Let me start off by saying that I love these shoes, there’s definitely a bit of room for improvement on them but they look great and are super light weight compared to other steal toe shoes. I work for amazon and we are required to wear steal toe shoes but the ones provided to use are typically bulky, uncomfortable and just ugly. The only issue I have with these shoes is that because of sole not being rubber or something, instead it’s a hard plastic which isn’t the most comfortable support for your heels after a 10 hour shift, but with some insoles they’re a lot more comfortable. Another issue is that since they’re mesh, they aren’t the most durable shoes I have, however I’ve had timberland steal toes that have worn out before these have and they were double the price, these are definitely still good to wear they just have a small aesthetic issue that I don’t care too much about, after all they did save my toes from being crushed by a uboat at work which is a large metal cart used to Carry large boxes. Overall I’m happy with my purchase and I’ll be buying more colors eventually

top_reviews.title: Solid dry weather traction. Great price.
top_reviews.text: For a basic hiking shoe under $40 they’re a steal.  I do upwards of 300+ miles year round so I burn through pairs regularly and these have held up well in dry and moderately damp conditions.  I’ve got Merrells, Columbia and Salomons for winter but these are fantastic for drier conditions. No issues with about 25+ miles on them to date and the tread has held up. They do need to be broken in a bit but don’t be deterred, just wear a thicker hiking sock and they’ll break in well.

top_reviews.title: Wears very well for everyday use
top_reviews.text: Like others, I bought the first pair for about 2/3 the price at Costco several years ago.  I really liked the shoes for everyday use (about 5 miles a day but sometimes up to 10).  I was disappointed that Costco no longer carried them but gladly paid the higher (normal?) price here because they wore so well.  As you can see, the sole did not separate the failure was eventually at the bottom seams.  The soles wore down fairly evenly.  These shoes were many years old and heavily worn on walks around town and occasional hikes  on trails.  They are not real "hiking boots" and there is not much stiffness in the soles for rocks and boulder hopping across creeks.  They are also not waterproof but for light hiking on trails and daily use, they are excellent.

top_reviews.title: These are my walking shoes....

top_reviews.title: Comfortable but short wearing
top_reviews.text:
I like a nice summer casual shoe but I'm not a fan of white athletic shoes, these had a midpoint them.
I bought my first pair at a membership store, my second pair I got (at double the price) from Amazon.

The shoes are well made and seem to constructed from quality materials.
Having said that, after 100+ days of extensive wear (including a daily mile long daily dog walk), a hole appeared in the upper portion of one show and the soles of both had extensive wear on the outer heels.
After such a short life, why but another pair?
I like the looks and they aren't that expensive....though my first pair at $14 was an obvious better buy. I'm not sure This Amazon price is a great value. Still it beats going to the mall to find a new show which may, or may not, last longer.

top_reviews.title: Comfortable (when broken in), sneakers HOWEVER quality seems to be a BIG issue
top_reviews.text:
May 2022: I have only worn these like 3 times MAX since the December update and the entire black part around the front (not the very front that goes under the sneaker), the part that goes around the front that many reviewers have showed pictures of it tearing have almost completely torn .... I WOULD NOT recommend these .... between that, the fit being "OK" but ANY of my Skechers ... even without memory foam are a bit more comfy .... I just cant recommend these....I love Skechers but I wanted to like these, I really did ... I am open to liking different brands ... these are just poor quality

December 20 2021 Update: I have worn these a few times since the last update ... some say 2-3 mile walks ... yardwork .. nothing crazy ... the front part that most people mention splitting is now splitting everywhere i didn't do the numerous repairs on them already. I still hestitate to call these "junk" even though I dropped ANOTHER star. I admit I originally put more "milage" on them when they were new than i'd typically do for a new pair of sneakers, and also admit my go-to brand Skechers is NOT Perfect but they A) hold up so much better, even if they have issues from time to time B) are a similar price when i catch them on sales which i always do C) they are (even with my walmart insoles that I like) more comfortable with the built in Skechers memory foam, with the last few pairs of Skechers I have picked up have Memory Foam.

These (and really I dont trust Fila now) have way too many issues with the amount of use i put on them

Sept Update: (last update where i was going back and forth liking/hating these sneakers removed) ... I have had these in a box for awhile and barely wore them in the last few months ... today I wore them out for a walk and MORE of the front was randomly ripping with fuse from inside the ... resin? ... I am not sure what that front part is but it is like a cheap (really cheap) attempt to look like fake leather or something.

I love Skechers but I'd never say they are perfect either but I just noticed that while I have made excuses for the tread in the bottom like "I wore these out alot more than I normally would a new pair of sneakers" ... WHILE STILL TRUE ... the tread only in the deepest spots is still there ... in say the back of both sneakers... all the tread is gone ... and after months of use I'd not claim my go-to brand Skechers is great ... but this is not good ... needing this many repairs already and they are not even what .. (I forgot really) 5 months old TOPS and NOT worn daily ... they should not be having this many issues before a year 1/2 to 2 years old ... and one use-case I had was wearing them in the rain if i had to ... they have not even been in a drizzle yet and they are falling apart. I will keep them as long as i can but these are 100% "knock around" sneakers at best now ...
------------------------
June 17 2021 update: Ok I officially CAN NOT recommend these. I know i can repair them again but knowing you haven't read my full review yet, I assumed the black around the front ripping, was due to me putting a shoe-horn in the right sneaker to stretch it out. I do admit fit wise that worked and it's been fine ever since but I bought these in Feburary 2021 and as far as the bottom tred wearing out fast, I admit I have put alot more wear on them and alot more miles than other new sneakers... so while they should last longer ... I will even give them a pass there ... but like a few others have posted pictures of ... noticing them out for a few mile walk today ... in a number of areas, the back part at the front just rips open for no reason ... not un-repairable or anything but it's not even worth it at say $25 which is what i paid. These were going to be kept in good shape, but these will be my "wearing them in the rain" sneakers, when my current "rain pair" are unwearable ...I rather put even say the $25 I paid for these into a USED (like-new, or maybe even "very good" here on amazon) pair of my go-to brand Skechers ... I will NEVER claim THEY are perfect but ... the quality is better ... even before this ripping for no reason issue started, I'd still say these Filas WERE "OK, but Skechers are better quality".

I am disappointed as they look good and once broken in fit-wise they are not bad ... but if they fall apart like this, THIS SOON (note: I have not worn them nearly daily eather, these past few months) ... I am not buying them.

-----------------------------------------
Update (prior updates condensed down):

I think I finally (did have to move where I put the SOFCOMFORT Double Thick Foam piece (from leftover insules) but right around the area where my two smallest toes are and/or right in back of them (on my foot) .that is where the issue was in (only the right.. never had the problem in the left sneaker) in the right sneaker … I think I have it just right and I am happy about that though there is another BIG problem now.

I JUST noticed ... the black part wrapping around the toe area... is ripping already in under 30 days and the more I wear it the worse the rip gets…. I hate to say it but this soon … this is not acceptible … I was really thinking about getting a backup pair and even with the Con of the fit in the right sneaker … with the little fix (that yes I shouldn’t have had to do) I did … I was happy enough ...while the sole (at the moment anyway) is still glued correctly, this rip has any idea I had of getting another pair, going right out the window. They do look nice (not as nice as the pictures online though … even on other sites) … but still nice… they don’t “seem” cheep but my go-to brand Skechers at worst would do this sort of thing after MONTHS of wear. I admit I must have say ...40+ miles on these so far … I am not going easy on them OR being super abusive … one reason being is if this sort of issue were to come up .. I want to know before I waste $$ on another pair. I am not editing my review below so you can see my more intial impressions but … my (with my own fix 4.5/5 ….without it .. maybe 4/5) has dropped to a 3.5/5 JUST because of the fact that while they are holding up … that wildcard of “will they last” is not looking good…. Also something I never said … I have put miles on these but the think treads which I loved at first … are wearing down FAST for what I expected… it’s not terrible but … parts of the bottoms are nearly “flat” already.

Even for the price… well I DID recommend them before … I cant outright NOT recommend them now … but “meh” is more of my answer seeing this question … maybe I can use Shoe Goo or Gorilla Glue to fix the rip but … as I said it’s not even 30 days and I shouldn’t have to do this already .. the fit “con” I can accept since it’s easy to get around that using stuff I already have … the rip .. yeah that annoys me

I just wore my go-to brand Skechers for the first time in two weeks or so and I do admit they are a better quality sneaker than these, but I have had cheap quality brand stuff and this is sort of in the middle, NEARER to "well made" ... I have to be honest ... those ones I wore today ... had to be repaired and the USE (not how many days .. how many miles I put on them before needing the repari) are CLOSE to the Fila's I think .. as I said I was not "babying" these like I may with other new sneakers.

Final thought is I think I got disappointed because first I had low expectations, THAN (see intial review) got really impressed ... THAN things started to become issues though if you dont count the times i undid my fix (to test them) .. the fit is ok now .. now as comfy as most of my Skechers but i'd still give it a two thumbs up there .. 1 3/4 anyway .. they shouldn't be ripping this soon; HOWEVER, not making excuses ... just being fair to Fila ... my Skechers need repairs sooner than I'd like to admit sometimes too .. and they are still my go-to brand. These are so close to being "really good" to me .. it's that they are that close but just off enough that makes me disappointed.

Sudden though: the rip did start the day after I put a (front) shoehorn in to stretch out the front ... noting this issue that I am disappointed in ... well the shoehorn + the padding may have made the right sneaker more comfortable .. but may have been a self-inflicted issue... I just want to be fair here.
----------------------
Intial Review:

First I will start off by saying that I hate writing reviews for stuff like this where I cant speak for them long-term. I just got these in the mail and am wearing them now. To already answer my own question, I usually go with Skechers and I was given a gift of a pair of New Balance that fit my size 13 feet fine. I have gotten a great deal (like $13 max) on some "no-name" sneakers before and the fit ... is a bit off....Basically I never needed wide-width in NB or Skechers .. but no-name brand ... are hit and miss ... some "13"s actually FEEL like 12s ...

Pros:
- Comfort: THESE Filas fit PERFECTLY... looking at them i actually thought they'd be tight but as soon as I put them on my feet, they are no different (width, and say length) then my other sneakers. The thing that shocked me is how LIGHT they feel .. .100% not complaining about these NOR my say typical Skechers ... but I was not expecting this at all. The feel under my foot ... just as comfortable, or maybe more comfortable then the sneakers I have and love. ... I am impressed.

- Price: while I have seen people say they have gotten these at Costco for $19.99 ... I got mine for $26 ... that is just above the range of "that is so silly good of a price, I cant help it".. I sort of like the look .. I love the brown "suede" part (not sure if it's real suede or whatever) and combine that with the price, I couldn't pass up trying these.

- Light: I know I said this already but i think i should say it again .. these feel light .. almost like I forgot to put my shoes ON, .. but seriously .. I am NOT complaining about this.

--------------------------------
Comments: Honestly, I would not wear these out in say sleet or snow ... or even south Florida here... heavy rain. They do not seem like the TYPE of sneaker that is suited for that. My thinking is a heavier sneaker (thinking typical Skechers I have) would be better if you have to go out in that ... or even a boot. I am not saying these will not hold up, but they just seem in my view like ones you would wear doing physical stuff outside, in say sunny conditions, but you may be active for awhile, say doing yardwork or playing sports/jogging.

Cons:

- This one may be specific to my physcial pair ... the brown suede part doesn't look as good as it does in soem of the pictures I have seen. Combine that with the fact the seller didn't put any of those cardboard pieces in where the sneaker "holds its shape" ... they looked a little funny when I opened the box. Combined TLC for the Suede part and me putting an extra piece of cardboard "inserts" that sneakers typically come with, these should do just great... but "presentation wise" they looked a little off .. .not a "deal breaker" for me though. I have to be honest ... NOT counting longevity which I cant speak for now... what I just said here is the ONLY Con I can speak of ... maybe style wise I'd change them a tad, but that is nit-picking really and not super important or worth going into more.

-------------------------------
Summary: Keep in mind I just got these and longevity is a BIG issue and I can not comment on that yet... hopefully one way or another I will come back and fill this review in on how things have gone. The thing is ... I WOULD say I recommend these , with that preference I just mentioned though.

For my first pair of Filas ever ... and as someone who has stuck to Skechers because of my bad-luck with some other brands ... Fila ... I AM impressed.

--------------------------------
Wore them a few times since the shoe-horn was placed in the front and part of the front did split (Shoe Goo'd that up) ... the shoe-horn did fix the problem and now i have no full or part of a custom insole in the right sneaker that had the issue of being tight in a VERY SPECIFIC area... yeah they shouldn't have split but ...

For the right price ... i'd consider another pair .. maybe my current ones are more of a "knock around" pair then I planned for and the new pair would be the ones I try to keep in better shape or something.

top_reviews.text:
I bought these a week prior to the event I needed them for since this style was sold out at stores like Target and such.
I have to say I love how they look, the velvety/suede material. These went perfectly with my red dress and to make it even better, they fit very comfortably as opposed to another similar pair I wore last year. I am a size 8 and the size 8 in this shoe was perfect. You'll kind of always have that slight space in the back of your heel as your foot is moving/adjusts in this type of shoe as you move but it's not bothersome.
I was satisfied with the quality and even had to briefly walk through some wet snow in them to and from the car and they survived! Granted, I wasn't looking for a super expensive brand name pair.

top_reviews.title: For all the sneaker-wearers, these are for you!
top_reviews.text:
(DISCLAIMER: This is a totally honest and unpaid review - I'm just really excited about these shoes lol):
I AM OBSESSED with these heels!! I am an incredibly clumsy person (I only ever wear heels if they're wedges, short block heels, or very RARELY if they have a platform), because I'm basically a safety hazard to myself and anyone around me lol. But these are FOUR inches tall, don't have a platform, and yet they're sturdy AF, comfortable AF, and easy AF to walk in. I have them in both black and nude, and have worn each of them out dancing 3-4 times now, and didn't fall once! No blisters, no pain, no issues at all. AND I didn't need to break them in at all.

I am prone to tendonitis and foot cramps, and I have flat feet, so these heels are basically a god send. I think I might have to add some gel inserts because the heels look like the arch may flatten out over time, but I also put a lot of pressure on the arch since I have flat feet - just something to note.

I recommend these to everyone! They're classic and chic, comfortable, and will make your legs look hottttt. Last note, I bought them in half a size smaller than usual (I wear a 7, bought 6.5) because of the previous reviews, and I'm glad I did!

top_reviews.title: Worked like a charm but, be forewarned.............
top_reviews.text: Probably the most comfortable walking and "touring" shoes I've ever worn. Walked all over the great hill towns of Northern Italy! Venice, Firenze', Bologna, Sienna, etc., etc., and all of Roma (Coliseum extended tour, Palatine Hill the Forum) and even Pompei (very difficult terrain in Pompei). I was actually surprised as my feet sometimes swell as I have type 2 diabetes (let me tell you, the walking did them a world of good), nonetheless, the description said a 5X. These are not 5X however, they are a 3X with extremely breathable and pliable material made of mesh nylon and LIGHT as a feather (which I definitely believe were their greatest attribute.) Whilst walking the bulkiness and weight of a normal shoe/athletic sneaker,... will eventually tire you, your feet, and your patience!  The Celestial Kingdom have a completely different concept of "wide" width or XXL in clothes so beware, IF you truly need a 5x these may not be for you. They are not knock 'em out, drag them around Appalachian trail shoes by any means but, under many difficult terrains in Italy, they did right by me. Frankly, I doubt I could have walked all that we needed to walk had I used my normal 3x New Balance designed as joggers or cross trainers. Buy them and try them out,...with Prime you can send them back if a you no like paisaino!!!  A capito??

top_reviews.text: These are much different than other AK styles of similar look. This is the risk of purchasing shoes online. They are much heavier in weight. It may feel good when you first put them on, but try to walk around on fluffy clouds that don't fluff back up and  are anchored by cement blocks.  That's what this shoe felt like. The heel is so heavy it would slap into my ankle bones and hurt me, and the heel  wide and low so my foot kept slipping out if it way too easily.
