top_reviews.title: Stylish and Very Comfortable
top_reviews.text: I needed some dressy shoes to wear to work, but I can't wear a traditional heel and I don't like the look of flats.  Wedges are a perfect compromise - they distribute weight much more evenly than a traditional heel and are still stylish.  Also they can be worn with multiple styles of clothing. I have another pair of Anne Klein wedges that I love, so when I saw these I had to get them. These are the most comfortable wedges I own.  I got the leopard print, and they look well made and very cute with the PU patent leather accents and the print.  The outer materials are thick and durable.  The stitching is perfect. The insoles are padded very nicely, they don't pinch or force your feet forward, and the upper heel has extra padding to keep them from rubbing or causing blisters. These shoes are extremely versatile - I have worn them all week with leggings, dresses, cropped pants, and jeans. They've been worn with zero discomfort for a full day at work.  I could jog in these if required.  Fully intending to get a pair of these in every color available!

I haven't worn many comfortable flip flops, so I had to see what all of the hype was about. So, I put them on and went out on the town=) To my surprise, they were pretty comfortable in comparison to other flip flops I've worn. They didn't hurt the tops of my feet and the bottom was very padded, so they didn't make my feet ache either. My only complaint was that the place in between my toes was a little soar the next day, when I put them back on. I would have never known this, had I not put them back on because it was between my toes. I did do a lot of walking the previous day, so I am still happy with them. I didn't have any blisters or discomfort other than that. Based on my experiences with flip flops in general, I would recommend these to other people. They're the best I've ever tried.

top_reviews.title: Good-ish, not for an actual Pro.
top_reviews.text: I assume anyone shopping for work boots like this is doing the requisite research, I certainly did mine. I had very high hopes for this boot, lots of excellent reviews, met most of my spec demands, etc.  These boots were purchased at the start of the wine grape harvest here in the Napa Valley, and now three months later I need to replace them. 12-15 hour days, six days a week for 10-12 weeks is simply too much for these boots. Being called "Mudslinger" I had hoped they would be capable of be constantly wet and covered in muck. After a few hours of exposure to water my toes were moist, and by the 8-10th hour my feet were itchy and damp. Not waterproof. Capable of being wettish maybe. The lack of actual waterproofness is most disappointing as the constant exposure to water is our biggest enemy in the winery. Now I understand the boot is not rated to be exposed to corrosive material and as such I chose a boot that was mostly synthetic and had a large toecap of rubberish stuff. The boot handled Peroxy Carb, Paracetic Acid, Citric/Tartaric acids, Caustic soda, alcohol, acetone, chlorine and salt rather well. The leather began to crack and deteriorate after about 7-8 weeks, but this was mainly due to the boot being wet and then dry and then wet again constantly. I like the lack of rivet eyelets. I like the neoprene liner. I like the grippy sole and rigidity, although being on my feet for a constant 12 hours has really worn the rubber down. I like the electrical protection. I like the spot mid sole that is deep for standing on ladders/bars/poles/branches whatever. The steel toe was excellent. I bought a 14 wide and still the toe box wasnt wide enough. I dealt with it. I have dealt with poor fitting shoes my whole life, why start now. I like the look of the boot and its lightness. I would not purchase these or any other Timberland Pro boot for work. They lack the toughness and genuine waterproofing a true "pro" needs. But for a scant over $100, barely surviving a harvest isnt terrible. Purchase if you don't actually get your feet really wet.

top_reviews.title: Waterproof breathable steel toe
top_reviews.text: These boots have everything I need in a workboot; waterproof but breathable and steel toe. They won't last as long as quality all leather boots but my feet sweat like crazy and I need boots with ventilation. To put in perspective in my Timberland Pro leather boots my socks are soaked with sweat in about 2 hrs of moderate work at 70 F and with the Mudslingers I can go 4-5 hrs without swampy trench-foot. These are not good cold-weather boots though due to the steel toe, it sucks the heat right out of my toes. I go with a composite-toe boot for winter. Great 3-season boot for the price though!

top_reviews.title: Good Boots for the Price
top_reviews.text:
Good boots. I've had them for a couple months now, and I must say I'm impressed. Quality is good, fit was good, and I can wear them all day with no blisters. The steel toe is a very nice touch, even though I primarily use them for hiking. Even with the steel toe, they aren't very heavy. They are completely waterproof. I tested it thoroughly in a mile and a half river walk, and the only times I got wet was when it was deeper than the boot.

The only reason I give it a 4/5 is because putting them on and taking them off can be a real pain. You have to loosen the shoe lace almost half way to the toe to get enough clearance to get your foot in it. And even then, it can be a little painful getting them on as you have to scrap your heel and ankle across the back of the boot. Also, the rim on the top is a little stiff, and lacking in padding, but that doesn't make to big a difference except when putting the boots on. It doesn't bother me a whole lot when I'm on the trail. And hey, for only $90, its hard to complain too much.

All in all, 4/5. Good boots for not a whole lot of cash.

top_reviews.title: What I've been looking for, for so long
top_reviews.text: These are the best slippers. I don't like the fluffy slippers with lots of decorations. I also wanted a soft sole so I don't clunk around. I believe in the whole indoor/outdoor slipper thing these days - shoes for outside, slippers for inside. I'm just a straight up, plain, but durable and comfortable slipper girl. I've tried Acorn,  Hafflinger, and a million others, but I've finally found what I've been looking for in the Glerups and I'll never go back. They are true to size always - I'm always a Ero 37, and that's what I got - perfect. They're warm without making my feet sweat. The shoe style is great if your worried about them slipping off your feet, although I will try the mules for ease of getting them off and on quickly.

top_reviews.title: Best slippers ever
top_reviews.text:
So far, so good! These are crazy comfortable, super light weight, and very quiet. I live on the upper floor, so I try not to stomp around too much. Other slippers bother me because they clunk with every foot step.

The height on these bothers my ankle a bit, but it was easy to stretch the fabric away from my bone. I just stretch it in to shape whenever it bothers me. I've given a 4 star rating for that reason.

I'm really excited to try these out when it's -25F outside, thus making it a comfortable -10 inside. So far, so good. I have reynaud's, so having cold feet is just my normal existence, but I've had warm feet since buying these.

From someone who loathes socks and finds any excuse to be barefoot, I look forward to wearing these every day.

**Edit**

Over a year later and daily use, these are holding up so well. They're perfect! Fun fact for you Reynaud's folk: make sure your feet are warm before putting these on, then they'll stay warm.

top_reviews.title: These are the most amazing things I’ve ever put on my feet!
top_reviews.text:
I can’t begin to say enough about this product! I work from home and have been looking for a good house shoe for a while. I stumbled across these Glerups (I opted for the shoes) quite by accident, and at first I was hesitant to spend so much on a slipper. But something g about the way they looked kept drawing me to them. I finally took the plunge and bought my first pair. Now I wear a size 14 wide, and finding anything g to fit my feet is always a challenge. The Glerups came 2 days later, and the second I slipped my feet in I knew I had found something truly special. I can’t begin to describe how comfortable they are. They fit perfectly! And I must say I prefer wearing them even to being barefoot. I will be buying a pair for boots as soon as I can!

Some notes:
- I went with the leather bottom shoe. I don’t ever plan on wearing these outside, so I didn’t see a need for the runner sole
- My whole house is hardwood floors, and the leather soles offer a nice grip. They are not slippery at all
- The very first time I put them on I struggled a bit to fit my foot into the opening. With a slight amount of work my feet finally got in. After just a short time of walking around the opening loosened up enough that it is now a breeze to slip them on and off
- YES they do shed, but only minimally. After each use I typically find a tuft of wool around the heel and sometimes another tuft inside up by the toe box. Simply remove with your hand and toss away.

top_reviews.title: Minimalist Sophistication
top_reviews.text: Pricey, simplistic slipper. You get exactly what you see, They are comfortable. No itchiness that some wool products create. Some people have mentioned they have no arch support, which is true. The snugness of the slipper does provide a bit of support. I have veryr high arches that require support; these slippers are acceptable for morning and evening wear.  They have a minimalist sophistication with quality construction. I never leave them alone on the floor. My dog has a true fascination for them.

top_reviews.title: Almost Perfect
top_reviews.text: These fit my low-volume foot with lots of wiggle room.  This is not a bad thing, it makes them extremely comfortable.  If they fit a little bit better volume-wise, they would be absolutely perfect.  The wool keeps my feet at the right temperature and without making them sweaty.  I have finally found my almost-perfect Winter house shoe. I wear a US size 12.5 in most shoes and the 46 fits well, a 47 was way too large.

top_reviews.title: Stylish, comfortable, and humane
top_reviews.text:
I really love wearing natural fibers, so I used to wear UGGs. They were comfortable, but not very stylish and I didn't like that a sheep had to die for my footwear. I decided to look for some less brutal slippers. I found these. They are so comfortable, I never want to take them off. I find myself reluctant to take the garbage out, go for a walk, or even go to bed because I don't want to take these slippers off.

They're as soft as cashmere and always the right temperature. And stylish - my feet no longer look like giant marshmallows!

I normally wear a size 41 AA or 40. The 40 slipper fits me perfectly.

top_reviews.title: Best Slipper I've Ever Worn
top_reviews.text: I am totally in love with my Glerups! The first pair I ordered were too big. A return and re-order in a the next size down did the trick. They fit well and  are very comfortable and warm without make making my feet sweat. I do not wear these with socks and love  the feel of the soft wool on my feet! The workmanship is superb. I can't say enough good things about these slippers! I will be a lifelong fan of Glerups.

top_reviews.title: Very Comfortable
top_reviews.text:
These shoes fit great (BUT SEE note below), they are extremely comfortable, and they appear to be well made. I also like the style. As I was shopping for a pair of navy Skechers, I came across these shoes. They are are less than half the price of the Skechers I was planning to buy, but I was hesitant to take a chance on these because I own several pair of Skechers and I've been pleased with all of them. After a few weeks of thinking about it, I decided to give these a try.

Based on the note in the description for these shoes, I ordered them in my normal size 12. The size 12 DID NOT FIT, with my toe poking painfully against the tip of shoe. I returned them and ordered a size 13. The size 13 is just a tad bit large for my size 12 feet, but they are more than snug enough and extremely comfortable - even more comfortable than my Skechers. I was so pleased that I purchased another pair in a different color. I've been let down by unfamiliar brands in the past, but I'm am glad I took a chance on these.

top_reviews.title: These shoes are awesome
top_reviews.text:
I've been pretty much exclusively wearing these shoes for a couple months now and I must say, whoever went to the future and sent these shoes back definitely changed the course of human history for the better...we salute you.

I wear 10.5 normally and got these in 10.5. When I first put them on I thought they felt loose and figured they'd unintentionally come off during use but then I started running around in them and realized that this wasn't the case. I've used them to run in the park as well as on the treadmill and regularly play racquetball in them and have no problems whatsoever.

Once in a while when I feel like exploring what the stoneage was like and I wear sneakers with laces I realize that the laces tend to either feel a bit too loose or a bit too tight. These on the other hand fit just right like they were handmade by Goldilocks herself.

I also like how quickly I can don and doff them. You know when you hit snooze 1 too many times and then you panic and try to rush your entire morning routine just to run out of time as you are tying your mesozoic shoes? That never happens with these. In fact, with the time I saved by not having to perform shoelace management, in the just 2.5 months of owning these, I've managed to explore 2 new cities, exercise more (leading to much weight loss), grow a new set of facial hair, learn the best cranberry pie recipe, write this review, and develop an appreciation for classical electronica.

The one downside to this type of sneaker as opposed to their neolithic laced counterparts is that these are less adaptable to different socks. If I wear socks that are too thin, I can tell. Likewise I can't wear socks that are thicker if I'm looking for extra warmth--but that's not the niche these shoes are supposed to fill anyway so that would be my fault for trying. In a sense these shoes work best if all your socks are identical but that's kind of another time saver because who needs to spend time matching socks when they only have one type?

All in all, I'd say, at least give these shoes a try. At worst, the price isn't bad.

top_reviews.title: What a surprise!
top_reviews.text:
I have regularly spent $125.00-$150.00 on shoes for trail running, hiking, and work. At about a 6 month life span I'm starting to have a hard time justifying the price of a pair of shoes especially for work. Through years of running I've messed up my IT band and have always thought it necessary to have expensive shoes to compensate. I've been trying to save money on work shoes by experimenting with cheaper shoes. I bought these based on reviews and figured if they were bad I'd just use them in my home while working out.

At first glance they reminded me of my water socks I use for kayaking. They looked very cheap and came in a sealed plastic bag, not a box. How's that for first impressions?

Let me make this very clear these shoes are made of a transparent mesh. I've always worn black socks . Black socks with the black shoes look very stylish and solid. These shoes are extremely light, like cheap flip flops light. After two weeks of wear my IT band is not bothering me. The last cheap shoes (Sketchers) I bought I could barely walk without discomfort. Oddly enough my Sketchers cost twice as much. I average 3+ miles of walking a day at work. Because of the breathrability of these shoes my feet don't sweat or stink like they usually do. I love the soles on these shoes they remind me of the flexibility of 5 finger shoes when walking.

I do not like that the white shoe's size label on each shoe shows through the shoe's mesh material. It's kind of glued/stiched on so there is no way to remove them.
The soles are very grippy on smooth surfaces, and give your feet a lit of extra flexibility you won't find in sneakers. It's almost like being barefoot with extra padding under your feet. Not the thin kind of padding on flipflops. I have larger feet and normally inexpensive shoes make me sound like I am stomping when I walk. I feel like a Ninja wearing, these my foot steps are very quiet. Another plus! *UPDATE* A few more weeks in they have started squeaking some, the performance has not been affected.

These are my new every day work shoes at least for the summer. I'm not sure having them in the winter would be a good idea. If they hold up 6 months I'll be buying more.

top_reviews.title: Naot shoes saved my life!

Naot shoes saved my life! I have narrow feet and the adjustable Velcro strap is perfect to make the shoes fit comfortably. The true test was when I spent 4 days at a trade show, standing behind a booth for 10 hours, and then walking all around the city of Tucson to visit other venues. Amazingly, my feet barely hurt after all of this time and I was able to immediately return to my teaching job without pain. This Motu Mary Jane pair were the ones I wore, which lasted 2 1/2 years of daily standing and an average of 10,000 steps at least 4 days a week. I recently bought my second identical pair and plan to stick with Naot shoes because they not only saved my feet, but there are also many cute styles.

top_reviews.title: GT 2000 2 improvements over GT 2000 exactly as ASICS describes
top_reviews.text:
POSITIVE: This is my first pair of GT 2000 2's after wearing 2 pairs of GT 2000s. I had worn the Gel Culumlus series for years before they were updated in a way my feet just did not like, so I've been wary of recent ASICS updates. However, the updates for the GT 2000 2 have proven to be (after a week of breaking in and two short runs) exactly what the company described: they are a bit more supportive at the mid-sole and feel a little lighter. They still have the wide toe box and narrow-to-medium heel that make them perfect for runners with broad forefeet who want firmess at the achilles tendon and ankle. I had let my previous pair get too worn out, to the point of overpronation creeping back into my form. On my very first run in my new shoes, I could immediately feel the improvement as the shoes much more effectively guided my feet into a better position and provided great support exactly where I need it. I wear custom orthotics, though, so take that praise with a grain or two of salt.

NEGATIVE: I would rate these 5 stars except for a quality control problem on ASICS' part. I ordered the shoes in my usual size, and received one shoe of that size and one shoe that was 1.5 sizes smaller. In the same box, which was labeled with the size I ordered. Minus one to ASICS for not catching that error during the manufacturing and packaging process. Amazon, of course, shipped a new pair right away. I received them the next day, which was a nice touch, considering the error was not on Amazon's part.

top_reviews.text: So uncomfortable I thought I was going to cry or scream in public. The tongue irritated my big toe joint to the point of sheer agony. Went running in these for and hour and a half- came back with blisters on the ends of my toes and a bruise on my toe joint. Toe box is cramped. Not enough support ANYWHERE on this shoe. Unbearable.

top_reviews.title: Uncomfortable for this runner
top_reviews.text: I typically wear the Kayano series, last one's the Kayano 20.  These were as close as I could get and were supposed to be of the same support style I needed.  I ran in them twice and felt very uncomfortable each time.  The last couple of night even walking was a torture.  I would take them off and my feet would ache unbelievably.  Everything from my hips down was sore and I felt like I had been hit on the bottom of my feet.  I am not sure why this alternative to the Kayano was so unbelievably painful to wear but they were definitely not what I expected at all.  I am a very small size, I typically wear a kid's size 2, so for me it is difficult to find a good stability shoe that fits small enough for me to run in.  I will not buy this style series again.

top_reviews.title: Best running shoe ever
top_reviews.text:
My last pair I wore for a year and ran 1155 miles in them. I normally would switch to a new pair after 300-400 miles of use, but my feet never got sore (which would have told me the shoe was breaking down), so I forgot all about how long I had been using them.
I hope Asics doesn't discontinue this shoe- it's a winner!
I have very narrow heels/feet, and the size 10 medium width with a sport-weight sock, plus orthotics for high arches (plantar fasciitis), fit my feet perfectly. I have room in the toe box so I'm not bruising my toes- my dress shoes are usually a size 8-1/2 to 9's.
Honestly, if you looked at my previous pair, you wouldn't know they had that many miles on them- they really held up well.

top_reviews.title: Fantastic so far
top_reviews.text: I am loyal to Asics for many reasons. They stand the test of time and give most athletes the perfect support for any foot and ankle problems. They are also better for runners in preventing knee pain. I know they tend to run small but as long as you order the correct size with this in mind you will be happy. The only con with this model is that it runs more narrow than usual.  I will say that it is something I got used to quickly and liked after a few uses. You might want to order 1 1/2 sizes bigger than your usual shoe size. My last pair was a size 9 but I added professional molded inserts. They fit perfectly. I typically wear 7.5 in any other shoe. This particular model I ordered in 8.5 because I wanted to try them without the inserts. There is a little too much empty toe space in my 9. I haven't owned these too long so I can't yet say how they hold up or feel when running but have done plenty of walking and they felt great. A little pep in your step is guaranteed. I feel that it was a great buy. Always fantastic quality !

top_reviews.title: Lining in back much thinner - hole after only 8 weeks of light wear
top_reviews.text: Not sure what changed, but I've been an Asics wearer for the last 15 years.  This pair has significantly less padding on the back of the shoe and a hard, rigid plastic cup to go around the heel.  After only 8 weeks, they already have a HUGE hole in the back of the shoe where my heel hits the plastic shell!  This has also caused my heel to bleed on multiple occasions.  This might cause me to go look for another brand - after 15 years of buying 2-3 pairs a year.  Ugh.  Not cool.

top_reviews.title: Almost perfect
top_reviews.text:
I love these shoes and they are close to perfect! Originally gave them 4/5 because there was a little spot where the sole appeared to be separating from the upper, but after several months of heavy use they are basically still as good as new.

I have some ankle issues and tight calves, so I thought barefoot shoes might help me strengthen the ankle muscles and allow my calves to stretch without a chunky heel. So far, they seem to be helping. I was initially concerned about stability, since one of my feet kind of collapses (overpronates) and this shoe doesn't really have arches, but honestly I have way less knee and ankle pain wearing these than a typical shoe. The zero drop is awesome.

The toe box is pretty roomy (more roomy than they need to be for my narrow feet, but still comfy) and the heel is snug. I've been wearing these hiking on dry (and sometines rainy) days in the PNW with no problems and I wear them to class every day as well. I wear size 7.5 in most shoes, and these were true to size.

The rubber sole is somewhat asymmetrical, meaning one shoe has slightly more coverage than the other on the toe. Kind of weird, but not a big issue. They really do fit like gloves. The arch area hugs my foot nicely and it barely feels like I'm wearing shoes. The only thing that keeps them from being perfect trail shoes in my mind is the lack of tread and the low ankle (which allows lots of dirt, rocks, and leaves to get in). I would love to see a shoe like this with a neoprene sock built in.

Compared to vivobarefoot's magna trail shoes, these are way nicer and comfortable. The vivobarefoots are wide and clunky, while the merrells are form fitting.

top_reviews.title: Vapor Glove 3 for rainy days!
top_reviews.text: If you wear thin sock liners with the regular vapor gloves and walk into wet grass or light rain you have wet feet & socks. These shoes give good water resistance with the great vapor glove feel.  They are  slightly  more stiff than regular vapor gloves.  Fit is like regular vapor gloves but with a short break in period associated with leather shoes.  As with any barefoot shoe,  your feet need to have time to strengthen if you  have not conditioned your feet to feel the ground of barefoot or near barefoot movement. My feet changed + 1 & 1/2 size over 2 years after donating all my support shoes which were destroying my vertebra, hips  and  meniscus knee cartilage.  I need B width (narrow) so need  to buy women's size so to fit properly.  Color choices can range to a bit colorful for  guys. Women needing wide shoes need to buy men's size (more like D) width and  will get more dull color choices and get less "cute shoes" comments from other women looking at your shoes.  I got generic gray color and like a lot!

top_reviews.title: Great looking and very comfortable
top_reviews.text: I just ordered two more pairs of these shoes, just in case Merrell decides to “improve” on them in their next version.  These are every bit as comfortable as my old barefoot Pacer Gloves, but they have a slightly thicker sole and a bit more support. I barely gave mine a break-in period, then wore them on a garden tour in Europe, on lots of wet, uneven ground.  They had lots of grip, kept out the rain and cleaned up easily with a bit of rubbing from a washcloth.  Best of all for travel, they don’t scream “gym shoes.”  With the natural colored rubber toe cap, they have this slightly retro soft oxford look that you can dress up or down.  Except for a couple of fancier occasions I wore mine right through dinner

top_reviews.title: You need these in your wardrobe!
top_reviews.text: These are my absolutely favorite shoes right now! I’ve owned several Merrell barefoot style shoes over the last several years and these are just amazing! The leather uppers keep some structure to the shoe while the soles allow you to feel what you’re doing. These are the absolute perfect balance of minimalist and still look great with everything! They look like street shoes, but feel like socks with a sole! Will definitely be buying more of these in other colors! I’ve been a loyal Merrell customer for over 6 years now and basically only wear Merrells until they start to fall apart! The only concern I’ve had with these is the black inside the upper of the shoe transfers onto your socks, but I love these so much and how comfortable they are that I’ve decided I don’t care. I hate wearing anything that isn’t a minimalist shoe, and these have been just incredible! If you’ve had the Vapor Glove 1 or Vapor Glove 2, you know some of the ways the sole doesn’t offer the right support and how the toe doesn’t quite hit right on top. The VG3 has finally solved that, and the leather upper of these has made the VG3 absolute perfection!

top_reviews.title: Can't Decide
top_reviews.text: The middle of the shoe is too narrow, the top of my left foot started hurting like mad when I first got them. They would work with a wider tongue space and longer laces. The toe box is just wide enough, but definitely tighter than I expected (I have just had a fourth baby and I have spent most of the last several years barefoot or in sandles, so my feet are wider than average all around). I have been wearing these  around the house for 3 days with 2 pairs of socks to help break in the leather. The pain went away but they still feel too tight around the middle and rub the top of my foot the wrong way. I have the laces so loose (and they are short at that), I can't tie them at all, I just tuck the ends in. I want these to work because they are the best looking, neutral colored, relatively affordable, minimal leather shoes I can find. I am going to order a half size up and see if that helps. I wish they offered these in wide sizes or smaller sizes in the mens version. I hope they broaden the tongue in future versions. A more finished leather that would hold up to wet weather would be nice. Will update when I try the half size up.

top_reviews.title: Most Comfortable Shoes I've Ever Worn
top_reviews.text:
My feet crave a "bare foot" feel shoe for my active job as a grocery stock clerk.

It's important that my feet and toes can move, flex, and do the complex work they are intended to do -- to provide agility and natural stability as I move quickly through a night of stocking shelves.

These shoes exceeded my expectations -- they are incredibly light weight, have surprisingly perfect arch support, a roomy toe box, and super low soles and they fit like absolute gloves. I truly feel like I'm running around the store in my stocking feet!

I was so pleased with these shoes that after one week of wear I ordered a second pair in another color.

After wearing other models of Merrells, as well as various Keens, Sketchers, and North Face shoes, I can definitely say that Merrell Women's Vapor Glove 3 Luna Leather shoes are, hands down, the most comfortable shoes I've ever worn!

top_reviews.title: Light and fast
top_reviews.text:
I bought these a half size down, as I have learned to do with racing shoes, but my feet are not wide. These are much softer-soled than other flats I have worn with similarly thin mid-soles. The grip was impressive on an icey track. No hot spots, my feet felt great. They'd probably be OK up to a half marathon, although I doubt anyone will try that these days.

If you're racing a road mile, 5k or 10k, and don't want to wear carbon-plated platform shoes, this could be the way to go. They might save your ankles if the surface is a bit uneven (potholes, ridges) or if there are sharp corners on the course.

top_reviews.title: Durability still to be determined
top_reviews.text: First off, these shoes are incredibly light. In fact, the lightest running shoes made by any credible brand. They also look aesthetically pleasing and fit true to size. It's like wearing a sock with laces and grips. With that being said, I'm not sure they will hold up over time. When manufacturing such a light shoe, compromises in material choice are made to shave weight. You can't have an ultra durable shoe and it weigh 3 ounces. You have to manage expectations. If I get 100 miles out of these, I will be pleased. Keep in mind, that's 100 miles in a shoe bought specifically for race day and short interval speed training. You don't buy this shoe for marathons lol. Like others have said, 10K would be on the high end in terms of distance. Personally, I don't like the carbon plated platform junk, and they hurt my calves. I quickly returned a pair of Hoka carbon x2's before buying these. I like a mid range heel drop and positive contact on the ground. These shoes fit the bill in that department, and although the foam is thin, it's shockingly forgiving on my knees. Only issue is, if you normally require any pronation support, running in these can cause discomfort after a run. They don't claim to offer any support, and how could they at 3 ounces, but just be warned. In summary, use them for the intended purpose, which is going fast and looking good doing it!

top_reviews.title: An excellent, well insulated boot - in kids sizes!
top_reviews.text:
Let's be honest - kids boots are, for the most part, just not insulated well. 100g or 200g at most if you are lucky - and even then they are applying that rating to polyester or felt. These boots are for my 8 year old son and I went with the brand due to my own positive experience with a similar pair I have from Rocky. These boots are well made, obviously insulated with 800g of Thinsulate Ultra, have a nice toe cap to help with wear and tear and have deep tread. While it isn't quite fall yet, I am pretty confident that these boots are going to prove durable for an energetic 8 year old and, most importantly, keep his feet warm when playing outside during a cold Minnesota winter day.

Update 12/6/13 -> after the past few days of cold weather here in the Upper Midwest (the high today was about 0) I can say that these boots do the trick. After his playing outside today for a while after school I asked him how his feet and toes were - he said they were just fine. Feeling his feet proved him correct - they were warm. Additionally, they have stood up well to the normal wear and tear from his wearing them this past fall; they still look almost brand new.

Update 3/23/14 -> Still going strong! After being worn during the 'Polar Vortexes' we experienced this winter, the boots kept his feet warm. They are also continuing to hold up very well to all the wear and tear he subjects them to; they are still looking very close to "new". Have learned the following two things: 1) the boots dry fast as all the puddles lately have given him plenty of opportunities to get them wet and 2) the laces themselves didn't hold up wall that well; the fabric weave around the 'core' of the lace wore through. Replacing the laces isn't that big of an issue ($2.50 @ Target) and in no way reflects negatively on the boots themselves.

top_reviews.title: FINALLY a shoe that fits
top_reviews.text:
I've lost count of how many shoes I've tried on since toe surgery trying to find a wide shoe that is actually wider than my current normal-width shoes. I had a dozen pairs from almost as many brands, and except for Merrells, the new ones I order in "wide" even in the same brand are the EXACT SAME WIDTH! I tried a pair of Easy Spirit TravelTime mules in 10W and they were maybe a little wider than my old normal-width clogs but not quite enough for comfort (ASIN B09PQ7ZYXR). (I'm waiting for the XW to be delivered in that style.) This style in XW are almost too wide barefoot, but with a pair of socks in the winter they'll be PERFECT!!

The good: They're the expected/right size length-wise. XW is WIDE (finally). They're well-proportioned so the XW doesn't look like I'm wearing clown shoes. They have removable insoles so I can replace them with orthotics if I'm going to wear them for more than short trips. They're comfy out of the box (as advertised).

The bad: They're not that supportive, but I wasn't expecting much given the price. The fuzzy lining is thin and feels pretty cheap, not plush like my old Merrells, and doesn't extend the whole way inside the shoe. It stops and goes back to normal fabric an inch or so in from the opening. I doubt they'll keep my feet from freezing if I'm outside for long in the winter, but for short trips hopefully they'll be okay. And I'm not sure how well they'll hold up over time, but if I get a couple winters out of them for <$40 I'll be happy.

If you need a wide shoe, give these a try!

top_reviews.text: I'm happy with these shoes but it took me four pair to get it right! They're comfortable and secure. Now for the sizing drama: REI no longer carries them in the store so I couldn't go try them on in person. I'm a woman with big feet (11.5), so I usually order men's shoes. Ordered the men's 9 in black and they sent me a *women's* 9 in a totally different style. I ordered the mens 9 in a different color (exactly the same size as my old pair of chacos that were finally falling apart after 16 years) and they were too small. Then I tried the women's 12 and they were too narrow. Every time I tried to buy the MENS black 10s they showed up as WOMENS shoes when I went to the cart. Finally ordered a men's 10 in a different color, which showed up in the cart as expected, and they fit great (and held up together are exactly the same length as my old 9s) so I'm going to keep them and hopefully not have to deal with the nightmare that was getting what worked for another 20 years again (unless they don't make chacos like they used to...). top_reviews.title: The Holy Grail of sport sandals
top_reviews.text:
The Z cloud sandal by Chaco is an innovative and original design that features a SINGLE STRAP that “tunnels” through the single layer sole.
It takes some attention to detail and time to adjust the strap properly for your foot, and initially I struggled to find a balance of firm medial arch support that didn’t pinch in the small toes. But with practice and persistent, I have this sandal figured out.
It is a brilliant idea. I remember casually talking with my younger brother about designing a single strap sandal but wondered if it was really possible to come up with a system that would work.
Well, the Chaco design team has done it.

And here is the icing on the cake:
I am flat footed as a goose.
After using these sandals for about two weeks, my ankles and arches are actually improving, even when I walk or stand in my bare feet.
BRAVO to the Chaco design team and thank you to the manufacturers. I am recommending these sandals to my brother and people I know.

top_reviews.title: Best shoes for problem feet
top_reviews.text:
After having surgery on an unrelated part a year-and-a-half ago, I developed chronic cuboid syndrome in one of my feet. As long as I keep my foot wrapped or in a bracelet 24/7, I can function well, but extended exercise, especially walking or running, caused me significant discomfort until I found these shoes. I tried multiple other brands of running shoes, spending hundreds and hundreds of dollars, but no other athletic shoes supported my problem foot the way these Adidas shoes have.

These shoes are lightweight, yet have tons of padding/cushioning, are comfortable for my average-width feet, and flexible enough that my wrapped/braced foot fits in the shoe with no pinching.

It fits half size smaller than the size you get so make sure you buy a size up upon purchasing. I wore them for 5 hours on my feet most the time while at work today on 9.28 to try to stretch them out but they stayed feeling a but snug at the toes. It is very comfortable to walk in at least and I was able to stay on my feet for half the day, even tho it bothered my big toe. The plus side is that it is great for all day wear & no after fatigue on the feet! Which I am pleased with, minus the toes feeling squished. I will return this purchase for a size up for the ones I need since I love how these shoes overall feel for all day wear as I am constantly on my feet at work.

Update 4.28.2020
My husband & I looked up the shoes authenticity & they are ADIDAS AUTHENTIC!! No knock offs!

I had a lot of top of foot pain also after rides. I have a 11/11.5 women’s foot and finding shoes is TOUGH. I bought these in women’s 11 and am happy to say they are perfect! My feet can breathe much easier, and no more pain after a ride. These shoes have eliminated all the issues I was having and my feet don’t feel so cramped.

top_reviews.title: Best shoe for Cycling!
top_reviews.text: I recently got a Peloton as well as their cycling shoes.  They were incredibly uncomfortable for me so I went on a mission to find a better pair.  I ordered the Nike Super Rep cycling shoes and these Tommaso options (in the dark gray with pink laces) with the delta clips.  I had the same issue with the Nike shoe that I did with Peloton’s: the shoe was rubbing against my inner ankle bones while peddling.  Luckily, I did not have that issue with these Tommaso shoes - these fit perfectly!  They’re lightweight and super cute, but above all, they are incredibly comfortable.  I’m a ladies size 10US and the size 41 option fit perfectly.  I’m so glad that I found these!

top_reviews.title: For the peloton
top_reviews.text: These are lovely. They are so much more comfortable than the Peloton-branded shoes, which I had been using before this purchase (way too narrow for my wide feet). It’s also way, WAY easier to clip in and out with these shoes. Like, a night and day difference compared to my old shoes.

top_reviews.title: Great cycling shoe
top_reviews.text: Highly recommend these cycling shoes. Much more comfortable than the Peloton shoes.  These have a little more room in the toe box, and the lacing system provides equal pressure distribution so there are no pressure points on the top of your foot. The insole is removable so I was able to install my custom orthotics. Also great value as they come with the delta clips already attached.

top_reviews.title: Perfect replacement for Peloton shoes
top_reviews.text:
I have wider feet - I usually can get away with most normal width shoes, but when a shoe runs a little narrow, I definitely feel it. I wear a size 9 almost universally. There are few shoes that I have to size up or down in. So, when I got my Peloton and peloton shoes, I went with the normal size I would wear in running shoes (my outdoor cycling shoes w/ SPD clips are size 9). My peloton shoes were tight at first, and I honestly thought they would break in (not a chance, as I found out). I fought thru it, but found myself using my peloton less because of how bad my feet hurt.

Decided to get the Tomimaso shoes w/ the delta clips. I was nervous that they wouldn’t fit right, feel cheap, or not work w/ my bike. Well, these shoes are literally perfect. My feet feel great (toe box is roomy) and the clips worked perfectly (ones that came with it). I got my usual size (9) and have no complaints.

I highly recommend these shoes if your current peloton shoes are not comfortable enough.

top_reviews.title: Irresponsible Ecco...why don't you care?
top_reviews.text:
I purchased these sandals from a small family-owned shoe store, while visiting relatives in Utah for just a few days... They felt comfortable while wearing them in the store, but I soon learned that after wearing for more than 5 minutes at a time that they would wear the skin off my pinky toes and the inside of my feet near my big toes causing a good deal of bleeding. I was in town for a funeral so I did not have time to return these shoes to the store while visiting. I thought that echo would have no problem taking these shoes back and replacing them with a pair that did not make my feet bleed... This was not the case. I contacted them several times politely explaining the situation. They did not offer to replace the shoes exchange the shoes or return the money I had spent on the shoes.
The only thing that echo offered me was the opportunity to pay the cost of shipping and handling, so that they may inspect the shoes and decide whether or not they were defective...
Now, to me....and I think that a lot of people would agree with me on this...shoes or sandals which make feet bleed are bad. If I were a footwear company, I would have been embarrassed, apologetic and felt a responsibility to resolve the situation to make my customer happy.... especially since these sandals are very expensive, given the materials that they are made from ($2 per pair production cost at most?).
When I told them that I was unhappy with the option of paying more money in relation to these sandals, just to have them inspected... With no promise of reimbursement of any kind... Their most recent email states that they will do nothing for me.

Ecco, you have hurt my feet, my wallet and my ability to trust that people will do the right thing.

I am a goat farmer, this is the most I have spent on a pair of sandals in years.... And I am so disappointed by the situation.

top_reviews.title: Disappointed, sort of.
top_reviews.text:
I really wanted to like these, they are a higher-end brand and at the time they were selling it at an amazing price because it was getting discontinued, but I ended up returning them.

First, some context: we were going on a vacation and wanted some water shoes that would hold up to tidepools and hiking in similar wet rocky environments. We don't anticipate using them that often in the long run, so longevity/durability was secondary. We bought a bunch of different pairs to compare, but unfortunately, you can't really "test" them out in the real-world conditions they were designed for if you're planning on returning the ones you don't like. So I could only judge them on how well they fit and their grip on our bare floor at home.

Out of maybe 5 or so different pairs of water shoes we tried, the Merrells, surprisingly, were about next to last in terms of grippiness. And believe me, I still wanted to get these because I figured it will last longer than an off-brand, as it definitely looked and felt the highest quality of the ones we tried out. But since we probably won't be using these very often, the most important factor was being as safe as possible from my clumsy self, i.e. the grip factor.

When I took a closer look to figure out how a well-known brand could actually be more slippery than made-in-China knockoffs, one thing that set this apart was the very thin layer of "velvet" - or something like it - on the bottom of the shoe. I attached a picture showing where the "regular" water shoe sole material ends and this velveteen-like layer begins, circled in red. It was this material that caused the shoe to slide easily on a bare wooden floor, an effect similar to felt pads one might apply to the underside of chair legs. This seems completely counter-intuitive, so I can only think that perhaps this layer actually has superior grip when on wet rocks? Who knows. I wasn't really willing to risk damaging them if I was considering returning them.

I would definitely consider these if you think you may need water shoes on a regular basis and therefore need something that can take a beating over time. Obviously I didn't test it for that long, but it just felt better made than no-name brands, and it was also noticeably lighter. I bet it dries faster too. But if you want something basic for only occasional use, I think it's overkill, and possibly may not even provide better grip. By the way, I tried to look up information about this material and came up empty. I didn't see it on any of the other pairs we tried.

My only complaint is that you can't tighten the middle and lower straps enough. I ordered 9M in denim blue-- so pretty. The length is perfect but I'd like them more snug around the ball of my foot and my toes, and I actually have kind of wide feet.

Oh, the fabric of the foot bed is so soft and comfy too. I'll update in after a few months wear.

Update 5/10/22: Today was my first time wearing these on my big shopping & errand day. Usually my feet hurt so bad when I get home all I can think about is getting off my feet and soaking them, but they only hurt a little. I'm definitely getting another pair of EO sandals as soon as I can afford it!

top_reviews.title: Look Like A Causal Shoe, Wear More Like A Slipper
top_reviews.text:
Product: isotoner Women's Slip-on Casual Loafer

I’ve worn Isotoner slippers off and on for decades now. I’ve always associated them with comfortable, cushy slippers. I wanted to love these casual shoe/slipper hybrid, but while they are okay, they didn’t meet my expectations in some areas.

They are very cute and the design makes them work with many different types of apparel. I really liked the way they looked from the beginning. I had visions of wearing something comfortable like a slipper but not looking like a slipper.

Since I wear a half size, I ordered the full size up. It was small for me. While I can wear them, it is a tight fit with my toes hitting the end of the shoe. My feet also tend to sweat in these, which I can’t stand. Wearing a sock with them really isn’t an option because of the tight fit. I finally got some thin no show socks, but it still isn’t really comfortable.

I have a lot of joint problems and need good cushioning and support, even with my slippers. I was actually pretty taken aback with the lack of cushioning in these slippers. With the proliferation of memory foam in foot apparel today, these were very much lacking. I’ve gotten cheap shoes at the big box store with more cushioning. It’s a feature that I associated with Isotoner in my mind. I’m not sure why it wasn’t designed into these slippers, especially for the price.

I also found the soles to be a bit slick. I have tile and laminate floors in the house and they just don’t grip like they should. Looking at the shoe, it doesn’t seem like it would be a problem, but it is. I’m not a spring chicken any more, and I do have to take care when wearing these.

I do wear these for brief periods of time only at home. I don’t wear them outside of the house, even to do things outside at my house. I was disappointed in these shoes, especially at a price of almost $40. I feel like I was paying for the brand but not getting the quality I expect from the brand. I’ve gotten similar shoes from Dearfoam that met my expectations better. I hope Isotoner continues to work on developing this type of shoe, because they really are great and it’s all about the comfort!

top_reviews.title: Better than trail running shoes but less support than hiking boots, decent middle of the road option
top_reviews.text:
Let preface this review by saying that I've only used this once on a 6mile hike. I went up and down slopes with elevation gain of around 1500ft. I went through some small flowing brooks that were about an inch high. Please note that I didn't trek around in snow or ice because for that, you'll definitely want hiking boots, not shoes. Otherwise, I think you'll be breaking your ankles. However, if you're hiking in some chilly weather, these would not be an bad option.

Who are these shoes for? The person who goes on a weekend trip trail hiker. A day hiker? Yes, this would be suitable as well. Up to the mountain? Hmm that's a tough sell but they're doable but I'd be worried about your ankles and traction for that kind of environment. This is better than some casual trail running shoe and I think that's what you got to remember, this is the next step up from that.

Pros:
+ waterproof
+ arch support with removable sole but the included sole is comfortable for me and I need the support
+ good bend around the toes whenever you're going up elevation
+ super lightweight

Cons:
- unfortunately because it's waterproof, it doesn't breathe very well so make sure to wear wool socks for sweating
- kind of pricey at $150 compared to other cheaper competitors that have similar WP capabilities but are only $110
- no wide option

Summary: This is the folks who like to day hike, stay in relatively dry areas with occasional pathways that traverse small streams.

top_reviews.title: Great shoe, order one size up.
top_reviews.text: These shoes are exactly what my daughter needs for the plays she's in. Bloch makes a high quality shoe, even at the entry level shoes these are. Ignore the Amazon sizing chart, it is not accurate for these shoes. I didn't realize it with the pair I first ordered for her, until they came and she tried them on. According to Amazon's shoe sizing chart (which is the one linked to these shoes), I ordered the right size (a US women's 7M), but the shoes were too small (they sent the size I ordered, so it wasn't the company's fault. I went to the Bloch website and looked at their sizing chart; it shows that the manufacturers size 7 (which is what I ordered and received), is actually a US size 6. So, we received the 7's today, they are going back tomorrow when the UPS place is open, and I just ordered the 8M's. Once she actually gets to wear them, I'll update this and let you know what she says about comfort level. My kids have had other Bloch shoes for dance classes before, so I'm not too worried.

The sole of one of the heels has come off (must have only been glued on, not nailed). There is a big hole in the heel under where the sole Used to be. These are extremely  poorly made shoes. I’m wondering if they are even truly Bloch shoes or if they are fake as you can see from the pictures that the BLOCH stamp is smudged or smearing on the bottom of the shoes. If I could, I would have given this rating zero stars. This is extremely disappointing as my daughter is in the middle of a show run and we purhased these new shoes specifically for this show so that she would have nice new shoes to perform in. BUYER BEWARE!!!

In 1949, Mr. Kihachiro Onitsuka began his athletic footwear company (Onitsuka Co., Ltd.) by manufacturing basketball shoes out of his living room in Kobe, Japan. He chose the name ASICS for his company in 1977, based on a famous Latin phrase "Anima Sana In Corpore Sano," which, when translated, expresses the ancient ideal of "A Sound Mind in a Sound Body." Taking the acronym of this phrase, ASICS was founded on the belief that the best way to create a healthy and happy lifestyle is to promote total health and fitness. Today, ASICS offers a full line of performance-driven athletic shoes and technical active sports apparel and accessories dedicated to bringing harmony to the body and soul.

top_reviews.title: Fantastic shoe, especially for the injury prone.

Lightweight, great balance, they hug the foot and keep me landing squarely. The absorbent cushioning also helped correct a little knee discomfort I felt during runs over 12km. They're equally good on both the treadmill and the road. They are not as breezy as other shoes (my Reeboks were great for letting in the breeze), but it's not like they're a sauna, either.

I bought a size larger than usual to accommodate my orthotics, and I've heard it recommended to buy a half-size larger even without adding extra support.

top_reviews.title: Left felt right, Right felt wrong
top_reviews.text:
I desired a pair of grey sneakers and love boost cushioning.

Stumbled across these and was excited about the price.

After getting them, I realized they are essentially ultraboost 20, with water resistant material and the golf sole.

Upon first inspection I was pleased with the utilitarian look mixed with youthful splashes of bright color. I also noticed a slight difference in the curve of the dark grey around the toe box on the right shoe but figured it was from sitting in packaging and would adjust once on my foot.

However, after putting them on I noticed a weird sense of overall pressure down the right side of my right foot. The left foot felt perfectly fine. I never actually even took out the knot the left shoe came with and it felt great.

I adjusted the tongue on the right shoe, re-laced the shoe twice and it either felt too tight or to relieve the pressure, felt too loose.

This is the second time I wore them thinking they just needed to be broken in. The left foot felt perfect but the right foot just felt weird. While sitting I felt like the right foot was literally pulling to the outside and i was using strength to keep the shoe flat. My foot began to feel fatigued.

I began to look at them closer and realized the right shoe was just over a quarter inch shorter between the laces and the tongue stitching. Like there is actually more fabric on the left shoe and a lack of fabric on the right shoe creating this added tension.

I concluded that the rright shoe was slightly irregular and was the likely creating the discomfort. Luckily, Amazon processed an exchange so hopefully the new ones will fit correctly.

To look at the slippers all the way around you wouldn’t think this because there are some areas where the fabric seems to be buckling or gathered, and one spot along the outer edge of one of the shoes where the fabric was not tucked under during the sewing process. The inside faux fur is very warm, and these are nice enough to wear outside or if you are making a trip to the grocery store.  If you are retired or work at home, you could wear these all day.  I don’t think the corded bow at the top was intended to be functional, but technically if you needed to tighten the slippers a bit, the cord does go all the way around the back of the slipper so you could pull the cord tighter and retie the bow.  Overall, nice comfortable slipper/shoes.

top_reviews.title: Chunky, Clunky
top_reviews.text:
These are quite chunky, heavier than I was expecting and a bit hard to put on, both because the material is tight, the entryway for the foot relatively small for a big shoe (I have size 12) and the straps for the Velcro cross straps are hard to fit in the slots they are to go through. I would not have bought these if trying on in a store.
They feel like wearing a heavy boot but sit fairly low on the ankle so they don’t provide the protection in deeper mud that a boot would. The soles are quite stiff so good for efficient riding but you wouldn’t want to walk far in them (always the trade off with bike shoes).
Once I'm finally buckled in, they ride fine and offer good power transfer to the pedals given how stiff they are.

top_reviews.text:
I work as theatre technician at a venue that does a lot of heavy lifting with stage risers and equipment. These shoes are light, breathable, and durable. 6TH MONTH UPDATE:
Shoes are still holding up really well, but the inside are starting to wear down. I discovered that the inside sole of the shoe is just a cushion insert over what I assume to be the kevlar midsole, which explains why I didn't have much of a break in period when I first started wearing them, so I may just get a new pair of inserts to replace the old ones. Another peculiar thing I've noticed is the logo in the image is different than on my shoes. These photos are what my shoe looks like after 6 months of everyday wear including kicking heavy stage risers and the like.

All things considered, I still adore these shoes, but these things are definitely something to be considered before buying them.

top_reviews.title: Great shoes, especially for the price, and a tip on getting rid of the suction squeak
top_reviews.text:
These shoes are so comfortable that I bought a second pair, a larger pair to wear with socks and a smaller pair to wear without socks. They really keep my feet aired out. I' wore my first pair on an almost daily basis for about a month without any problems except one: a squeak.

I was able to get rid of the noise pretty easily. I figured out that there is a hollow circle in the center of the sole that creates a suction on hard flooring. I took a utility knife and scraped a little of it away to get rid of the circle, and problem solved.

I also bought a pair for my son, who prefers to wear boots but likes the lightweight material and will wear them this summertime.

I do not anticipate these lasting more than a year or two simply based on the cheap poly plastic foam sole & the very thin glue lines (does not appear to be stitched/sown anywhere).
No wicked smell (multiple folks have had that issue), they kinda smell like grape nighttime cough syrup…but why in heck did I smell shoes in the first place?!?

Just my 2¢, but these shoes should really be priced between $9.99-$14.99 to truly be worth it.

**These are listed as size 14 USA/48 China, but these are NOT size 14. These are a stretchy 13…maybe a 13.5 once really stretched out over time.
Also the heel is slightly more narrow than any other shoe. (Maybe it seems that way because they are a full size smaller, I’m not sure)
It’s possible that these shoes are geared more towards dudes with smaller feet.

top_reviews.title: 5 Star Shoes that Get 2 Stars for Major Flaw.
top_reviews.text:
Let's get the good stuff out of the way on what could have been great shoes. First sizing; I have reviewed many shoes and boots from Amazon with the biggest problem being sizing either way off small, small narrow, or seldom spot on to USA sizing, to usually have to order 1 size up to get it right. These are order 1 size up to get it right shoes. I wear a USA 12W, and ordered 13 to get that. Ok with that. Let's move on.

The materials and construction is very good on lower and upper shoe. The seams are good as is the stitching. They have a nice breathable material for the top that does also seem water resistant and they have no tie shoe laces that close with a cinch clasp. As to comfort which is very important. These shoes fit well without squeeze, pinch, or any annoying rub points. So would be comfortable for long walks. Also it is a good looking shoe design if looks are important to you. All very good and relatively light for walking / hiking.

Now the bad stuff that undoes all the good. These have about the worst groove and grip patterns on the sole bottom where the rubber meets the road I have seen. In fact there is absolutely NO, NONE, ZERO, GROVES under your feet to bite the terrain of all types you walk on with these shoes. You only get a raised shallow pattern. This grip pattern is very shallow and very spread apart and WILL WEAR OUT very quickly leaving you a worthless shoe without grip that is then slippery and dangerous.

I have off the shelf $20.00 sneakers from Walmart with better and deeper tread patterns than these shoes. And when finally worn down it's time to pitch them without big money waste from low investment. Think about it this way... One of the major reasons for auto accidents according to insurance companies are bad and worn tires. Well, these hiking shoes are provided to you with almost pre-worn treads with very little left to wear out. The manufacturer needs to go back to the drawing board and design some very deep grove patterns in these shoes similar to off road SUV tires or snow tires. That will give you both the bite and grip you need for any surface, plus the longevity to get your monies worth out of these shoes because you work hard for your money and should get something good in return for it. So, no. Sorry, I like everything about these shoes except the very cheap and poorly designed soles soon to wear out and waste your money

top_reviews.title: Fast On/Off, Great Traction
top_reviews.text:
[[VIDEOID:32f7d7181bb4ea34693cd23f96f97fa3]] I am loving the no tie laces. At first, they were a bit awkward, but these are super easy to use; The more I use them the better they get. They make getting the boots on and off so much faster and feel pretty secure. Unfortunately, when tightened, the lace is too long and flops on the ground. The instructions say you can put them in the tongue pocket, but that is under the laces. Fortunately, I realized you only need to push the plastic pull dongle under the lace where the pocket begins. Once you get past the idea of putting the whole lace in there it’s easy. Don’t lift up the tightened lace, just push the lace pull dongle in. I show this in my short video. So glad I took the time to get past this short learning curve. So far, it is totally worth it.

The boots are immediately comfortable with no break-in needed. The fit is perfect, snug but not tight. Even though they are well over the ankle, they feel like comfortable beefy knock around shoes. There is plenty of padding around the ankles, and I’ve noticed no hot spots. These boots are comfortable pumping pedals while driving the car. They are super light!! My right one weighs 13.6 oz and the left one is 13.8 oz. Together that's only 1lb 11.4oz.

All of the glue welds and seams are super super clean. These look like much more expensive shoes. There has been no water leakage with copious amounts of wet. As you can see in my video, walking through a creek was great with no leakage. I tested these boots across a wet normally slippery deck and noted the outsoles were pretty grippy. It was the same in light compressed snow, where I had difficulty forcing a slide. While I don't know how long this tread will last, I do know I don't have to be nearly as careful with where I step due to its excellent traction.

These have been quite comfortable in 30°- 50°f weather. Though I have not done any vigorous hikes in them, I have been wearing them daily for the week I have had them and am very happy I grabbed them.

While they fit me fine they do seem tighter than some size 12's I have tried on before. For a hiking boot you don't want a bunch of extra room where your foot can slide around and wear into your skin. With these I can wear a pair of heavy socks but I wouldn't be able to wear 2 pairs for extra insulation if it was cold out. My only concern with these is the laces. It took me a while to figure out how to tighten them properly but once I did they seemed nice to use. But I couldn't get them as tight as I would like and I worry about their lasting strength. I might replace them with something stronger if they end up breaking.

top_reviews.title: I wear only Vionic shoes
top_reviews.text:
Since having knee replacement six years ago I wear only Vionic shoes or shoes (usually Clarks) with Vionic inserts. I chose this pair and the Splendid midi to try for fall and winter. I ordered my usual size of 9.5 Medium in black. These two pair of shoes which ran about $250 for both pair arrived packaged in a bag together. Both boxes were crushed and had to be taped back togerther to return. However, my shoes appeared to be in good condition.

When I took the Lindin shoe out of the plastic bag I was stunned to find that the inner footbed was not removeable. Over the past six years this is the first pair of shoes that have not had a removeable inner footbede. I was VERY disappointed. One of the things I depend on is a removeable footbed so that I can use it in other shoes. The shoes are very expensive and I look at these footbeds as a good investment so it can be reused. I may return these shoes for no other reason.

In regard to the footbed I will also point out that the footbed is lined with a fabric that is very light beige and is heavily textured. The light beige will be discolored easily and the textured material feels weird on a bare foot.

The shoe appears well made and I like that the elastic area is not too tight. I have bone spurs on the top of both feet but still it was not too tight. The sole flares out at the bottom and I am concerned it will cause me to trip. I have a narrow foot and found this shoe protruded outward midway the outer side of each foot. While the shoe is roomy enough to wear a thin sock I believe this will be unsightly.

Also, in regard to the arch support. In my opinion it is not as supportive as other Vionic shoes I am accustomed to wearing.

All in all, I am unsure about this shoe and whether I will keep it. I plan on trying it on in front of a mirror and deciding after seeing how it looks with slacks and skirts for fall.
UPDATE: These shoes make a noise with every step you take. Sounds like a whoosh of air with every step. Returning.

top_reviews.title: Lovely color and comfortable
top_reviews.text: I have very cold floors in the winter and I work from home so I basically live in slippers! Mine were getting pretty worn, so I went on the hunt for new slippers. I had 2 requirements: They must go up over my heel and they have to have a rubber sole in case I have to run outside really quick. These meet both of those requirements and more! The only issue I have is that I should've ordered the 6.5. I normally wear a size 6, but these are a little more snug than I would like. Other than that, they are soft, warm and comfortable! I like that they come up over my ankle to keep not only my feet warm, but my ankles as well. These are nice!

top_reviews.title: Best slippers!
top_reviews.text: These have become my favorite slippers out of all the ones I own. I had been on the hunt for a pair of slippers that actually go up the ankle to keep your ankles and heels warm, not just your feet, so once I saw these I had to order them. The insole has some nice memory foam like cushion for comfort, the outer sole is not very heavy-duty but it's stable and non-slip. These keep my feet and ankles super warm and toasty without making them sweat, I have been wearing them pretty much whenever I am in the house and I find them to be very comfortable. They are not very attractive, but I am willing to look past that given all the other positives. Also I am a size 8 and the 8-9 fit me perfectly, so if you are actually a 9 you might want to size up one more size.

top_reviews.title: Warm but a bit weird.
top_reviews.text:
Once you get these on, they are very cozy, but I must say, they are something of a struggle to get on in the first place! The fabric is warm and soft (definite plus!) but there is little to no stretch in it (which makes it hard to slip them on over your heel as there is also no zipper or other fastener to undo to make the opening larger). I could live with that okay if that was all, but in addition, the sole is very narrow for the size of the upper so you constantly feel like you are sort of slipping off and walking on the side of the slipper. (One other minor thing is that without looking at the bottom of the shoe, you can't tell right from left--they look identical except for the sole. I put them on the wrong foot twice before I figured out how to tell.)

Be advised that these run really small. I usually wear a 10 but since I have learned that shoes made in China seem to run small, I ordered an 11. Unfortunately, these run about 2 sizes too small so even with the larger size, my toes come right to the end of the slipper. Given the extra room in the box of the shoe, it doesn't make them uncomfortably tight or anything, but I could definitely use a bit more toe room. I suggest, if possible, you order at least one, possibly two sizes up from your normal size--depending upon how roomy you would like these to be.

I would like to have given these a 4-star rating, but the several minor problems taken together make 3-stars more appropriate.

top_reviews.title: Good work boots for the price.
top_reviews.text:
These fit about as expected. I'm an 11.5 E and these are slightly narrow but the length is just about right and even with enough toe-wiggle room that I can wear thicker socks and still be comfortable. The uppers/outers are all-leather and it's fairly thick and sturdy, not fashionable thinner leather. Stitching looks good and is in a strong, heavier thread weight (likely polyester thread) and everything seems pretty well put together. The soles are the typical grippy, flexible type you see on many work boots and these are a bit stiff initially but with some walking, they have eased up slightly and while they offer good support, they are increasingly comfortable. There isn't a lot of cushion inside so you may want to add an insole pad or something like it but again, these are sized with a bit of room for thicker socks; a good pair of socks should provide any additional cushion for the average wearer.

Laces and eyes are smooth and easily tied and stay that way. The uppers provide good comfort, even for my feet and I have a pronounced arch which makes the tops of my feet fairly tall. This makes boots a dicey fit but these are adjustable enough that I'm happy with them. I didn't order these for fashion, I ordered them for yardwork but if you like the rugged look, these aren't bad looking at all. With a layer of leather dressing, these should last at least a couple of seasons of steady wear. Tread is the horizontal striped kind, not a waffle pattern.

top_reviews.title: Not bad at all!!
top_reviews.text:
I just want to start by saying this review is just about first impression after unwrapping and trying them on for the first time so I won't be able to give a review as to how long the quality lasts. Also, I bought these to be worn STRICTLY in the house as I have hardwood flooring and during the winter time that can get a bit chilly for my feet and when my feet get cold I will almost surely catch a cold! Lastly, I have lived in New Jersey (-10 is the coldest I've experienced) there and now living in Southern California (45 degrees is the coldest I've experienced). So hopefully this review will help those who may be on one end of the cold spectrum or somewhere in between.

Packaging: They don't come in a box they arrive in a clear plastic bag which is inside of your typical amazon, greyish, rectangular looking packaging bag. Mine came in great shape! No damage whatsoever!

Material Quality: Great so far! The bottom of the slippers are made of a firm to hard rubber material. Inside is made of Faux fur lining which feels great! The sole feels like there might also be some memory foam underneath the faux fur lining which added some extra comfort/support for the soles of your feet.

Size: In shoes I wear a 10.5 in mens (U.S.) with an average side width. I ordered a 11-12 because I wanted to have the option to wear socks inside of these slippers if I wanted or not. I've tried wearing them barefooted on the first day and it feels great. They don't feel huge at all. Actually they felt more like an 11-11.5 worn barefooted, but that's most likely due to all the stuffing/memory foam and because they haven't been broken in yet.

Weather: As I stated early having lived in New Jersey and suffered the negative degree wind chills (-10 is the coldest I've experienced) there and now living in southern California (45 degrees is the coldest I've experienced) I would say that these (so far) would make a great winter (around the house) slippers for folks on either end of the cold spectrum or somewhere in between. Again, I bought these with the sole purpose of wearing INSIDE the house. I think the life expectancy of these would definitely be shortened by wearing these outside (especially if you're the type to drag your feet while wearing slippers when you walk *I'm guilty*).

Overall review: These are worth the try if your somebody that deals with cold feet and want to keep those bad boys as warm as possible. Oh yeah, if you're the type to get sweaty feet quickly then these may or may not be for you? They are slippers so the back of the slipper is open which could help in getting some air in there but with all the faux fur and cushioning lining the slipper your feet may still get a bit sweaty. But it's still worth a try. If it doesn't work for you then just return it. :)

top_reviews.title: Great boots so far! *Updated
top_reviews.text:
These are really well made boots. Not mass-produced glue-factory garbage commonly sold at even higher prices than this. I’m writing this on my first day wearing them. I had to stretch the ankles a bit, after that they’re like wearing sneakers. I would actually prefer slip-on boots to come a bit tight at the ankle. I would rather have to stretch them a bit than them coming looser and end up being too loose after breaking them in. I can tell by the way these are made they will likely last a long time. The soles look to be fully sewn-through and the leather is nice and thick. I can’t see any part of the uppers that isn’t real leather. This is how boots SHOULD be made.

Update, 5/6/21
So these are almost completely broken in now. I actually sent an email to the seller, Cebu about the ankle area and the person communicating with me was very gracious. He said I could wear them for a few more days and see if they break in or send them back and get a new pair. As of this morning they’re almost broken in all the way after some mink oil the first day and a few days wearing them, the ankle parts are almost a non-issue now and these boots are extremely comfortable and high-quality. I will be buying more of these in the future, I’m sure.

*Edit So, I’ve had these a bit over a year, but I haven’t worn them a whole lot, only when I can’t get away with not wearing my regular boots. I’ve realized the soles ARE glued on, just made to look like they’re sew-through. I would guess I’ve worn them for about 4 months worth of regular work days. The heel is peeling on one and they’re starting to get uncomfortable to the point I’m probably going to need new insoles. All in all, still not bad. I think the heel is just doesn’t have enough glue on that one side, a simple manufacturing oversight. You can tell by the newer pictures, though that they aren’t that worn, and I’m a supervisor so I would expect them to last longer.

top_reviews.title: Does not support my feet
top_reviews.text:
I have very weak ankles and flat feet, so finding comfortable shoes is a real chore. I have found FANTASTIC walking shoes with New Balance 928s, but they're not very appropriate for work because they're a bright white sneaker. I needed to find comfortable shoes for the office. The NBs come in black, but they're still sneakers, so I continued my search.

I found these after some extensive Google searches. They're supposed to be for people with foot problems, have lots of cushioning, are adjustable, and specifically made to use with inserts. Unfortunately, they're not working for me. This is the second day wearing them to work, and I've decided to return them.

The flap on top has velcro on both sides to make the fit "adjustable". Unfortunately, this means that I cannot get a snug fit whatever I do. I have to try to hold one side of the shoe in and quickly fasten the velcro before I gain too much slack. It never works, and the shoes are always loose even though I don't have the velcro as snug as it will go. Perhaps a better design feature would be to add an elastic insert to the flap so that you could actually stretch it and velcro to get a more snug fit.

This loose fit leads to my foot sliding around on the inside. My inserts actually slide around too. These shoes have actually caused me MORE foot pain. I assure you that I did not get too large of a size. Like I said previously, there is still uncovered velcro. If I could just pull the flap further, then I could cover all the velcro on the shoe, and make a tighter fit. However, I can't pull the flap over any further because there is no give to it. If I got a smaller sized shoe, I probably wouldn't be able to close the top flap.

top_reviews.title: I was surprised how lilight these were  They should only be for home use. Read on.
top_reviews.text:
For a steel toe boot / shoe they were very light weight. For the type of work I do now, (home) I don't have as many concerns as with my old jobs. where it seemed like every other day some dummy was dropping 50lb steel parts around me. I was always concerned with crush resistance of steel toes. A friend lost a toe to a cheap pair of steel toe boots because the edge pinched it off. Buy safety shoes according to the work you do don't try to save a couple bucks. if you work in a stamping plant buy the best If your a carpenter buy shoes made for that type of work.
The shoes seem nice "But" there is no literature that comes with them, or printed on them or on the box, zip, nothing at all no stamps or seals of safety or testing (seems a little odd). They should only be for home use.
As messed up as my feet are, I would not risk them on cheap apparel. I think the ad was stretching the interpretation what these shoes should be used for.
I'm going with four stars because they look to be good used for home chores. (I'd like to take all stars because they hint that they would be good for industrial use. Where is the OSHA stamp of approval???)
I hope that my review is helpful. I will update this review if necessary.
