top_reviews.title: A few design flaws
top_reviews.text:
Ok... I didn't expect a lot from these to be sure and I figured they'd get used in the yard and when cutting the grass etc. The fit was pretty much spot on but they run a little slim on the sides compared to some shoes. The steel toe is a bit different for me in a casual shoe vs a boot but I wanted the protection while still being comfortable in NC summer. Comfort wise they're ok but I guess I just prefer a little more support around my ankle. It's a little off putting to have all that steel over your toes and you've just got a little stretch material behind your ankle with no support. The finger loop on the back is pretty much useless with it being so small so that can make it a little tough to get that stretchy material over your heel.

They'll get used this summer for their intended purpose but not something I'd walk around in daily.

top_reviews.title: Lightweight Yet Sturdy
top_reviews.text:
I've been wearing these for winter hiking since I received them. I haven't had a chance to wear them in spring or summer weather yet so I'll only be commenting how they've done in the snow.

Out of box - These hiking boots are relatively comfortable first thing out of the box. There was no "breaking in" period in which they were uncomfortable.

Weight - These are truly lightweight and more like a trail shoe or running shoe as far as weight goes.

Water Resistant - These don't keep feet completely dry but they work well enough for winter hiking. As long as I wear wool socks with these, I have no problems with keeping my feet warm enough.

Fit - These fit just a bit bigger than I expected. However, this makes it nice for wearing a medium to thick pair of hiking socks.

Comfort - While these are comfortable right out of the box, my feet have been sore the following day when I've worn them for longer than 3 miles. I wish there was a little more arch support and foot bed support in general. My achilles gets sore in these and the only way I've been able to help with that is adding a small heel lift. I prefer my trail running shoes over these for comfort and footbed support.

Breathability - The fabric is lightweight and breathable.

One more thing to note is that the ankle support is great on these for those who want to wear them backpacking. Also, the sole has decent grip.

One lacing strap is broken and I lace my shoes loosely do there wasn't strain of any kind on the strap, and the fabric parts are beginning to rip by the arch of the foot and across the top of the foot.

I walk in my shoes: road, and trail. I don't rock scramble or do anything that beats up my shoes.

I contacted them, and their solution is for me to send these back, and then I can buy a new pair at a discount. But even with a discount, I can't see buying shoes that won't last 1000 miles. top_reviews.title: Caution upon receiving
top_reviews.text: This is not a review in regards to any seller or Amazon, but the shoe itself. I also never write reviews, but have grown so tired of this issue that I feel compelled to save someone else from the headache or wasted money. My daughter has been required to wear this type of shoe at her school for the last 7 years. After buying MULTIPLE pairs over the years, I would say almost half have had to be replaced due to having a mildew type smell. This smell is immediate upon wearing and completely random- I have learned to now recognize the faint smell now when shoe is unworn and brand new. Once worn a few weeks (and my child does not have any issue whatsoever with overly sweaty or smelly feet- never a problem with any other shoe), the smell of “mildew” becomes overwhelming.  Some purchases were made on amazon, and some locally. No rhyme or reason. When replaced because the smell is so strong that the other children in carpool complain, and I grow tired of spraying or stuffing with dryer sheets, I buy a new pair and it’s a 50/50 shot they will or won’t have this issue. It may be a chemical used in one particular factory, but the smell is ridiculous and strong enough to cause issue for my child. So buyer beware- when you buy these shoes, as crazy as it sounds- smell them. If there is ANY hint of a smell that is “off” from the usual new shoe/leather smell, exchange them! I pretty much have a garbage can full of shoes because i didn’t do this thinking it was a fluke, but this has gone on for quite a long time now. I do have a very sensitive nose, but have been told that they smell the same by many others that do not have a strong sense of smell. Utterly ridiculous how much money wasted on shoes, as they are not returnable once worn and that’s when the smell becomes overwhelming!

top_reviews.title: So tight I could barely get just one of these on
top_reviews.text:
I was thrilled to open the box for these boots given the design -- they seemed to be perfect for wearing to nice outings with a skirt or jeans, as well as practical, with a smooth mud-proof and rainproof outer surface.

Next though, I looked at how tight the upper part of the boot was, and that there was no zipper, only expanding panels and pull tabs. I began to wonder if these boots didn't look at bit tight or small.

After a battle, I was able to get one of the boots on. I didn't even try to get the second one on. I wore the socks I would typically wear on a mild winter's day -- neither very thick or very thin. The boot was so tight, it was clear that even wearing footie stockings would not solve the matter.

NOTE: I am always a size 9, if anything, sometimes I can fit in 8 1/2 women's footwear. I definitely ordered a 9, and while I can't seem to find any size labels on the inside of the uppers or the sole, the length of these boots conforms to other of my footwear, so I think these are indeed a size 9.

With that said, the toe box seems comfortable, then the bridge (midfoot or arch) gets very tight, with the ankle and calf very tight as well. I think someone with very slender feet and ankles would fit these fine, and anyone more sturdily built will need to go up a size.

top_reviews.title: Not The Same GT-2000 Series Quality
top_reviews.text: I have owned several pairs of Asics GT-2000 running shoes. Love them as they fit, are sturdy and well made. I wanted to buy another Series (4) shoe but no more to be found. The reviews for the Series (5) and (6) were not that great. So I went ahead and purchased the new Series (7). Not the same shoe anymore. See photo. Shoe on left is my old (4) and right (7). Notice the toe: old shoe vinyl is stitched; new shoe seamless fabric. Notice the laces: old shoe sturdy vinyl stitched; new shoe seamless fabric. Not sure what this 'new age' fabric is but I don't like it. It seems the old shoe was made of several parts designed and put together. The new shoe seems like one big piece of fabric that has been molded and shaped to fit. No stitches, only glue and seamless fabric. I'll keep the GT-2000 (7) they feel okay and I ran with them today. But they are not the classic GT-2000 series shoe anymore. Get used to it, Asics has reduced their material and manufacturing costs with this fabric material and they now seem like any plain old running shoe. For the price, I expected more. My last GT-2000 shoe.

top_reviews.title: Terrific Addition to the Asics GT 2000 Series
top_reviews.text: I've been wearing Asics GT 2000 running shoes for years and have always found they suited my running style and mileage very well. But after the middling-to-poor reviews that the GT 2000 6 series garnered, I was concerned: had the GT 2000 series run its course? I'm happy to report it hasn't, not at least by the evidence of the GT 2000 7. The shoes feels lighter than the previous entries in the series, but its support, especially in the heel box, is superb. The front of the shoe also does a very good and very noticeable job of distributing the force of my foot hitting the running surface. The shoe is also stylish--I bought mine in black/white--with flexible meshing around the front. I was nervous about the purchase--but I shouldn't have been. Terrific shoe.

top_reviews.title: Asics quality ended with the GT 2000-5
top_reviews.text: I have worn Asics GT-2000 brand for over a decade now. Versions 2, 3, 4 and 5 were absolutely spectacular shoes. I generally would buy the version from the previous year to save some money since there are few differences between the shoes. Until version 6 which is what I would have purchased this year. The reviews stated that the quality of version 6 was far far worse than any previous generation. So I went ahead and shelled out the $120 for the version 7 back in January. It is now just 8 months into wearing the version 7 and these are toast. All of the tread is gone and there are large flat spots all on the bottom of the shoe. These after 8 months of standard walking and jogging use look like my old version 5 pair after 18 months of the same beating. The old versions I would wear would regularly go 1.5 years before wearing out all of the tread. If these shoes only last less than half of the time the old ones did, then these shoes don't deserve to be more than $50-60. Asics, you have lost my trust and confidence. I am afraid after a decade of loyalty, your decision to get rich quick has cost you many customers, including myself. I will have to look for quality elsewhere. Shame on you.

top_reviews.title: Right for my slight over-pronation
top_reviews.text:
I bought these after several years of using the Brooks S-257, which I bought from a local company which put customers on a treadmill and video recorded their gaits, and then recommended shoes (sadly no longer in business). Since that time I have been a less-than-serious runner, but in the last 2 years decided to get more serious/consistent about running. 257's got to the point of some pain after I would run a 5K, so I decided to start looking for a replacement.

So as a complete novice, I know NOTHING about running shoes. I remember that I'm a mild over-pronator with somewhat flat feet. Time for Google.

I started out with Brooks, because after all, they lasted me several years and were comfortable (if a bit heavy). Of course my trusty 257's have since been long discontinued. So after reading a lot of comparisons and reviews, I had to decide between (previous model) Brooks Adrenaline GTS 18 (on clearance, good price), or the new model Adrenaline GTS 19. Being frugal, I figured the 18's would be the best bet (saving $40). Also ordered the ASICS Mens Gel-Cumulus 19.

The Cumulus are not great at all. They felt half broken-in after the first run, and my feet and hips were in some pain for a couple of days.. NOPE.
Next run, GTS 18. Not as bad as the Cumulus, but still had that shockey kind of tired pain in my feet after running. The pain and tired would last a day or more, so no good. Was really surprised that such a highly-rated shoe would hurt my feet and hips! So, time to bite the bullet and spend the dough-rey-me. Decided I would do my own comparison and ordered the Asics GT-2000 7 and these GTS 19.

Was excited about the "rail" in the GTS 19. Revolutionary. Awesome. Best thing since sliced bread... but not for me. They really feel fine for the first mile or so (which I run in around 7 minutes), but then fatigue begins to set in, and I really have to kinda watch my gait. By mile two still ok, but have to begin considering my steps. The shoes are feeling kinda thin. I mean... I'm getting tired, and what form I may have becomes less than professional. Have to pay attention to try to monitor each step. But.. I only have 1.1 miles left. As I draw to a finish I don't care much about my gait. I'm just dragging my tired rear-end across the finish. At this point, I'm more concerned with salvaging my time and trying to finish strong and keep that spring in my step. BUT, my feet are feeling a bit worn (no pain, just tired), and feel like I should concentrate on each step, or I might actually hurt my feet.

Also noticed that the tongue area was kind of rubbing the front of my ankle in an uncomfortable way. The shoe never really felt secure on my foot. I personally do not like tight-fitting shoes, but no matter how loose I tied them, the opening around the ankle felt stiff and kinda annoying. Like a stiff collar on a shirt. Is this really my best option?????

Yesterday I tried out the Asics GT 2000 7. I ran my second best ever time. I didn't even think much about it. My feet never hurt, I don't remember actively concentrating on how my steps were coming down. I sit here typing this the next day, and my feet or hips don't hurt at all Maybe I'm wrong, but it seems to me that the Asics are more like my classic 257's.

The GTS 19's will be going back. The Asics GT 2000 7 is really a great shoe (for me).

top_reviews.title: Tips with Pics
top_reviews.text:
Okay for all you first time
buyers or anyone who is unsure of how to buy the right size, I am a native of San Clemente which is the home of Rainbow Sandals (lived in So Cal my whole life until a couple years ago *tear, tear*). I have worn Rainbows my entire life and I can tell you that these are the best sandals you can ever purchase and the most comfortable. And they last for a long time.

That being said, for the best and most
comfortable fit when selecting a band new Rainbow sandal you want to choose one that leaves no room at back of the sandal. Basically, a sandal that is almost exactly the same size/shape of your foot give or take a centimeter or 2 on the sides and don't worry about the tightness of the straps so much, if your feet don't quite get in all the way at first - these babies stretch out ALOT. When I first buy a pair, they are very tight and my feet do not quite fit in the straps and my heel might hang off the end just a little until they are worn in. To help wear them in faster, I will wear them to the beach or pool or whenever around water and walk in the water to loosen them up.

Once these babies are worn in, they are the best and most comfortable sandal in the world... If you get properly sized.

Ps. My favorite trick (see bottom right square in photo) to stretch out the straps is to put them on and use one foot to hold down the opposite sandal at the back and lift my heel up and over my toes so that the ball of my foot digs into the sandal. I do this standing or sitting every time I wear them until they are stretched out.

Also, the reason why one of my sandals in the picture is frayed a little is because my dog kind of got to it when she was a pup going threw her crazy "let's chew on everything including the cabinets phase". As you can see, the other is still in excellent condition.
Anyway, hope this helps some people.

top_reviews.title: Fits smaller than other styles.
top_reviews.text:
I have the twisted sister and flirty braidy in the same size, (M), and color. While Rainbows generally have a painful break in, the twisted sister is worse for the first few days than the braidy. The toe strap is father back, pushing my foot back off the sandal, and leaving too much excess footbed at the toes. Also the straps are shorter, harder and tighter. Meaning I really needed to get those all the straps stretched in order to get a good fit. I added a couple comparison pics.
Though they're exactly the same length and width, the twisted sisters fit much tighter and will require more care when breaking in. Anyone with slightly thick or wide size 7 feet would be miserable in these while they broke them in. I have thin, somewhat narrow feet and I was miserable.
The GOOD: The straps actually stretched pretty quickly. After just a few days of casual wear. I got not blisters because I didn't overdo it. Then I could wear them more often and get them really broken in. They're cute, I like these, but I prefer the overall look and feel of the Flirty Braidy version. The twisted sister straps will be murder those first days. Rainbows get super soft and comfortable, so it's worth it to me.
HINT: put the flops on, get an idea of where they will rub, and then immediately put bandaids or moleskin on those areas before you ever wear them. I find the best way to break in Rainbows is just wear them, go for some long, slow walks.
Stay away from water. It ages leather no matter what.

top_reviews.title: Great shoe, break-in period not bad
top_reviews.text: When I ordered these flip flops, I was prepared to be in a significant amount of pain during the break-in period, with lots of blisters to show for it. I was pleasantly surprised when my expectations were shattered. I'm not going to lie, these were definitely a tight fit when they arrived (tight enough that they were painful, initially, and left some deep imprints on the top of my foot), but I didn't get any of the blisters that I was expecting. After the first few days of wearing them on my feet they were sufficiently stretched out that there was no longer any pain, so the break-in period really wasn't bad for me. Like I said, the straps were extremely tight when they arrived, so I just sat around with them on my feet while they stretched out. The second day I walked around the house a little (but still mostly sat), and by day three they were worn in enough that I could walk around freely in them. It's been two weeks since I got them and they are soft, comfortable, and have a really nice (light) imprint from my individual foot. There is great arch support and the foot bed is solid without feeling too stiff (if you press into it with your finger there is a little give but it's not squishy). I like that the strap is a little on the thicker side (better for walking) but still looks a little feminine with the braid. As far as size goes, I'm a 7-7.5 in most shoes and the med (6.5-7.5 I think) fit perfect. Brand new, my foot was right at the edge of the back but after a couple weeks, it seems to have stretched out a little, so don't try to size up; Get your actual size. I don't think this is an especially narrow flip flop either. I consider my foot normal to slightly wide and I have even worn narrow shoes (some flats and flip flops) that were not comfortable and I didn't have a problem with this shoe. I think it's a more normal width (maybe ever so slightly on the narrow side). Great simple looking flip flop, seems durable and made with great materials. I would definitely recommend this product. And, once again, if you aren't walking around a ton when you first get this sandal, the break-in period is really not that bad.

top_reviews.title: Not just for men!
top_reviews.text: I'm a woman and bought these for myself. I used to buy Reef's Seaside sandals until they stopped making them a year or two ago. Since then I've been on the hunt for another pair of Reefs that fits as comfortably as the Seaside ones did. I kept getting frustrated with the women's sandals because they're always too narrow and the material is never soft and cushiony enough. I took a gamble and ordered these in a men's size 7 (I usually wear a women's 8) and they were perfect! I have very little arch and these were wide enough for my (mostly flat) feet. The sole looks so much like the seaside ones I used to love. After wearing them for a few days my foot had perfectly molded into the bottom of the sandals...just how I like. Honestly, the thick strap makes them look a little more masculine than I'd like, but I'm so comfortable I just don't care!

description: Newton Distance S 9 Running Shoes A staple racer to many, including 3X Ironman World Champion Craig Alexander. This stability model of the award-winning Distance features light minimalistic overlays and dual-density foam for a high-performance feel. Ultra Breathable Mesh Upper The Newton Distance 9 running shoe is built for speed. Engineered with an ultra lightweight, ultra-breathable mesh upper the Distance 9 will have you clocking up the miles and hitting new records without feeling the heat. As cool air permeates the mesh, any uncomfortable heat build-up is removed creating a regulated temperature and a healthy environment that feet can thrive in. The new minimalistic overlays offer support without adding unnecessary bulk or weight and work in tandem with a traditional lace closure for a secure, locked down fit. The no-sew toe cap eliminates discomfort from chaffing and rubbing for a distraction-free ride. Newtonium Cushioned Midsole Featuring a full foot Newtonium cushioned midsole, cushioned lugs in the forefoot and heel provide full-foot cushioned protection, attenuating shock impact where you strike down the most alleviating stress on the joints and reducing fatigue. Working in tandem with the Newtonium cushioned midsole is the action/reaction technology providing exceptional energy return. Generated by the active movement of the cushioned lugs, the active/reactive technology creates a trampoline-like effect responding to your every step with quicker bounce-back for effective and highly responsive energy return. Constructed with a second density medial support the Distance S 9 provides a firmer medial side post to prevent overpronation during running. SHARC Outsole The Distance 9 shoes SHARC Outsole consists of a high abrasion and high-density rubber providing increased and enhanced floor fighting traction in both dry and wet conditions.

top_reviews.text: I often think requests for reviews should be extended a few months--to a year out from the purchase of a product. So many things are designed purposely to last only for a short time, to keep the wheels of capitalism well-greased. That said, I won't offer any opinion about how well these shoes hold up because I have no idea--yet.  They appear to be well-made and are light, which according to my chiro, shoes should be very flexible to allow the feet to move freely. I noticed some reviews indicate ordering your true size, but I found that not to be the case. I had to order a full size up after returning my "true size", which fit way too small.  They do have some arch support--compared to my goddaughters' Nike's and Addidas!  I did purchase inserts for additional support, but I tend to have flat feet, so that may not be necessary for those who don't.

5. The sponge is made of lower density memory foam resulting in loss in stability.
6. The toe box has smaller height.

It seems like Nike has given in to corporate greed and doesn't mind destroying its flagship products with poorly designed newer versions with only cost reduction in mind.

top_reviews.title: Cushiony Support
top_reviews.text: I have back problems as well as foot issues. I cannot walk comfortably barefooted or even in most basic slip on shoes. I needed something that not only supported my feet, provided stability, but would also be comfortable to wear all day. I am retired and was looking for a shoe to slip on in the morning and wear all day around the house, outside doing yard work or to run and errand. These shoes have definitely made a difference. From the moment I put them on my back felt better, I was able to remain standing for a greater length of time and when I went to bed my feet and legs weren't throbbing from the stress of being on my feet. I love them...now I just have to see how long they'll last.

top_reviews.title: Like a bear hug for your feet!
top_reviews.text: These are absolutely amazing! top_reviews.title: Comfortable but now smelly
top_reviews.text: I bought these shoes a little over 3 months ago. I love them and wear them constantly around the house and yard. My only drawback is that they stink after 3 months of wear. And yes, I know, they’re shoes so they’re going to stink, but these smell worse than any others. top_reviews.title: Different Than Most Shoes/Hikers From The Columbia Brand.
top_reviews.text:
I have been a HUGE fan of the Columbia brand for years! Their outdoor clothing, shoes, hikers, and more have always stood for the utmost superiority in outdoor wear over many other brands. So when I noticed these that claimed waterproofing beyond others with the navic fit that keeps the midfoot stable while locking your heel in place and maximum cushioning while keeping support and stability even if on uneven terrain? I thought perhaps perfect for my son, as ever since a sudden syndrome left him with temporary paralysis he has had a horrible time finding shoes that allow good support but with comfortable wear.

I do not know if it is the waterproofing material that is so odd, perhaps the breathable/still waterproof construction combined with this that I don't care for? But there is something different with these hikers that I just don't like.
These are incredibly lightweight, amazingly so they do not give off the secure feeling I have always felt with any Columbia purchase prior. To me, it feels almost like these are knockoffs of some sort, although I know they are the real deal. Perhaps it is my old age, being used to the use of materials that now are unneeded to provide the great outcome in hikers. Maybe being used to the heavy leather, and the thick soles associated with it before the technology has moved past the need for it? Whatever it is I am sure it's just my not being used to something lighter weight than some of my tennis shoes will take some time to adjust. The soles have a unique pattern to them, and are from an advanced tread pattern that provides a great nonslip and grip on the wettest of ground, including snow it says also!

My son says they feel odd to him also, as he is used to the hikers I referred to in a larger clunky style. But he said the stability when he attempted to use seems spot on, so again? Any presumed oddities must be simply personal idealizations with no familiarity with this better concept. I hope it will grow on my son to produce confidence in the footwear, which is indeed needed as his new normal of limited mobility has much to do with confidence within the footwear and not slipping or falling. I'm sure time will produce such.
I did and still do have trust in the brand Columbia, and I am sure it is just getting used to the "new normal" in losing the memory of what USED to be in solid footwear, and what IS now in better. Just hard to adjust to this totally progressive look and feel. But I hope after wearing them for a while, my son will feel as confident in these as he always has in his older hikers.

top_reviews.text:
I didn't expect to like these. My idea was to try them on and send them back in exchange if they were either the wrong size or made in China. Well, neither of these were the case, so I have worn them for a day.
Olu Kai is a Hawaiian company, the slippers are made in Vietnam. The fit well, and are quite comfortable. I wear them with socks as my goal is to keep my feet warm. We don't wear "outdoor" shoes in the house, and just socks or even shoes that are only worn inside the house make my feet cold. These are breathable, so my feet don't get clammy, and just have just enough insulation to keep my feet warm.
As for the size, they don't make 9 1/2 so I went with 10 and the fit is fine with socks.
The styling is a little funky: they are not sleek. pointed toe, but rather rounded and there is no taper from back to front. I'm sure this adds to the comfort. The soles are flat and their is no heel, so it is a little like walking barefoot.
Enjoy!

top_reviews.text:
First note, use the sizing chart provided in the pictures. It is accurate and I could have saved myself a little time if I did that first.

I am a size 13 with one foot that is slightly larger than the other. I originally ordered a 13 and the larger foot was just a bit cramped. I thought that with time and maybe shoe stretchers it would get bigger, but I decided instead to order a size 14. I am glad that I did. The size 14 fits me very well. After they came in, I looked at the sizing chart (which honestly I never really do) and it seemed pretty spot on.

In terms of comfort, I really like these slippers. This brand always conforms to my foot shape extremely well. I have had these for two days and I already noticed them getting even more comfortable as it shapes around my feet. Clearly I cannot comment on the long-term durability, but these feel well built and very solid.

These are pricey slippers to be sure. However, I work from home and I wanted something very comfortable that I can run out and get the mail if needed. These fit that bill so far. If I have any issues in the future, I will update the review. I have spent close to $100 on slippers before that felt 1/3 the quality these seem to me.

top_reviews.title: Wow.  The Best Pair Of Slippers Ever - For Comfort And Foot Support
top_reviews.text:
Slippers have been an endless battle for me as my feet get older and need better support without sacrificing comfort and warmth. The market is flooded with low cost slippers of both name brands and off brands and most of them lack proper foot support. I'm sorry, but memory foam is a bad choice for the soles of slippers if you have any form of foot issues. And frankly, most slippers on the market use thin memory foam which offers no support or protection of your foot.

When my new OluKai slippers arrived yesterday, I unpacked them and tried them on and whoa... are these comfortable! The term fits like a glove feels like walking on air actually applies for these slippers.

Easy to put on, yet feel like they were custom made to snuggle your foot. Great attention to detail in design, as if they actually had your foots well being in mind when they designed them.

While not inexpensive, the price is worth it as I fully expect these to last much longer than the random typical $30 slipper. So in the long run, the cost to put slippers on your foot is probably better with these.

Surprisingly light weight for the comfort and support. Some slippers are kind of clunky on your foot, but not these.

The sole inserts (which are removable and can be washed) are outstanding. Good as my support inserts I have to put in all my tennis shoes.

I love the bottom treads, as they are non-slip, non-marking, and appear very rugged yet not thick and heavy.

I cannot speak to durability yet, but just from careful inspection I can attest that the workmanship, quality of materials, and in particular the stitching is very well thought out with selected reinforcement at key areas where most slippers start to fall apart with use. I expect, since I am not really hard on slippers, these will last me years.

OluKai has a new customer in our family, as I am ordering these for my wife and daughter as well. I plan to order a pair of their sandals next, and then something from their shoe line. If they are as well designed and crafted as these slippers.. I may become an OluKai all-the-way customer.

top_reviews.title: Significantly narrower than the older Minimus shoes -  Also thick/padded heal, soft sole.
top_reviews.text:
Advertised as X-Wide, but measures a full 3/8" narrower than the older New Balance Minimus MX20v4, in same size.

I am a big fan of the New Balance minimus shoes and have owned many different models including:
many pairs of the MT10
MT20
MX007MR
MX20v4 (a favorite, durable and wide)
The first model year had sole seperation issues, but since then the only significant issue for me has been the soles wear through.

The v7 shoes are signficantly narrower than their predecessors and I was disappointed to find that the Minimus Prevail is as well. In comparison to the other Minimus models, I found it has thick heal padding and doesn't feel like a barefoot style Minimus shoe at all. Both the new Prevail (black shoe/sole) and old MX20v4 (green & grey) shown in the pictures are size 13 2E (the Prevail was "X-Wide" on Amazon but is just 2E).

As you can see in the pictures, the Prevail is nearly 15mm narrower in the toe box (too narrow for me), about 10mm wider at the heel, and has significantly thicker heel padding. With thick padding and without the fitted heel, the Prevail feels like a normal running shoe instead of a Minimus shoe.

Lastly, the Vibram sole on the new Minimus Prevail is soft - almost like a soft gum sole. I believe it will wear significantly faster than the previous Minimus models.

top_reviews.title: Different fit from the Minimus trail shoes
top_reviews.text:
I’ve been wearing the NB Minimus trail runners exclusively for years. I wanted to try some of the cross trainers so I wouldn’t be putting extra off-trail miles on my trail shoes. Some of the trail shoes have a zero drop and some have the 4mm drop. I prefer the zero drop but don’t mind the 4mm, which is what these cross trainers have. I can feel the little bit of elevation but it’s not a big deal.

What is more noticeable is the narrower toe box. These run much narrower, so I had to order these in a W(wide) to be comfortable. Even with that, I wish I had more room for my toes. Fortunately the nice flexible knit these are made from provides some give. The other thing that is different is the heel on these shoes. Maybe because they want to add stability for standing weight lifting (?) the heel is very stiff and kind of clunky. This adds noticeably to the weight of the shoes, and makes then feel a lot less nimble. All that being said, these still have that fit that hugs your heel & mid foot, and opens up in the forefoot.

Even though they’re heavier, they’re still light compared to a lot of gym shoes. The laces are nice, not too long and stay tied well. The tread has been fine so far for indoor floors and for sidewalks. There’s enough padding in the collar but not too much (minimal).

I think what won me over was how cool these shoes look. The knit is super trendy and the New Balance “N” embossed on the knit fabric looks great in a subtle silver. They look sleek but substantial. I got the black, and it looks good with gym clothes or jeans, and could probably even pull off a casual going-out look.

So I kept them and I wear them often, even though I wish they were wider in the toe box and the heel was lighter and less stiff. They’re not the perfect feel, but they’re pretty good. And they look great.

I switched to zero or minimal drop shoes about eighteen months ago, and all of my back pain has gone away! I don't think these shoes would work for me as a running shoe, but I wear them all day walking around New York City, and they were the only shoe I brought on a three week trip to Bangkok. top_reviews.title: A disappointment

I tried the Lorelai in a 7 and a 7.5. The 7 was too short and tight overall. The 7.5 was about 1/4 of an inch longer than my longest toe which is the one right next to my big toe. These shoes were also tight with a narrow fit, especially the toe box where the elastic is. The toe box was so narrow it hurt my feet. Overall the style runs small and narrow. I think these are made to wear without socks. I tried them on with a thin summer weight sock, but the  shoes were much too tight for me. I wear a medium width and I have thin feet, but this style was too tight and narrow for my feet. For those of you who wear orthotics or need cushioning, the insole is cushioned and does seem to be removeable. It also seems to offer some cushioning. It is a casual shoe. As the style is too tight snd narrow I returned all the pairs.

top_reviews.title: Inconsistent sizing issue
top_reviews.text:
I CAME BACK TO DO AN UPDATE FROM MY ORIGINAL GLOWING REVIEW

My Lorelai slip-on LUFT outsole failed in under a year - the bottom of the shoe cracked, broke and disintegrated with moderate wear on city street.

They went in the trash early in 2021 - so about 1 years use. The leather still looked great but the new Keen outsole LUFT one hundred percent failed.

Unfortunately I was so keen on the slip-ons that I went ahead and purchased the chukkas and the sneaker before I realized that the outsole was not up to Keen's previous standards.

Sadly I can report that my Lorelei chukkas, and another pair of the lace up Lorelei sneaker I purchased also now have failing outsoles.

The LUFT sole is junk. Keen - where is your quality control? That is the basis for your reputation!

In comparison my Keen Vibram sole workboots/hiking boots are going strong after many years of use.

I will no longer purchase anything by Keen without Vibram outsoles as it's a waste of money.

top_reviews.title: Runs 1/2 size too small, very comfortable once broken in
top_reviews.text:
These shoes are leather and pretty stiff at first, but it doesn't last long at all. I am a true size 8, and while I am able to wear these just fine (really, I am keeping them), I would recommend going up 1/2 size (not more IMO). They are very comfortable, but fit like a glove, and definitely will not work for wide feet. I wear them with naked feet and don't think they'd work even with no-show socks. When I first tried them on, I wasn't sure that I'd keep them. They were snug over the top of my normal width foot, and it felt like my toes were at the end, but doable. No blisters or discomfort though. After the second day wearing them, they're great. Somehow the footbed relaxes. Really comfortable footbed and padding, and much softer after only two days. I just wish that the leather was waterproof. I am already really enjoying wearing them and know that after the way they relaxed after only two days, I am confident that these will become a favorite go-to pair.

Note: I ordered the "gray" color. I'd only give this color (or the pair I received) 2 stars. The color is not really in the gray family at all. It is very much a taupe (more of a tan/brown color) ... but different from the sole of the shoe, which is actually gray. Time and again I find myself a little disappointed in the color, especially since there is such a contrast between the leather and the sole. Update: While the product page color states "gray", once you add it to your cart the color/item description displays as "London Fog" ... which I would say is accurate. The color does look like the trademark London Fog taupe/tan color.

Update: I purchased these in March. It is now October. I wear these shoes a lot! I reach for them constantly. They are so comfortable, and so very easy to slip on. I also find that they feel very secure on my feet, which is a great thing for certain activities. Although the leather is not waterproof, they dry quickly and don't have any stains or discoloration. I am considering purchasing another pair, but debating on another 8, or going up a half size to 8.5. I do still wish that the grey was really gray, and not tan/taupe.

Upgraded my review from 4 to 5 stars. I really like these shoes. They are super comfortable and I can wear them all day with no foot pain whatsoever! They have never rubbed my foot, and never had any blisters, and they still look good. (I never wear socks) Just know going in that you should probably order a half size up. I did not order up. I am a true size 8, and these are totally fine on me (after several days of breaking in), although I'm sure an 8.5 would have been fine too. Love these shoes.

top_reviews.title: Super comfortable, Reefs quality
top_reviews.text: I have had these flip flops for a couple weeks now and wanted to wait that long before writing this to test the durability. I was skeptical after seeing some reviews about the strap breaking, but figured it was worth the chance for $30. So far, mine have held up to some decent abuse. I work on a coral atoll island with a lot of rough, uneven terrain around the shoreline. I have taken a couple missteps when my feet were wet which made my foot slide off to the side and the toe strap is the only thing that caught me. I fully expected it to break each time that happened, but so far so good, and I also haven't had any issues with the sole separating from the upper part. I bought these because I'm in and around the water pretty much daily, it also rains a lot here, and I hate when my "material" flip flops get wet, stay wet, and start to stink. I was always having to put them out in the sun to dry out. Not the case with these, I can get them wet all day and they dry in a very short time with no smell to them at all. The sole also has tons of cushion, the harder rubber bottom has good grip on all surfaces I've tried so far, and they look good too. Also, the piece that goes between your toes is in just about the right spot for me. I think my feet have fairly normal dimensions (I don't wear wide sizes in shoes or boots) and the fit is what I expected. With a material piece between the toes it gives some leeway for different sized feet, but a more solid piece like this one is going to make it a little more noticeable if the placement isn't exactly right for your foot. I couldn't be happier with them and I'm actually going to buy a couple more pairs for backup just in case I do manage to break them. For the price, it's worth having multiple pairs of these vs one pair of the expensive material ones.

Basically, they are awesome shoes, but size up from your usual Keds size.

top_reviews.title: Crowin' over my ROCKROOSTER Bedrock boots
top_reviews.text: I took these ROCKROOSTER Bedrock boots for a hike off-trail. I drug 'em through hollers' and hills, briars and sharp rocks in a boulder -filled Kentucky creek. I tried out their waterproof function by standing in the creek with water covering the top of the toe section. No leaks,(except when I stepped in a 12 inch deep water hole with these 6 inch boots! Duhh!). The vibram sole was very "grippy" and kept my feet stable , and my ankles were well supported. The insole in ROCKROOSTER boots,(I have two pair), gives you what I call good step recoil and help make the boots extremely comfortable, and my feet did not overheat. When this 68 year old man returned from this vigorous hike my feet and lower legs were not as fatigued as when I wear my Army boots. I like 'em! Be aware that these are URBAN trail boots when I say that the briars and sharp rocks left the softer midsole kinda' chewed up. These boots are not designed for my hillbilly abuse, but they did not fail in any respect. I wear a 10 , and a 10 1/2 was comfortable. I would describe this particular style as a boot with an athletic shoe top and midsole , with a gravel gripper Vibram trail sole. By the way, the strings are plenty long. Thanks folks.  Rick T., Ky.

top_reviews.text: I am hard on boots, shoes and sandals in the last couple of years I have just torn thru boots (quality boots ) and sandals. typically the last 5 pairs I have purchased on amazon including Teva, and other high end higher price fail with either straps pulling out or more commonly soles delaminating. I now stay away from the athletic looking bi-laminate running shoe sole sandals as I just cant keep enough glue to fix em. These are not my idea of "ideal" but they seem well built, the leather is thin, dont expect much adjustability out of them the design will not offer much change. I soaked mine in a tub of warm water then went on a 2 hour bush stroll to break them in, fit is good even without adjustability and about par for size 10.5 and distributors suggested fit I did not note any color seepage as some reviewers stated. I doubt they will hold up especially where i wear them out in the woods exploring rocky creeks and tracking animals. These might be well suited if your just knocking about on a cruise ship or strolling a boardwalk on your much earned vacation for me they where comfy right out of the box no irritation. They look like something a tourist would wear with or without socks. I dont care about looks (never really did), its all about functionality and durability with me. top_reviews.title: GREAT SHOE
top_reviews.text:
Big fan of Belvedere shoes. Not my first pair from them not will it be my last. Sizing seems to be consistent from one design to the next. A good thing to know for those who’ve purchased a style of theirs before. The trick is the sizing though. I come from a time where shoes once came in sizes AND widths. I guess inventory “costs” and “losses” put a end to that over time but I do miss those days because we all now have to do trial and error sizing if we are not a “D” or “E” width. I am not a “D” but rather a “B” that’s probably gone “C” with time in years and load on foot. Feet widen as the arch settles with age. That said, if you are narrow like me, go down one size. I’m a 13 B/C and 12 is a great fit. If you are “C/D” and in the size range below 12 where there are half sizes, you might want to try a half size down. I had read online somewhere where it was suggested to go down one size in Belvedere so I did on my first purchase. I’ve even ordered 2 pair many times across vendors. Then returned the one that doesn’t fit right. But.....as I said, consistency with Belvedere so once done your good to go for future purchases.

Now about style and appearance. Pictures do not do this shoe justice. I was all over the place with Exotic Gator/Croc shoes because I couldn’t walk into a store and see them all in a row. Mezlan, Belvedere, Caporicci, Zelli. All nice and own their shoes in other styles and skins. I am so glad I went with these and here is why. The texture and overall appearance. Alligator is nice and textured but no where near a Croc Hornback skin. These are stunning and dimensional. There’s something to them. We’ve all seen embossed leather that looks like Alligator on belts and shoes. Even harder to tell these days if it’s from other higher end vendors like Paul Parkman with a price much lower than 800-1k a pair of Gator. Embossing leather to look like these, much harder. There is NO MISTAKING these and not in a gaudy way. Very classy shoe. If you’ve been looking for a real Exotic Gator/Croc shoe and have decided it’s time to pull the trigger, give these a real look. Order them in and look. Trust me....you will not regret it. Very attractive lace up Exotic. Love the toe box on these. The way the hornback skin looks on the toe box! These are the S..t!

Almost forgot another important thing about Belvedere exotics on this review. The soles!! No “break-in” and buttery soft! A real bonus. You could wear all day and night right out of the box and not regret that decision at the end of the evening. No dig-in issues at the ankles either. It’s a soft, comfey shoe right outa the box!

top_reviews.title: Surprisingly nice golf shoes
top_reviews.text:
I am surprised how nice these shoes are. At first, I assumed these were imitation leather, but the closer I looked, the more I thought they were really leather, so I googled Thestron golf shoes. These are listed on their site, and the description says the uppers are waterproof leather. I have a lot of problems with shoes irritating my ankles with stiff materials or seams around the ankle bones. These are really nicely built around the ankles, with a sort of sock like lining, and they are very comfortable in the ankle area. The materials are really well put together and seem like it will be durable. They have pretty hard soles with a great spike pattern. I removed the insole, and the footbed itself is cushioned. The insole is also cushioned, and the overall effect is a well cushioned feel. The insoles are probably fine for most people, but if you like a more structured feel or need more stability, you may want to change out the insoles. The tongue is also well-padded, and the shoelaces don't feel uncomfortable if you tighten them.
These are also a pretty good-looking shoe. I think it walks the line between stylish and traditional pretty well.
The only con for me is that they run slightly larger than most of the shoes I own. I have almost all size 12 shoes. These are size 12, but they are slightly too large. I am looking in to exchanging them for size 11.5. If I can't do that, I will keep these. They aren't so large that I can't make them work.
All in all, these seem to be a pretty high-quality shoe for the price. I would order these shoes again, maybe just a half size smaller.

Being part of the vine program, and wanting a new pair of golf shoes, when these showed up I was skeptical, but thought I would give them a shot. They look and feel cheap out of the box, so first impression was not great, but once I put them on I was surprised they were as comfortable as they were. Also, on the golf course, I really appreciate the grip they seem to have. It definitely feels more like I am wearing golf shoes than just athletic shoes. Also, before my first round, I wore them on a walk around my neighborhood and they were relatively comfortable for that as well, but I do not plan to keep using them for that as I want them to last for golfing as long as possible. I believe the style and quality of the shoe could be better, but I also can't find any real complaints regarding how well they work as golf shoes. I will probably go back to spiked golf shoes once these wear out, but I will say I was pleasantly surprised with these.

top_reviews.title: In love with ASICS all over again because of these
top_reviews.text:
I've been running in ASICS for 18 years. My shoe of choice has always been the GT series, which once fit me perfectly, had the right balance between cushioning and stability, and took wear and tear like the dickens. Sadly, ASICS has gone through a significant redesign of the GT series, and the new design slips in the heel box for me. I hung on to my GT-2130 series 2 and 3 models until they wore out, because the series 4 and 5 both had the same problems. I experimented with Saucony and Brooks for a while, but neither of them did the trick.

Then I read the recent reviews of this new Dynaflyte series and decided to give them a try. The short story is: I'm in love with them. I run about 125 miles a month and these shoes are perfect for my pace and mileage. The new upper is snug and very breathable. The ride is comfortable--- more comfortable than my best experience with the GT-2000 and GT-2100 series over many years. They're also nicely styled (which is a nice to have for me, not a must have, but they do look good in the tomato orange!).

This has renewed my love for ASICS shoes. I'm back on the road without worrying about my ride, and I'm a happy camper.

PS --- the other comments about fit are true--- I went down a half-size from my usual fit, and these are just right.

top_reviews.title: Run 1/2 size large; soft feel but some responsiveness; lightweight
top_reviews.text:
These shoes are quite comfortable, good shock absorption, but for me I need a bit more support. On the plus side, they use the Speva lasting (the layer under the insole) and an Ortholite insole - this is the best combo for Asics shoes in my opinion.

In recent times I have liked many ASICS shoes for fit, feel, etc, just not the bottom feel. Many of their shoes have Ortholite insole on top of Ortholite lasting layer. This combo is very mushy, your foot sinks into the 2 layers of foam and they are not responsive. They make my feet hurt since they are searching for some foundation.

This Dynaflyte 2, and it sounds like the upcoming GT-2000 v6, are using Speva lasting and Ortholite insole. Many Nike shoes like Pegasus, Zoom Structure, Zoom Span, etc. use this combo and it is a great blend of shock absorption, cushion, but some responsiveness without mush.

As per the listing and ASICS site, I ordered 10.5 instead of my usual 11, and they fit perfectly. If I weighed perhaps 30 lbs. less, likely these would have been fine, but I need a bit more stability.

top_reviews.title: Great shoe when sized right.
top_reviews.text:
I had to update my original review where I complained that the toe box was a little snug (see below). In fact, since writing that review, the shoe ended up bending back one of the nails on a toe of my right foot and I had to stop wearing them. I decided that the problems with the snugness may simply be that I bought the shoes too small, so I went to my nearest Running Warehouse (about 30+ miles away) determined to try a larger size. Unfortunately, they didn't have DynaFlytes but I needed a replacement shoe and figured I would once again try different brands and styles with the following criteria: light, comfortable but with good cushioning (because of the paranoia I have about my knees as I mentioned in the original review).

I tried Brooks, Hoka, Saucony and, of course, ASICS. After much back and forth, I again chose ASICS, this time the Roadhawk FF. They felt lighter and less bulky than the Cumulus 19 and ultimately just a little more comfortable than the Saucony (my other finalist). While at the store I actually decided to actually measure my feet and - what do you know - it turns out my left is an 11 but my right is 11.5, and it was my right where I had had the trouble with the DynaFlytes. So... I had been running fine with the Roadhawks (11.5, by the way) but my aborted use of the DynaFlytes - and the below review - kept nagging at me. Especially since the Roadhawk has the Flytefoam sole but not the gel while the DynaFlyte has both. Anyway, I decided to try another pair of DynaFlyte 2 at an even better price at Shoebacca (thru Amazon) and this time chose 11 instead of 10.5. Lo and behold, they are perfect! Light, comfortable, great cushioning and still a good-looking shoe! So, sorry to the ASICS folks for my previous review - my bad, I just bought the shoes a 1/2 too small - and thank you for continuing to make such great running shoes!

Original review:
I've been wearing ASICS pretty much since I got serious about running. They're comfortable and light and the gel in the sole makes me feel hopeful that the daily pounding on asphalt may not be slowly wrecking my knees (so far, so good). I moved from the Contend 3 to Cumulus 18 (both bought in stores and compared with other styles and brands) and then Cumulus 19 before deciding to try the DynaFlyte 2 (both bought online). I'd read the reviews in Runner's World and online on the DynaFlyte and was excited to try something new with the cushioning I had grown to trust but in a lighter shoe. I normally wear an 11 but went down to a 10.5 based on the reviews I had read. They are light and they're a nice looking shoe but they feel a little tight through the toe area when compared to the Cumulus. Maybe I should have stuck with an 11? Anyway, I'm training for a half-marathon and I've been able to run in them fine - no blisters or lost nails - but I can't get past the fact that they feel just a little too snug up front. I think once I wear these out, I think I'll go back to the Cumulus.

top_reviews.title: Size runs  MUCH too small
top_reviews.text: I read the other reviews saying that the sizes run small, but went ahead and ordered the X-Large, reasoning that it was supposed to fit sizes 9 1/2 to 10 1/2, and a slipper that was a bit too small for a 10 1/2 should fit my size 10 feet OK.  Well, they arrived, and even after struggling for several minutes, I was unable to even get them on.  So I ordered another pair in size XX-Large, which purports to fit sizes 11 - 12.  I was able to get this pair on (though I had to work at it) but my toes are jammed painfully against the end of the slipper.  Since the struggle to put on the slipper resulted in the tag being torn off, and the accompanying information was explicit that returns have to be in new condition with all tags and packaging, I guess I'm stuck with the newer ones.  I just hope they'll stretch over time.  Otherwise I've got an expensive (but admittedly attractive) pair of chew toys for the dog.  They do seem to be well-made, and I believe they would be comfortable if they fit.  Just be sure to order a couple sizes bigger than your real size.

top_reviews.title: Perfect, cozy winter shoes

I ordered the crackleberry, so the color helps these look like cute, cozy shoes instead of "wearing my pjs in public." I definitely recommend them, though they are just a wee bit small, so consider ordering a size up if you are debating between sizes.

I feel like I am wearing supportive shoes.  I work from home so I wear these more than any other shoe.  I think these will be a great purchase for a long time.

top_reviews.text:

Highly recommend these slippers!

top_reviews.text: My use for these shoes is for outside work in an urban environment not on the trails, and my review will only reflect that.  I work outside all day long in the elements and needed a waterproof lightweight shoe for the winter that can take a beating on our streets and sidewalks. All I can say is wow, these Peakfreak's exceeded my expectations in every way!  These boots are very lightweight for what they are and provide the cushioning I need for being on my feet 9 to 10 hours a day.  I thought they might be a little hard for walking the streets, but the cushioning that Columbia uses on these boots is really nice.  We recently had a really wet and cold storm system pass our way and I can say these boots kept my feet dry and warm through the several days of the squall.  No water penetrated the shoe at all and there's something to be said about their OmniHeat lining as in fact it did keep my feet warm in the upper 30's low 40's weather we were having.  Overall I am quite impressed with this boot I've only wore them for about a month so we shall see how the sole holds up on the pavement, but I'm optimistic as they have impressed me on all other facets.  Good job columbia!

top_reviews.title: Needs a half size but otherwise excellent
top_reviews.text: So I have milked my old Nike tennis shoes (pictured) for 10+ years of use but, as you can see, they are pretty much done. I saw these BAASPLOA trail runner/hiking shoes and thought that these would be a good apples-to-apples replacement for my Nikes. I was a bit disappointed that they were not offered in half sizes (except 8.5, but of course, I'm a 10.5) so I ordered up to size 11. They arrived today and I was pleased by the overall outward appearance. I'm not a name brand snob but I do want my shoes to look decent even if they are off-brand. A check mark on that box. I then examined the collar and interior of the shoe. The collar area has a nice soft pad and there are sewn in pads at the heel and two that make up the arch support (see pic). When I slipped them on everything under my foot felt great! Soft and supported. It came as no surprise that there was a small amount of excess room at the toe but it really didn't bother me. I laced the shoes up and wore them for the next 2.5 hours straight while doing a variety of landscaping chores around my house. Never once did I experience any discomfort or ill fit. Further, even though I was mildly exerting myself, the shoes breathed well and I didn't end up with sweaty feet. The tread (pictured) is fairly aggressive which fits with the way I plan to wear these shoes. I think they look pretty nice with denim jeans (pictured) and I'm sure that they will look equally good with my Carhartt work pants. Obviously, at this point I cannot comment as to durability so I won't knock them on that account. The price point is about what I would expect for shoes of this build and quality. Not any kind of a crazy bargain but way better than similar shoes from the big brand names. Gotta' give it five stars at this point.

top_reviews.title: Good, but not great.  Quality control needs to be better
top_reviews.text:
I largely spend all my time in ballet flats so I wasn’t sure how I’d adapt to a pair of hiking shoes. Would they be too heavy, or stiff, confining, or hard to drive in? I needn’t have worried. The Shulook hiking shoes made their maiden trip today in the middle of a cold rainstorm when I pulled them on to run a series of errands. I had some concern that they’d be slippery on the brake and gas pedal when wet – they were not even close to slippery, and I was doing my best to slide them around to test them. The nice waffle design plus the spiky circular inset rubber on the sole (pictured below) helped for a surefooted trip, and the waterproof design helped me come home with dry feet after several hours of navigating the puddles. I intend to use them for trail walking and I expect that they will perform well for this. The hiking shoes were slightly heavier than I thought they’d be but I truly didn’t notice the weight after a while, and they were completely flexible and comfortable for walking and driving.

I appreciated that the shoestrings were adequate enough in length to tie in a decent double bow, and there wasn’t an excess of string hanging down to get in the way of a hike. A spare pair of shoestrings was thoughtfully included in the box. I mention this because I once ordered a pair of sneakers that had barely enough shoelace to tie.

I’d have liked to have given these a five star review but a couple of things prevented that. The shoe insert was improperly formed, and the left and right inserts were not symmetrical. I didn’t detect the off-center raised pattern when I was wearing them, but I feel the toe guides and arch supports should match each other in a good quality product (photo below for clarification). The same lack of symmetry extends to the top of the left and right shoe. The mesh areas are not of equal shape or size and as a result, I could slightly detect a seam on the left shoe that wasn’t felt on the right shoe. In fairness, that could have been due to a difference in my left/right foot size and structure, but looking down at the shoe, you can see that they are not symmetrical and the left shoe rubber cants inwards a bit at the big toe. I’m not unhappy with the shoes I ordered only for my personal use, but I wouldn’t have been happy if say, I ordered these as a gift for someone.

I’ve had foot surgery in the past and I found these to be adequately supportive for a trail walk.
These are best suited for trail walking in my opinion, as opposed to serious climbing and hiking, but only because they don’t have the higher ankle support. They’re a pretty good hiking shoe option, but I could wish for a little more attention to better quality control details to make it a great purchase.

I’ll come back and update in the future to let you know how they’re holding up to wear and tear outdoors on the trails.

top_reviews.title: Love Oboz and Love These Boots!
top_reviews.text: I had never heard of Oboz before until I ordered a pair of boots in a different style a few years ago.  I fell in love with this brand and when I saw this style, which looked like it had a bit more ankle support, I just had to order them.  Straight out of the box, I couldn't believe how light they were.  Even with thick socks, they were easy to pull on.  I usually wear a size 7 in a shoe, but I ordered a 8.5 in these boots because they seem to run just a little bit small and my toe kept hitting the front of the boot. I knew I needed a larger size in addition to the toe thing because my feet swell when out hiking. The 8.5 fits wonderfully and allows me room to wear thick hiking socks with a little bit of wiggle room, but snug enough to not have a loose heel.  I've worn these boots out in the field on a number of different occasions and have not had a single blister or hot spot.  Plus, they have good ankle support for me and the tread is sturdy and has kept me me from slipping in wet or slick situations.  I also really like the bright red color I ordered.  I did, however, have to replace the rounded laces with flat laces in order to keep the laces from coming untied.  I have this issue with pretty much all of my hiking boots and really wish hiking boots would  come with flat laces in general.  Once I replaced the round laces with flat ones, I had no more problems.  As for arch support - I have flat feet so I can't really tell you much about that, except that my feet are  comfortable and the boots are not heavy and clunky like others I have in my closet.  I know how quickly styles come and go, and I like this particular style so much, I ordered another pair just to have after this pair wears out.

top_reviews.title: First pair of Oboz
top_reviews.text: I tried these boots on at the local outfitters.  Loved them but couldn't bring myself to spend the asking price of $160.  The lady at the outfitter said her and her daughter wear them often and have done many hikes.  They like these boots//shoes so much that they carry a great selection.  She did recommend getting a half size larger to allow the extra room in toe area for up and down trails, otherwise you would end up with sore toes.... which is exactly what was happing with my current pair of hikers. She also mentioned to tie them a little loose around the ankle until they are broken in.  I ordered these about a month ago. Second day I had them I went to appalachian trail for two mile waterfall hike. I purposely stepped in water at the falls and NO wet feet!  I walk 2-13 miles a day and have had no sores or rubbing.  They wear well and I have found now that they are my go to boot!  Getting a pair for my husband!

top_reviews.title: Excellent for urban hiking
top_reviews.text:
This is my 4th pair of Adidas trail runners, as I've been wearing them for years for urban hiking. I find them to be exceptionally comfortable and light, and they have very good traction.
For hiking in the wilderness I would wear proper hiking boots, but on urban trails (like L.A.'s Runyon Canyon, Griffith Park, etc.) these are perfect. They look nice too. And I like that these have regular "old-fashioned" laces, rather than the weird and cumbersome lace-up system that many sneakers these days come with.

They do fit true to size, but through trial and error I've learned that I prefer my hiking shoes half size larger than my normal size, to allow plenty of room for socks and to eliminate any chance for pinching or chaffing. I have never gotten a blister with these trail runners half size up.

I needed some trail running shoes and have purchased the Saucony Excursion 14; they are still a bit wide, but at lease I can tighten them in the midfoot and the wider toe box is fine. I really wanted to like these shoes; this is the look I wanted, but not the fit.

top_reviews.title: Best snow boots my son has ever owned!
top_reviews.text: I have gotten tired of purchasing new boots every year or so that are not the greatest quality, or are sacrificing in comfort and functionality, for my growing 7-almost-8 year old. If we can even find boots locally (seriously, BIG "if", and yet we live in Wisconsin...still can't figure that one out), they are crappy boots that barely last one whole season and don't always fit him the best, while not exactly being the most inexpensive, either. I have already upgraded to Lands' End for the rest of his winter gear, but boots is just always a tough one. They have to fit right, look right, work right, etc. I will admit these seemed a bit pricey, but in my internet research I found, these were the only decent boots I saw. I am so glad we got them because they are AWESOME! They seem very well made and will be both durable when playing plus water-proof for the elements. Biggest deal for me personally is how well they fit. Fit is huge for us, my son is very picky. Just with shoes. Everything pinches or squeezes, doesn't feel right, look right, again..the same criteria listed before. But, these fit the bill and met all expectations. He is a size 1 in shoes and I purchased a 1 in these as well, and the fit is perfect. They even look good on him, which is hard to come by in a snow boot. From reviews, it seems these can even be used as rain boots by removing the inserts? (Another great bonus - removable inserts!) Essentially what I'm saying is, these boots are wonderful and were a great, very worthwhile purchase.

top_reviews.text: I bought a pair of these for each of my kids. We live in MN, so have long, cold winters and the kids are very active outdoors so these boots saw a lot of action. They held up beautifully - no wearing down of the soles, or cracks in any of the rubber outer (a common problem we have with other brands... so by the end of the season they are leaky and trashed). Finally, my kids feet stayed toasty warm in these, even when staying out for quite a long time (sometimes hours) . I would recommend these boots completely; tried and tested in real conditions.

top_reviews.title: best childs boots ever
top_reviews.text: Kamik snow boots are the best. I have purchased this model for my wife who has small feet and my grandchildren. I wear a similar model. We live in the Western Catskill mountains on the side of a mountain. These boots with wool-blend socks keep our feet warm and dry in all kinds of weather.  They stay flexible in sub-zero temperatures are light and have good traction. Last winter our grandchildren all came over and it was 6 F degrees outside. I was plowing our 500-foot driveway and they decided to sleigh down the entire length. They were outside a  total of 6 hours only breaking for lunch.  Down they would go, then pile into the tractor's tub sled trailer and I would pull them back up. Of course, they also had appropriate undergarments, snow pants, coats, hats, and mittens.  The linings slip out easily and dry quickly.  When I did an inventory last week of who needs or outgrew their boots I immediately ordered a new pair for my oldest granddaughter and the old ones will get passed down.

top_reviews.title: Constant Condensation inside !
top_reviews.text:
We've had these about 3-4 weeks now.

There is not much cushion from the cold on the bottom, so I've purchased extra insoles .

After first use ( no snow or rain, just cold) I removed the liner to put in the new cushined insole. As I slipped the insole in I felt water droplets on the top of the foot area. Since then I have been checking after every use and they are indeed constantly wet! I am not sure if this is due to sweaty feet, but I don't see how sweaty feet could form droplets outside of the liner.

After reading another review I am going to check for a hole in the sole. The bottoms are not thick, they are very bendy which is why I was concerned there was not much between his foot and the cold ground.

I am contemplating returning these if his feet are wet again today.

top_reviews.title: A Terrific Shoe

top_reviews.title: Best sandals
top_reviews.text: Living in AZ, I wear sandals very often but have never found a pair that were completely satisfactory.  Usually it takes months to wear in, often with pieces of moleskin or bandage to cover the "rough" spots. The Mephisto were comfortable, walkable, and had no rough spots.  I have other Mephisto shoes so thought I would try their sandals, great choice!

top_reviews.title: We were very disappointed in these sandals
top_reviews.text: We were very disappointed in these sandals.  My husband has worn these sandals in the past and they lasted "forever".  However, I purchased these for my husband for Christmas, 2014 and they have already torn.  (See attached picture.)  We are unable to return them because of the Amazon policy, but actually I don't think this is Amazon's issue.  What happened to Mephistos quality?

top_reviews.title: You get what you pay for!
top_reviews.text: There are lower priced premium sandals out there (for example, Ecco and Teva, both of which I own or have owned), but for my troublesome, very narrow, flat feet, the Mephisto Shark Fit sandals are hands down the best I've owned. They provide all-day comfort, and unlike a few experiences I've had with Teva's, I don't get any blisters, even without socks on. The Mephisto's are exceptionally well made, and though they are costlier than even my favorite Ecco's, they're a much classier-looking sandal. A piece of advice: if you have very narrow feet like mine, buy one size smaller than your regular shoe size. The sandals will fit better and you won't be forced to pull the straps in as far as they'll go to get a snug and comfortable fit.

top_reviews.title: Mephisto Shark Sandals Are Very Comfortable
top_reviews.text: Incredibly comfortable Euro manufactured sandals by Mephisto of France.  They add comfort to the overall leather and leather-like materials by using a suede footbed rather than plain leather or synthetic. This helps avoid sweating.  There is a patented shock absorbing insert on the bottom sole in the heel area, which adds to the comfort for all day walking.  Warning:  if you are a heavyweight, or for anyone over a couple years of use, the shock absorber will fall out of the shoes.  Then you can sign up for the Mephisto refurbishment program!  They will rebuild your precious expensive sandals for a little over a hundred bucks, in about 4-6 weeks, and get them back to you while you suffer on some lame cheap other sandals.  The size conversion from EU size numbers over to the US sizes is a bit inexact.  If you fall into the range of 8.5-9.0-9.5-10.0 US, you'll need to decide if your EU sizes are in the 42-43-44 range.In THIS model, the 9.5 US is closer to 43 than 44.  It is unclear how exactly the box they send you will be marked, size-wise.

top_reviews.title: Worth every dollar!
top_reviews.text: I do not write many reviews, but I had to for these Sandals. This is my first pair of Mephisto shoes of any kind. I have for, knee and back issues. They are all better by quote a bit when I can wear these. I am beiginnig to wear to work and really do not care if anyone does not like them.....they are very expensive, the most I have ever paid for a sandal......but if they pst as long as other reviewers have said, they are worth every dollar! Love the feel of the insole, not too cushy.....but exactly the right amount of support. The straps are what seems the most different than most sandals, they are extremely comfortable and easy to put on and remove. I am sold on this brand and shoe.......and I have over 30 pairs of other shoes I could wear...

top_reviews.text:
Was very excited about receiving my new pair of Mephisto Shark sandals. I’ve had a pair for 15 years and had them refurbished at Mephisto twice. It was time to retire the old favorites.
Unfortunately when the new pair arrived I was disappointed to find the front Velcro straps to be different than my original pair. The front (over toes) strap is too short to close!! I’m hoping this is an unusual defect, and will contact Mephisto to see if they changed the length of the front strap. As compared to my original pair it is inches shorter!

top_reviews.title: Very disappointing - soles worn out ... holes ....
top_reviews.text: Very disappointing.  I bought these sandals for my husband.  Where comfortable, they are not lasting shoes.  After only 3 months of on and off wear (June through August),  the sole has worn out (actual holes) .  And that means a couple a hours a couple of times per week.  I cannot believe we spent $300 and they will be unwearable after one season.  Being the way they are built, you cannot just go to a shoemaker and fix it, you just throw them out.  Very upset actually.  When we both them we read in the product description that they are life time warranted .. I will try to see how that works out, although I do not expect much.  Certainly no Mephisto for us again.

top_reviews.title: Best Shoes I Have Worn
top_reviews.text:
I just purchased my fourth pair of Sharks, and I cannot live without them. To be honest, when someone recommended them to me some 10 or so years ago, I was taken aback a bit at the price. Previous to that time, the most I had ever paid for a pair of shoes was perhaps around $100. So I was hesitant on trying them on, but once I stood up with them on my feet and took a step, I was hooked.

These are simply the most comfortable footwear I have had on my feet. I wear them pretty much every day, even during the winter (when I sometimes break down and put on a pair of socks as well.) I took a pair to Iraq where they were my footwear of choice as soon as I could take off my combat boots. They are extremely durable, as I have had mine on walking across coral reefs, in the desert, on icy streets, and on New York sidewalks.

I am so happy with my Sharks that I just bought my second type of Mephistos, the Match, for business meetings, but while those are great, too, nothing beats my Sharks.

Life is too short to have hurting feet. Get some Sharks and your feet will thank you.

top_reviews.title: All my other shoes are jealous...
top_reviews.text:
I grew up wearing moccasins. They are my favorite kind of shoe, and if I could, I'd wear them all the time. Sometimes, though, they are not so practical. I work in retail, and am on my feet on a concrete floor 40-45 hours a week, so I need really comfortable, supportive shoes. I work in a hardware store, so I need durable shoes that offer decent protection with good traction and still allow for a suitable level of dexterity for someone who would rather be barefoot.
I found Peace Mocs a few years ago, and always have a pair of Denise in Black and in Brown in my wardrobe. I am on my 8th pair of this style. I have simple taste, and usually go for function and comfort more than style, but these are good looking shoes, as well as comfortable, and totally functional for anything you might need to do, unless you're on one of those Real Housewives shows, or something, but I'm talking about normal people who have to do actual work. Add some Dr. Scholl's work soles, and you can stay on your feet all day.
I very honestly wear these shoes everywhere that I don't wear a skirt. If I am walking somewhere I can't wear my bed slippers, I have my Peace Mocs on. If I can't wear my Peace Mocs, I probably don't want to go.

Some advice on these shoes from someone who has worn 7 pair to pieces: If you order these in your normal shoe size and they are "a bit too tight" that's kinda how they are supposed to be at first, especially if you wear them with socks like I do. If you exchange them for the next size up, by the time they're comfy, they're too big to be comfortable, and you'll hate them. For maximum comfort and long wear, break them in. Breaking them in is a little bit of a process, but if you do it, you will love these shoes so much your pets will get jealous and you'll have to lock them in a closet so they don't pee in them.
The shoes, of course.
You should never lock your pets in the closet.
Breaking in moccasins forms them to your feet, and that's one of the things that makes them so comfy. My break in process is simple, and requires little conscious effort. What I do is walk around my yard in the dewy grass, then I go to work and walk around in them for 8 hours. After a few days of that, they're perfect.

Here is a more generic process: 1. Get a spray bottle and fill it with water. 2. Spray the outside of the shoes just enough to dampen the surface. 3. Bend and stretch the shoes in every direction you can think of, stretching and softening the leather. I do this by wearing them. 4. Wear your shoes until they dry. If you can't walk around continuously, walk around often most frequently when they're almost dry, to keep the leather from stiffening up.
It's kinda like cooking pasta.

Point is, these are great shoes. I will wear them until they stop making them, or I lose my feet. I hope neither one ever happens.

I want to start this review on the first day of wearing them. I got the black and red Peak running shoes.

I have to start out with the fact that I'm a large man, 6' 2" @325lb, who stays on my feet for at least 11 hours a day 6 days a week.

The first thing I noticed and liked was the sides of these shoes are very stiff, sorta like an ankle brace. These shoes are the more of a pull on shoe with a string to give it a little more support. I like the way these feel for the fact that they seem to hug your entire foot, not just the sides or the heal area.

When I took my first step I was kinda surprised at the comfort in the heel area. It was almost like a very springy insole that really and truly has a lot of bounce to it. I had to take a few steps to get used to the bounce and spring feeling.

I have had them on for 6 hours today, with 5 of that on my feet, and I cannot believe how comfy these shoes are. They feel so light and airy and should do the trick for me.

I will update them down the road as they wear, but right now they are a very solid 5 star rating.
